confirmed.title: Phase-2 batch correlation evidence never reaches the graph, claims, or rules
confirmed.evidence: finalize() calls evidence_correlator.correlate_batch(&all_intents, &all_actions, &snapshot) (runtime.rs:1702-1704) and then only persists the result (1707-1722) and passes it to classify_authoritative (1768). The graph is never updated with it: graph_builder.handle() is called only from the phase-1 path (runtime.rs:891), while the replay executor does exactly the missing step (replay/executor.rs:165-185: correlate_batch then graph_builder.handle per evidence). graph_builder.finalize() only builds GraphRefinement records and returns a FrozenGraph that the runtime discards (runtime.rs:1741-1743 `let _frozen = ...`).
confirmed.impact: Evidence links that the streaming correlator missed (out-of-window, evicted from the intent/action buffers, or arriving before the intent was known) exist only in `evidence` rows. They never create IntentCausesAction or PolicyBoundaryCrossing edges, so the authoritative rule engine, pattern matcher, ClaimBuilder and TracebackBuilder (runtime.rs:1754-1826) all run on a graph that lacks them. A run whose only correlation is discovered in phase 2 gets zero authoritative claims and can be reported Safe even though correlate_batch found a high-confidence intent->action link.
confirmed.fix: Feed `batch_evidence.evidence` through `graph_builder.handle()` (and persist the resulting delta nodes/edges) before the phase-2 rule/pattern/claim pass, exactly as replay/executor.rs does; then classify and build claims from the updated graph.

verification.reason: The claim holds at every cited point. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/runtime/runtime.rs, finalize() takes the buffered intents/actions (1700-1701), calls evidence_correlator.correlate_batch (1702-1704), then only persists Evidence/EvidenceRefinement records (1707-1722), snapshots the graph that was built without them (1725-1739), and passes the evidence to graph_builder.finalize (1741-1743) and classify_authoritative (1764-1775). grep confirms graph_builder.handle is invoked exactly once in the whole runtime, at line 891 inside the phase-1 path (the only other handle-like calls are handle_intent_content at 837 and handle_intent_pbc at 855, both intent-only and also phase-1). graph_builder::finalize (collector/src/responsibility/graph/graph_builder.rs:1087-1172) merely translates identity/evidence refinements into GraphRefinement records and returns FrozenGraph::new(...); it adds no nodes/edges, and the returned `_frozen` is only read for its refinements (1746-1751). The phase-2 consumers all read the un-updated graph: pattern matching at 1754-1761, rule evaluation both via classify_authoritative (classification/engine.rs:393-414, whose Layer 1 is self.rules.evaluate(graph)) and directly at 1786, PBC edge counting at 1799-1806, ClaimBuilder at 1821-1826 and TracebackBuilder at 1893-1899. The rule engine matches on graph edges (classification/rule_engine.rs:139,153), and graph_builder.handle is precisely what creates IntentCausesAction/PBC edges from evidence (graph_builder.rs:433-458). The comparison to replay/executor.rs:159-187 is accurate — the replay path correlates and then feeds every evidence record through graph_builder.handle before classification, which the live finalize path omits. The premise that batch can find links phase 1 missed is also real: the streaming correlator evicts by TTL/size (evidence/buffer.rs:62-83, correlator.rs:160-161) while correlate_batch is explicitly window-free (correlator.rs:288,319). The one partial mitigation is that batch evidence records are passed into compute_score/sub_score_evidence (classification/scoring.rs:46-105,276-297), so they can nudge the score, but they cannot create the PBC edges that rule evaluation, patterns, claims, and tracebacks require — consistent with the claim's impact, including the PBC<10-and-no-unsafe-rule gate capping the score at 0.10 (scoring.rs:93-105), so a batch-only correlation can yield zero claims and a Safe verdict.

confirmed.title: Phase-2 scoring always receives None for content threat and baseline deviation
confirmed.evidence: `last_content_threat` and `last_baseline_deviation` are declared (runtime.rs:152-154), initialised to None (309-310) and read in finalize (1772-1773), but no code ever assigns them - the whole file contains no `last_content_threat =` / `last_baseline_deviation =` write. Phase 1 does compute both locals (`content_threat` at 993-994, `baseline_deviation` at 1049) and passes them to classify_provisional at 1267-1270.
confirmed.impact: compute_score_parts treats None as "no signal": D2 falls back to graph patterns and D6 to sub_score_behavioral (scoring.rs:53-58, 63-66). So the DeBERTa prompt-injection score and the behavioural-baseline deviation that drove the phase-1 route are silently dropped from the authoritative score, and phase 1 vs phase 2 disagree by construction (phase 1 Unsafe -> phase 2 Safe) purely because of the missing assignment.
confirmed.fix: Set `self.last_content_threat = content_threat` and `self.last_baseline_deviation = baseline_deviation` at the end of each trigger_inner cycle (max-combining with the previous value), or keep per-agent copies and feed the phase-2 agent's values instead of run-wide lasts.

verification.reason: I verified the cited code directly in /tmp/mtal-audit. In collector/src/responsibility/runtime/runtime.rs the two fields are declared at 152 and 154, initialized to None at 309-310, and read only at 1772-1773 inside finalize() (declared at 1632, called from finalize_session at 2059). A repo-wide grep for `last_content_threat`/`last_baseline_deviation` across all .rs files returns exactly those five lines — no assignment exists anywhere, so the claim's central assertion holds. The phase-1 locals are declared at 946-947, updated at 993-994 (DeBERTa max-combine) and 1049 (baseline deviation), and passed to classify_provisional at 1268-1269; nothing copies them into the struct. The downstream impact also checks out: scoring.rs 44-46 documents `None` as "not available", 53-56 substitutes sub_score_pattern when content_threat is None, and 63-66 substitutes sub_score_behavioral when baseline_deviation is None, so both real signals are discarded in phase 2. classify_authoritative (engine.rs 393-420) uses that score against threshold_unsafe to emit DirectUnsafe/DirectSafe, and the resulting classification_result (including score/decision) is fed into AlertBuilder::compose_with_context at runtime.rs 1858-1876, so the defect reaches the authoritative alert. One minor overstatement in the impact wording: final_verdict itself is aggregated from hard rules, PBC/pattern observations and phase1_observations (runtime.rs 1784-1817), so the phase-2 score is not the sole determinant of the final verdict label; however the authoritative classification result and its persisted score/severity are still corrupted by the missing assignment, so the defect is real and material.

confirmed.title: All per-agent progressive scoring is attached to one arbitrary agent chosen from a HashMap
confirmed.evidence: trigger_inner picks the scoring subject with `graph.all_nodes().filter_map(|n| n.agent_id.clone()).next()` (runtime.rs:948) and then feeds D1-D6, CUSUM, evidence_conflict, the baseline tracker and the ScoringSignal only for that agent (951-1122). ResponsibilityGraph stores nodes in `HashMap<NodeId, ResponsibilityNode>` (graph.rs:33) and `all_nodes()` iterates `self.nodes.values()` (graph.rs:654-656), so the iteration (and therefore the selected agent) depends on the randomised hasher and on the current bucket layout.
confirmed.impact: In any multi-agent run the six-dimension scores, CUSUM alarms, baseline deviation and evidence_conflict flag are attributed to whichever agent node happens to come first, and the selected agent can change from trigger to trigger as the map rehashes. `per_agent_scores` in the emitted EvaluationSummary (runtime.rs:1966-1998) therefore contains at most one agent with a mixture of dimensions measured across different agents, making per-agent claims, ablation A-pattern/A-delegation results and CUSUM statistics non-reproducible.
confirmed.fix: Iterate over the agents in the graph (from `identity_resolver` or `graph.agents()` with a sorted, deterministic order) and run the EWMA/CUSUM/baseline update per agent, using that agent's own PBC edges and evidence.

verification.reason: The claim's code evidence checks out exactly. runtime.rs:948 reads `if let Some(agent_id) = graph.all_nodes().filter_map(|n| n.agent_id.clone()).next()`, and the entire per-agent scoring block (dimension updates at 951-1000, fused readback 1006, CUSUM alarms 1013, evidence_conflict 1024, D6 baseline update 1043-1050, ScoringSignal emission 1079-1122) runs only inside that `if let`, using that single agent_id. I grepped every production caller of `update_dimension`/`get_agent_fused_score`/`cusum_alarms`/`evidence_conflict`: outside this block they appear only in progressive.rs unit tests (lines 355-407), so no other path populates per-agent state; `per_agent_scores` at runtime.rs:1966-1998 is therefore built from a `progressive_scorer.agents` map that only ever gets entries for the selected agent (and possibly a different agent per trigger, since the selected one can vary). The storage claim is also correct: graph/graph.rs:33 declares `nodes: HashMap<NodeId, ResponsibilityNode>` using `std::collections::HashMap` (graph.rs:21), i.e. the randomized RandomState hasher, and `all_nodes()` at graph.rs:654-656 iterates `self.nodes.values()` with no sorting. Multi-agent graphs are a supported and tested scenario (graph_builder.rs builds one Agent node per agent_id, e.g. 1219-1235, and delegation edges from_agent_id/to_agent_id at 2389-2390, 2499-2500), so the first-with-agent_id node is genuinely arbitrary. Minor corrections that do not refute the finding: the file is actually graph/graph.rs, and the `filter_map` does not exclude `UNATTRIBUTED_AGENT_ID` (unlike the agent_count filter at 929-937), so the arbitrary pick can even land on the unattributed pseudo-agent; also the dimension inputs are graph-global aggregates (pbc_count, pattern confidence, agent_count, repetition), so "mixture of dimensions measured across different agents" is partly an understatement rather than an overstatement. No evidence anywhere in the snapshot handles this deterministically, so the defect stands as high severity.

confirmed.title: Shutdown breaks the event loop without draining the input stream, so the tail of the run is never routed
confirmed.evidence: process()'s select! loop has three ready branches; the shutdown branch (runtime.rs:2237-2242) calls finalize_session() and `break` immediately, abandoning `input` with whatever events the runners have already produced. Nothing drains `input` before phase 2, and `tokio::select!` chooses randomly among ready branches, so the number of events processed before shutdown depends on which branch is polled first (the branch is checked every 500 ms, competing with a possibly always-ready event branch).
confirmed.impact: On Ctrl+C/SIGTERM the last buffered events (all intents/actions produced since the previous trigger, plus everything queued during the final debounce interval) are dropped before phase 2, so the run's authoritative verdict and persisted graph depend on shutdown timing. The same code path also decides whether the final trigger() even sees those events, making final-verdict reproducibility impossible for benchmark runs.
confirmed.fix: On shutdown, drain `input` until it returns None or is empty for a bounded grace period (e.g. poll with `now_or_never` until quiet), routing each event, before calling finalize_session(); use `biased;` with the event branch first so pending data is consumed before the shutdown branch is considered.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what is claimed. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/runtime/runtime.rs, process() (line 2194) creates a select! loop (2205) whose three branches are input.next() (2206), tick.tick() (2231), and shutdown_poll.tick() (2237). The shutdown branch checks RUNTIME_SHUTDOWN (2238), then calls finalize_session(&run_id) and `break` (2239-2240), and after the loop the function returns `Box::pin(futures::stream::empty())` (2247) with no drain of `input`. That drain cannot happen inside finalize_session either: it takes only `&mut self` and `run_id` (signature at 2055) and has no access to the stream; it triggers on currently-buffered state (2056-2058) and flushes persistence (2076-2100). There is no Drop impl for ResponsibilityRuntime and no other consumer of `input`: AgentRunner::run awaits analyzer.process() sequentially (/tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/framework/runners/agent.rs:66-70), and the input is select_all of runner streams that are pull-based async generators over child stdout pipes (/tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/framework/runners/common.rs:263-322), so anything the runners have written but the runtime has not pulled is lost when `break` drops the stream — the pipeline cannot route it elsewhere. RUNTIME_SHUTDOWN is set by the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler in /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/main.rs:51-78, i.e. this is the live shutdown path, not dead code. The nondeterminism also holds: the select! has no `biased;`, so when both input.next() and the 500 ms shutdown tick are ready (2202, 2237) tokio picks randomly, making the number of tail events routed before the break timing-dependent. The only minor imprecision in the claim is that the unprocessed tail sits in the OS pipe / unread stream state rather than in an application-level buffer, but the loss is the same. No test covers shutdown draining (no shutdown/RUNTIME_SHUTDOWN references in the runtime tests or tests/). The claim and its proposed fix are sound; severity high is appropriate for a shutdown-path loss of the tail events that feed the authoritative phase-2 verdict, though the practical magnitude is bounded by roughly the final debounce window plus data buffered during the last trigger's observer calls.

confirmed.title: Observer LLM call and backpressured writes block the only event-draining loop for up to 15 s
confirmed.evidence: `self.trigger().await` is called inline from the select! loop (runtime.rs:2223 and 2233-2235), and trigger_inner awaits classification_engine.classify_provisional (1255-1272), which awaits the Observer HTTP provider with a 15 s default timeout (observer/provider.rs:103, 174-175). trigger_inner also awaits `write_blocking` for every claim, alert, graph node and edge (1504-1558), and write_blocking awaits channel capacity (persistence/writer.rs:316-324). While any of these futures is pending, the loop reads no events.
confirmed.impact: Each Observer call or full writer channel stalls event ingestion for seconds; the SSL/process runners are starved, their child binaries block on stdout, and the eBPF ring buffers overflow, so actions from exactly the interval around an ambiguous decision are lost. That couples the run's detected behaviour to LLM latency and to SQLite write throughput.
confirmed.fix: Decouple the trigger from ingestion: push routed events into a bounded internal queue and run trigger()/Observer/writes on a separate task (or at minimum make Observer calls spawn + timeout without holding the loop), so the select! loop keeps draining `input`.

verification.reason: Verified in the snapshot: runtime.rs:2194 `process` runs the `select!` at 2205 whose only event branch is `input.next()` at 2206, and `self.trigger().await` executes inline in the branch bodies at 2223 and 2234, so the input stream is not polled while the trigger runs. `trigger()` (726-729) awaits `trigger_inner` with no `tokio::spawn` anywhere in the path; `trigger_inner` awaits `classify_provisional` (1264-1272), which in classification/engine.rs (95, 232, 242) awaits `obs.evaluate`, reaching observer/provider.rs:174-179 `tokio::time::timeout` with `timeout_ms: 15000` at provider.rs:103. `trigger_inner` additionally awaits `write_blocking` for claims/alerts/graph nodes/edges at runtime.rs:1504-1558, and writer.rs:247 uses a bounded 4096-slot `mpsc` channel whose `write_blocking` (316-324) awaits capacity. Refutation attempts fail: AgentRunner::run (framework/runners/agent.rs:50-74) merges streams with `select_all` and chains analyzers lazily without spawning, and the child stdout reader (framework/runners/common.rs:269+) only reads when polled, so this select loop is the sole drain of the ingestion pipeline and the stall propagates as backpressure to the child processes. The writer's own comment at writer.rs:312-314 acknowledges that stalling the event loop drops kernel events, yet the trigger path uses the blocking write. The cited line range 2233-2235 is off by one (actual 2234) and the 15 s bound is conservative (up to 50 observer calls per run, plus unbounded writer waits), so the defect as described holds.

confirmed.title: Observer cache key is built from unsorted HashMap-derived type lists, so the L1/L2 cache almost never hits
confirmed.evidence: The cache key hashes `edge_types`/`node_types` collected from `graph.all_edges()` / `graph.all_nodes()` (runtime.rs:1133-1140, 1150-1166) - HashMap iterators (graph.rs:654-661) - and CacheKey::compute hashes the slices in their given order without sorting (observer/types.rs:273-287). `subject` is the same arbitrary first-agent lookup as above (1141-1149).
confirmed.impact: The key changes whenever the graph's hash layout changes or a new node/edge type appears, i.e. on most trigger cycles and always across runs, so `observer_cache.lookup` misses and the quota (max_observer_calls) is spent re-asking an identical question. The persisted cache_prior/verdict reuse advertised by `clear_task_bound` is effectively unreachable, inflating Observer calls and skewing the cost/benefit numbers reported for the Observer.
confirmed.fix: Sort and deduplicate `edge_types`/`node_types` before hashing and derive `subject` deterministically (e.g. the lexicographically smallest non-unattributed agent), so structurally identical graphs map to one key within a run.

verification.reason: The mechanics are as claimed: runtime.rs:1132-1166 builds the key by collecting one string per node/edge from graph.all_edges()/all_nodes(), and graph.rs:33-34 stores nodes/edges in std HashMap with all_nodes/all_edges returning values() (graph.rs:654-661); observer/types.rs:273-287 hashes the slices in iteration order with no sort/dedup; subject is an arbitrary first non-unattributed Agent via find_map (runtime.rs:1141-1149), likewise order-dependent. The key feeds lookup at runtime.rs:1168, and a hit replays the stored verdict via CachedObserver (runtime.rs:1200-1212) without incrementing observer_calls (runtime.rs:1302-1305), so key instability does defeat the exact-signature dedup the cache promises. However, several impact statements are overstated or wrong: the cache is in-memory only (cache.rs:49 `l1: HashMap<u32, ObserverOutput>`), never persisted, so "always across runs" is moot; L2 was deliberately removed and build_prior always returns CachePrior::default() (cache.rs:73-76), so the "persisted cache_prior ... advertised by clear_task_bound" claim is false (clear_task_bound at cache.rs:79-81 only clears L1); and because the key contains one entry per node/edge rather than distinct types, it changes on any graph growth even after sorting, while within a single run with unchanged graph contents the same HashMap instance iterates in stable order, so repeated evaluation of an identical graph can still hit and "almost never hits" is unsupported. The proposed dedup would also create false hits by discarding counts. Net: a genuine but low-impact canonicalization defect.

confirmed.title: Provenance taint is order-blind and attributed before identity resolution
confirmed.evidence: route_event_inner registers every tool result of the request body via provenance.observe_request with `agent = identity_resolver.agent_for_process(pid)` resolved *before* dispatch_event runs identity resolution for this event (runtime.rs:416-445), and annotate_intent is then applied to all intents extracted from the same body (474-494). SpanStore::match_untrusted filters by agent only when both sides are Some (span_store.rs:133-138) and never compares the span timestamp (stored by observe_request but unused) with the intent timestamp.
confirmed.impact: Two false-positive paths: (a) a tool result that appears later in the conversation than the tool call being annotated still taints it, because the whole body's tool_results are registered before the intent is checked; (b) spans recorded while the process had no provisional agent (None) taint every agent, so in multi-agent runs one agent's untrusted output can raise an UntrustedInstructionFlow PBC claim against another agent. Both depend on event ordering, which the routing code itself notes is not globally ordered across CPUs.
confirmed.fix: Resolve the agent after dispatch (or re-annotate intents once identity is known) and store the observed-at timestamp on each span and reject spans newer than the intent; drop spans with unknown attribution from cross-agent matching instead of letting them match everyone.

verification.reason: The code matches the claim. In `runtime.rs`, `route_event_inner` reads the LLM request body and calls `provenance.observe_request` with `agent_for_process(ProcessId::new(event.pid, data["start_time_ns"].unwrap_or(0)))` at lines 416-435, *before* `dispatch_event` at 447-453; for a raw TLS/plaintext body (source "ssl"/connection_id), `classify_event` returns `Signals` (routing.rs:455-457) so dispatch calls `identity_resolver.resolve_provisional(resolved_pid, ...)` at routing.rs:223, i.e. identity is resolved after the span was already attributed. Moreover the lookup key at runtime.rs:421-428 uses the event's `start_time_ns` (0 for HTTP/TLS-layer events per routing.rs:641-658) rather than `resolve_process_id`, so it misses the provisional map keyed on the real start time and yields `None`. The annotation loop at runtime.rs:474-494 then re-resolves the agent for `intent.process_id` (line 476), which may be `Some`. In `span_store.rs`, `ContentSpan.timestamp_ns` is populated (add at 92-106) but `match_untrusted` (120-160) never reads it, and its agent filter (134-139) only skips when *both* span agent and query agent are `Some` — a `None`-attributed span therefore matches every agent, contradicting the doc comment "Content from another agent's request never taints this one" (provenance_tracker.rs:76-78). Because all tool results in the body are registered before any of that body's intents are checked (parse_request_provenance collects every tool result; extract_from_request emits history tool_use intents), a result later in the conversation can taint an earlier tool call, and in multi-agent runs a `None` span from one agent can match another agent's intent; a match calls `annotate_intent` (provenance_tracker.rs:133-156) and graph_builder.rs:962-984 mints the `UntrustedInstructionFlow` PBC edge against that agent. No re-annotation or post-dispatch span fixup exists (only call sites are runtime.rs:429/430 and 474-494), and the only `None`-agent test is the `store_is_bounded` bound test (span_store.rs:358-370), not cross-agent matching. Severity medium is appropriate: the impact is false-positive provenance/claims in the project's core mechanism, though it is a conservative over-taint rather than a missed detection.

confirmed.title: Intent/action buffers grow without bound and every trigger reprocesses all historical intents
confirmed.evidence: trigger_inner does `self.graph_buffer.intents.drain(..)` and then re-pushes every intent (runtime.rs:834-867), so each cycle runs handle_intent_content and handle_intent_pbc over every intent ever seen. The cleanup block clears nodes/edges/evidence/timeline but explicitly keeps intents and actions (1603-1610), GraphDeltaBuffer::clear() also leaves intents/actions untouched (buffer.rs:133-141), and lookups are linear scans (`self.intents.iter().find`, buffer.rs:124-131) performed once per evidence item in the hot loop (runtime.rs:887-888).
confirmed.impact: Work per trigger is O(intents x triggers) and the evidence phase is O(evidence x intents), i.e. quadratic in run length, and graph_buffer.actions is never pruned at all. For the long corpus runs the collector spends increasing CPU per trigger inside the event loop (compounding the blocking issue above) and memory grows monotonically.
confirmed.fix: Keep only the intents/actions still needed (e.g. those without a terminal correlation, bounded by an LRU/window), index them by IntentId/ActionId in a HashMap, and move phase-2 history into a separate append-only store rather than re-scanning the phase-1 buffer.

verification.reason: Confirmed in the snapshot. runtime.rs:834 drains `self.graph_buffer.intents` and line 866 unconditionally re-pushes each intent (`push_intent` is documented as unconditional at buffer.rs:66-71), while the per-trigger cleanup at runtime.rs:1607-1610 clears only nodes/edges/evidence/timeline and intents/actions survive until `std::mem::take` in `finalize()` at runtime.rs:1700-1701. Consequently every `trigger()` (fired every `trigger_every_n`=50 events at runtime.rs:2222-2223) re-runs `handle_intent_content` and `handle_intent_pbc` for all intents ever seen (runtime.rs:836-864), with `handle_intent_pbc` scanning every `tool_args` entry through `evaluate_boundary_policy_with_resource` (graph_builder.rs:1038+). The evidence phase drains only new evidence (runtime.rs:874) but resolves parents via `find_intent_by_id`/`find_action_by_id`, which are linear `iter().find` scans at buffer.rs:125 and buffer.rs:130 (used at runtime.rs:887-888), giving O(evidence x intents); the envelope block at runtime.rs:793-801 adds another full-history pass per trigger. The re-processing is idempotent (ensure_policy_boundary_node dedupes at graph_builder.rs:1272-1297, upsert_provisional_pbc at graph_builder.rs:136), so this is wasted CPU and monotonic memory rather than a correctness bug. One detail in the claim is wrong: GraphDeltaBuffer::clear() at buffer.rs:133-141 does clear intents and actions (lines 137-138) and is not called on this buffer at all, but that does not affect the core finding.

confirmed.title: Content-hash intent dedup is global and never reset, so legitimate repeats are dropped
confirmed.evidence: accept_intent_once inserts into `seen_intent_signatures`, whose key is (pid, start_time_ns, tool_name, serialised args) with no turn/message component (buffer.rs:45, 80-83, 151-163). The set is not cleared by GraphDeltaBuffer::clear() (133-141) and init_session() resets the cache and provenance but not the buffer (runtime.rs:360-373).
confirmed.impact: An agent that legitimately issues the same tool call twice (e.g. two identical `Bash{command:"ls"}` or two identical writes) is counted as one intent for the whole run: the second occurrence produces no intent, no evidence and no repetition signal, so D4/pbc_repetition_count and any rate/frequency metric systematically under-count repeated behaviour - exactly the signal most attacks rely on. Reusing a runtime instance for a second session silently suppresses all intents seen in the first.
confirmed.fix: Key the dedup on the message/response identity (message_id or turn index) rather than content alone, or bound the set to the current conversation turn and clear it in init_session().

verification.reason: The cited mechanism is real: buffer.rs:45 declares `seen_intent_signatures: HashSet<u64>` per-run; buffer.rs:80-83 `accept_intent_once` inserts only `intent_content_signature()`; and buffer.rs:151-162 hashes only `process_id.pid`, `process_id.start_time_ns`, `tool_name`, and serialized `tool_args` — no message id, turn index, or event ordinal. `clear()` (buffer.rs:134-141) clears nodes/edges/intents/actions/evidence/timeline but explicitly NOT the signature set, and `init_session()` (runtime.rs:360-373) clears only `observer_cache.clear_task_bound()` and `provenance`, never `graph_buffer` (created once at runtime.rs:319), so the set persists for the entire run and would survive a second `process()` call on a reused Analyzer. Both live call sites (routing.rs:164 for openclaw TOOL_CALL and routing.rs:334 for request-body extraction) `continue`/skip on a false return, so the duplicate intent is never pushed, never persisted, and never gets its own evidence. Crucially, `extract_from_request` (intent_extractor.rs:398-480) walks every assistant message in the conversation and emits one Intent per `tool_use` block with no per-block stable id, so two genuinely distinct but content-identical calls (e.g. `Bash{ls}` in two different turns, or an identical write retried) both hash to the same signature and the second is silently discarded — exactly the reviewer's claim. Two parts of the stated impact are overstated, which is why I keep (not raise) severity: (1) `EvidenceCorrelator::on_action` (correlator.rs:224-286) matches each incoming action against the retained intent buffer (120 s TTL, buffer.rs:18-19), so a repeated syscall within the window can still produce a second evidence pair `(first_intent_id, second_action_id)` via `try_correlate` (correlator.rs:480-520), and graph_builder.rs:192-193/868-869 appends distinct evidence ids to `evidence_refs`, so `pbc_repetition_count` (runtime.rs:2140-2151) can partially recover; (2) `sub_score_role` divides `pbc_count` by `intent_count` (scoring.rs:347-350), so undercounting intents can inflate D3 rather than only deflate D4. But the underlying defect — content-only, never-reset dedup that cannot distinguish re-observation of history from a legitimate repeat, with the feasible fix (history-ordinal/turn component, which is stable across later requests unlike the freshly generated `message_id`) — is present exactly as described.

confirmed.title: EvaluationSummary reports fabricated/duplicated counts
confirmed.evidence: `run_duration_ms: 0` is hardcoded (runtime.rs:1954). `claim_count` is `phase1_claim_count + claims.len()` (1961) although ClaimIds are deterministic (comment at 1449-1450) and phase 2 rebuilds the same claims with an empty skip set (1821-1826), so every claim is counted twice. `alert_count` is `phase1_alert_count + u64::from(can_identify_agent)` (1962), counting a final alert even when the alert write/emit path is skipped or fails (1901-1910).
confirmed.impact: The `[evaluation:json]` line is the machine-readable result of a run; it reports a zero duration, ~2x claim counts, and an alert count that does not match the `alerts` table. Any FPR/recall or per-run aggregate built from this summary is wrong in a run-length-dependent way (more triggers = more double counting).
confirmed.fix: Record the session start Instant in init_session and compute run_duration_ms from it; report claim_count as the number of distinct ClaimIds persisted (the phase-2 set), and derive alert_count from the alerts actually written.

confirmed.title: Phase-1 alert gate's agent-identification condition is vacuous

confirmed.title: HardViolation is raised for intent-only provisional PBCs, not confirmed actions
confirmed.evidence: final_decision.rs:14 defines a hard violation as a rule on a confirmed action, but RuleEngine::evaluate (rule_engine.rs:58-101) scans graph.all_edges() with no check of edge confidence, phase or evidence_refs. confirmed.fix: Only let a rule hit become a HardViolation when the hosting edge is backed by confirmed action evidence (non-empty evidence_refs, Authoritative phase, or a confidence floor); route provisional intent PBCs to the Observer as candidates instead.

confirmed.title: IpLiteral rule flags private and routine IP connections as hard Unsafe

confirmed.fix: Derive OperationCategory from action/edge semantics (file write, file exec, process enumeration) or delete the unused categories and unreachable rule; add a test proving hog.sh produces an Unsafe hit.

Its only call sites are rule_engine.rs:66 and 87, both inside `evaluate` (52-110), and a repo-wide grep of Rust sources shows `OperationCategory` is referenced only in rules.rs and rule_engine.rs, so no parallel classifier exists; FileWrite appears only as a rule `operation_types` entry (rule_engine.rs:285, safe.cargo_output, which also lists FileRead) and ProcessEnum/ResourceHog appear only at rules.rs:21/23 and rule_engine.rs:444. `unsafe.hog_script` (441-446) requires FileExec|ResourceHog with Glob "**/hog.sh" (443-444), but `extract_resources` formats a Process resource exclusively as `format!("process:{}:{}", pid, start_time_ns)` (194-197), which cannot match a pattern ending in `/hog.sh`; when hog.sh appears as a File resource the op is FileRead, which the rule's operation_types exclude. There is no test mentioning hog anywhere in collector/src, so nothing exercises the rule. The one theoretical escape (AgentDelegatesTo also yields FileExec at line 165) does not rescue it: extract_resources emits nothing for ToolCall/LlmConversation targets and Context ids are conversation identifiers, not file paths. Severity medium is reasonable — dead rule plus lost write/exec semantics means `/tmp`-resident script execution can even be labeled Safe by safe.tmp_normal.

confirmed.title: Observer signature carries a score breakdown computed from zeroed inputs
confirmed.evidence: build_observer_signature calls compute_score_breakdown with repetition_count=0, intent_count=0 and ScoreSignals::default() (scoring.rs:466-474), then stores that breakdown next to the real score argument (scoring.rs:632-651). With intent_count=0 the role score falls back to the PBC/agent sigmoid centered at 100*agent_count (scoring.rs:353-356), and content, baseline and repetition contributions vanish.
confirmed.impact: The LLM arbiter receives a breakdown whose total is inconsistent with classification.score and which systematically understates role/content signals. Arbitration is biased by numbers the engine did not actually compute, and the Observer reasoning cannot be audited against the score it was given.
confirmed.fix: Thread the real repetition_count, intent_count and ScoreSignals into build_observer_signature, or omit the breakdown from the signature so only the correctly computed score is shown.

verification.reason: The code does exactly what the claim says. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/classification/scoring.rs, build_observer_signature (lines 459-474) calls compute_score_breakdown with literal 0 for repetition_count (line 471), literal 0 for intent_count (line 472) and ScoreSignals::default() (line 473; derived Default at lines 28-32 yields content_threat=None and baseline_deviation=None), then stores that breakdown as classification.score_breakdown (line 636) alongside the real score argument (line 634). The real score is produced in engine.rs where compute_score and compute_score_breakdown are both given the actual repetition_count, intent_count and signals (engine.rs:117-128), and only the score is forwarded to build_observer_signature at engine.rs:229 — so the breakdown and the score in the same struct come from different inputs. The consequences are real in the path actually used: provider.rs:120 builds the prompt with build_compact_prompt, which prints D1-D6 directly from that breakdown — d3 = sb.role_score, d4 = sb.repetition_score, d6 = sb.behavioral_score (llm.rs:167-177) — next to the correctly computed Score (line 178). With intent_count=0 the role score takes the fallback branch at scoring.rs:347-356 (center = 100.0 * agent_count), and repetition_score = sub_score_repetition(0) = 0.0 (lines 372-376), so the role and repetition dimensions shown to the arbiter are systematically understated relative to the score. One small part of the impact wording is inaccurate rather than refuting: because ScoreSignals::default() sets baseline_deviation=None, D6 does not vanish — it falls back to sub_score_behavioral(graph, evidence_records) (scoring.rs:427-430) — and the content signal is at least shown separately through content_signals in the prompt. But the central defect (a breakdown whose dimensions/total were computed from zeroed inputs, displayed next to a differently computed score) is present at the cited lines and reachable on every ToObserver path.

confirmed.title: Replay passes intent count as repetition_count, so replayed scores cannot match live phase 2
confirmed.evidence: classify_authoritative's fourth argument is repetition_count and fifth is intent_count (engine.rs:397-400). Live phase 2 passes pbc_repetition_count(graph) and all_intents.len() (runtime.rs:1761-1774), but replay passes intents.len() for both arguments, with the comment that these are the same inputs as the live Phase 2 path (executor.rs:213-218).
confirmed.impact: sub_score_repetition becomes intents.len()/50 (scoring.rs:360-365), inflating D4 in replay, while replay also supplies ScoreSignals::default(). Replay-derived scores, alerts and any GT verification built on replay therefore disagree with live runs despite the code claiming parity.
confirmed.fix: Compute pbc_repetition_count on the replay graph for the fourth argument, keep intents.len() only as intent_count, and thread persisted content/baseline signals if replay parity is to be claimed.

verification.reason: The code matches the claim exactly. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/replay/executor.rs:213-218 the replay calls classify_authoritative with graph_builder.graph(), patterns, evidence, then `intents.len() as u32` twice, and the inline comments explicitly assert "same inputs as the live Phase 2 path". The callee signature at classification/engine.rs:393-402 names the 4th and 5th parameters `repetition_count` and `intent_count`, and both are forwarded into compute_score/compute_score_breakdown (engine.rs:406-421), so the 4th argument is unambiguously the repetition count. The live Phase 2 path at runtime/runtime.rs:1760-1775 instead computes `let repetition_count = pbc_repetition_count(graph); let intent_count = all_intents.len() as u32;` and passes those, where pbc_repetition_count (runtime.rs:2140-2151) is the max evidence_refs length across PolicyBoundaryCrossing edges — a graph-derived quantity, not the number of intents. sub_score_repetition (classification/scoring.rs:360-365) is `(repetition_count/50).min(1.0)` and feeds D4 with weight 0.10 (scoring.rs:61-92), so replay's D4 is driven by total intent count while live D4 is driven by repeated boundary observations; these coincide only in the accidental case where one PBC edge has evidence_refs equal to the total intent count. Additionally, replay passes `ScoreSignals::default()` (executor.rs:219) while live passes `content_threat: self.last_content_threat` and `baseline_deviation: self.last_baseline_deviation` (runtime.rs:1771-1774); scoring.rs:53-65 and 413-425 show those signals override/replace the D2 pattern and D6 behavioral dimensions, so replay scores diverge there too. The divergence is not inert: the classification_result is fed directly into AlertBuilder::compose (executor.rs:279-290), so replay alerts/refinements can differ from live Phase 2, and the comment's parity assertion is false. A fix is feasible without new data plumbing for the repetition argument since pbc_repetition_count only needs the replay graph (though it is currently a private fn in runtime.rs, so it would need moving/exposing), while full ScoreSignals parity would require persisted content/baseline values.

confirmed.title: Blanket /root/ sensitive-path rule turns every root-owned workspace file into a boundary crossing
confirmed.evidence: SENSITIVE contains the substring /root/ (policy.rs:550) and is_sensitive_path uses path.contains (policy.rs:576); is_safe_internal has no /root exemption (policy.rs:492-527). The graph-builder skip for workspace/build paths (graph_builder.rs:608-620) only knows /tmp/claude-, /proc, /sys, /dev and build directories (graph_builder.rs:1473-1480), not the runtime workspace root.
confirmed.impact: Agents running as root in containers or VMs, a common benchmark setup with the workspace under /root, get an Observed boundary crossing for every file they touch. This forces Observer calls and produces review/Uncertain verdicts for entirely benign file access.
confirmed.fix: Replace /root/ with specific secret paths (for example /root/.ssh, /root/.aws, /root/.config/gcloud) or exempt a runtime-derived workspace prefix before applying the sensitive-path list.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what the claim reports. policy.rs:550 includes "/root/" in SENSITIVE and line 576 matches via path.contains; is_safe_internal (492-527) is the sole whitelist and contains no /root exemption, so the early return at 529 does not help. evaluate_capability_boundary marks any sensitive file Observed/matched (lines 85-92), and the only precondition is is_concrete_path (319-329, checked at 337-348), which accepts any absolute path such as /root/workspace/src/main.rs. In graph_builder.rs the action-level call at 581 is skipped only by is_workspace_path (608-611; intent-level equivalent at 1047-1052), whose prefix list (1473-1481) covers only /tmp/claude-, /proc/, /sys/, /dev/ plus build artifacts (1491-1499), and is_workspace_path (1538-1547) has no runtime workspace-root logic. No other filter removes /root paths. The claimed impact also follows: PBC edges drive has_boundary_signal and ToObserver in classification/engine.rs:133-155. The only caveat is that the trigger requires a workspace under /root (current scenarios use /home/lzk, /tmp, /etc), exactly as the claim conditions it; no code refutes it.

confirmed.title: Unevidenced provisional PBC edges become Confirmed/Critical claims with empty evidence_refs
confirmed.evidence: claim_builder.rs:208 copies `edge.evidence_refs` verbatim onto the claim, and there is no non-empty check. graph_builder.rs:159-167 (`upsert_provisional_pbc`) creates PolicyBoundaryCrossing edges with `evidence_refs: vec![]`; the content/provenance producers at graph_builder.rs:951 and 979 rely on a later `upsert_pbc_edge` upgrade that only happens when a correlated action for the same (agent, boundary) key arrives (graph_builder.rs:190-216). Intents with no syscall action (UserPrompt / content-boundary path) never get that upgrade, yet claim_builder.rs:384-395 maps their 0.80-0.85 confidence to `Confirmed` and claim_builder.rs:401-411 to `AlertSeverity::Critical`.
confirmed.impact: The flagship prompt-injection and provenance boundaries are persisted as Confirmed Critical claims backed by zero evidence; traceback then cannot find an evidence-linked edge and falls back arbitrarily, and the claim counts as evidence in downstream metrics.
confirmed.fix: Refuse to emit a claim whose evidence_refs is empty (or emit it as Unproven with a dedicated provisional claim type), and have phase 2 delete or explicitly downgrade provisional PBC edges that were never upgraded with correlation evidence.

verification.reason: The core defect holds. claim_builder.rs:164-215 iterates every PolicyBoundaryCrossing edge in the graph with no evidence filter, and line 208 copies `evidence_refs: edge.evidence_refs.clone()` verbatim; graph_builder.rs:136-176 (`upsert_provisional_pbc`) creates those edges with `evidence_refs: vec![]` at line 164. The upgrade path (`upsert_pbc_edge`, graph_builder.rs:180-230, provisional adoption at 206-215) only fires when correlation evidence with the same (source,target) key arrives. The 0.85 provenance producer at graph_builder.rs:962-985 keys the boundary on the synthetic `NormalizedResource::ToolCall { tool_name: "UntrustedInstructionFlow", call_id: span_id }`, which no action/correlation path ever produces (action paths key on real evidence resources at 640-660, 687; `handle_intent_pbc` keys on file/URL resources at 1060-1074), and runtime.rs:475-486 populates `intent_provenance` precisely for intents matched to untrusted content, so these edges stay evidence-free. Claims are built from the live builder graph including provisional edges (runtime.rs:909/1377 phase 1, runtime.rs:1754/1822 phase 2 with an empty `claimed` set, so even phase 1 omissions are re-claimed), then persisted with empty refs and no filter (runtime.rs:1506/1888; writer.rs:856-877). claim_builder.rs:178 + 384-395 map the 0.85 edge to `Confirmed`, and severity_for_claim_type at 401-411 yields `Critical` for PolicyViolation above 0.80 (and for the other non-Blocked types above 0.70), so a Confirmed/Critical claim with zero evidence is persisted. traceback.rs:197-227 then scores candidate edges only by agent match and evidence overlap, so with empty evidence it ties at score 2 and picks the first matching edge (and generate_explanation at 299 suppresses the evidence line). One correction to the claim's wording: the 0.80 content-boundary edge produced at graph_builder.rs:951 (and the 0.60 edge at 1072) maps to `Observed`/`Inferred` and `Warning`, not `Confirmed`/`Critical`; only the 0.85 provenance edge produces Confirmed/Critical. That narrows the range but not the finding, which affects the flagship UntrustedInstructionFlow path.

confirmed.title: supply_chain_attack template is structurally impossible to match
confirmed.evidence: The template declares `required_edge_types: vec![IntentCausesAction, PolicyBoundaryCrossing]` with `min_distinct_agents: 2` (pattern_matcher.rs:276-286). `required_edges` is filtered to those two types (pattern_matcher.rs:70-73), then the multi-agent guard requires `has_cross_agent_edge` to find an edge whose type is Delegation/AgentDelegatesTo/ContextInheritance/ContextFlowsFrom/TaintPropagation/TaintPropagatesTo inside `required_edges` (pattern_matcher.rs:177-192). Neither ICA nor PBC is in that list, so the guard always returns None.
confirmed.impact: Supply-chain attacks are never detected by the graph-pattern layer, and the template silently contributes nothing while appearing implemented and passing the producer contract test.
confirmed.fix: Add a delegation/context-flow edge type to the template's required edges (as the other multi-agent templates do) or verify the cross-agent relation over the actual agent endpoint nodes of the component, not over the template-filtered edge list.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what the claim reports. `default_templates()` defines `supply_chain_attack` at /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/graph/pattern_matcher.rs:276-286 with `required_edge_types: vec![IntentCausesAction, PolicyBoundaryCrossing]`, `min_matches: 2`, and `min_distinct_agents: 2`. In `try_match`, `required_edges` is built by filtering `graph.all_edges()` with `template.required_edge_types.contains(&edge.edge_type)` (lines 70-73), so it can only ever contain ICA and PBC edges. The multi-agent guard at lines 177-193 runs because `min_distinct_agents >= 2`, and checks `required_edges.iter().any(...)` for Delegation | AgentDelegatesTo | ContextInheritance | ContextFlowsFrom | TaintPropagation | TaintPropagatesTo (lines 179-189); since neither ICA nor PBC appears in that `matches!` set, `has_cross_agent_edge` is a constant false and line 190 returns None for every graph, regardless of how many real cross-agent edges exist in the full graph (the check never looks outside `required_edges`). No refutation path exists: the matcher is actually used in production at runtime.rs:911-915 (and 1756-1760) and in replay/executor.rs:208-211, templates cannot be overridden per-template by config (only fully disabled via `disable_patterns` at runtime.rs:910), no test constructs a supply_chain match, and no other Rust code path detects supply-chain attacks (the only other Rust mention of supply-chain/typosquat is a benign-scenario string at runtime.rs:2120). The contract test does not catch it either: `matcher_reachable` in collector/tests/graph_pattern_contract.rs:187-197 evaluates cross-agent reachability against the global `produced_edges` vocabulary rather than the template's own `required_edge_types`, so it returns true and `inert_graph_templates` is empty at docs/capabilities.json:124 — exactly the "appears implemented, passes the contract test, silently contributes nothing" impact described. The contrast with the other multi-agent templates (multi_agent_collusion line 334 `AgentDelegatesTo`, trust_boundary_crossing line 345 `AgentDelegatesTo`, session_hijacking line 356 `ContextFlowsFrom`) shows the omission is unique to supply_chain_attack. Severity high is appropriate: the template is unreachable even when the correct delegation/process evidence exists, no other layer covers the category, and the test suite's reachability helper masks the defect.

confirmed.title: Pattern-match confidence is a hardcoded 1.0 and feeds 25% of the risk score
confirmed.evidence: `try_match` ends with `let confidence = 1.0;` (pattern_matcher.rs:195) for every match, independent of template, number of matched elements, or evidence confidence. `sub_score_pattern` averages those values (classification/scoring.rs:247-253) and that dimension is D2 with weight 0.25 in the fusion (scoring.rs:78-88). The same constant is persisted as `PatternVerdict.match_confidence` (classification/engine.rs:39-50).
confirmed.impact: One weak match (even the Info-severity `reconnaissance` template) drives a quarter of the fused risk score to 1.0 and records 100% match confidence, so the score and the persisted verdict are not calibrated to the evidence.
confirmed.fix: Compute confidence from match completeness and the confidence of the edges that satisfied the template (matched required edge types/resource kinds, min evidence confidence), and carry that value into scoring and persistence.

verification.reason: The code says exactly what the reviewer claims, and no intervening path re-derives or overrides the value. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/graph/pattern_matcher.rs, `GraphPatternMatch.confidence` is declared at line 38 and assigned the literal `let confidence = 1.0;` at line 195, then copied into the struct at line 207 for every successful `try_match`. `try_match` never reads `edge.confidence`, matched-edge counts, or per-template specificity: the only `confidence` token in the whole file besides lines 38/195/207 is `confidence: 0.9` inside the test edge helper at line 464. The value flows, unmodified, into (a) `sub_score_pattern` at collector/src/responsibility/classification/scoring.rs:247-252, which averages `p.confidence` and therefore returns 1.0 for any non-empty match; (b) `dims[1]`/`weights[1]` at scoring.rs:75-85, where weights are `[0.28, 0.25, 0.20, 0.10, 0.10, 0.07]`, so D2 carries 0.25 (the claim's "78-88" range closes over the correct lines); (c) the persisted `PatternVerdict.match_confidence` at collector/src/responsibility/classification/engine.rs:39-49 (field write at line 44), plus scoring.rs:558 and :646; and (d) the progressive scorer dimension `DimIndex::D2Content` at collector/src/responsibility/runtime/runtime.rs:957-962, which again averages `p.confidence`. The fusion math at scoring/fusion.rs:29-57 is a 50/50 blend of a weight-normalized linear term and a weighted geometric mean, so 0.25 is an accurate weight, and when D2 is the only active dimension the fused value is 0.625 (not merely 0.25), so the claim if anything understates the pre-gate effect. Two nuances do not refute it: `fuse_dimensions` is documented as a ranking heuristic (fusion.rs:5-7), and the final score is multiplied by `evidence_gate` (scoring.rs:156-164), which for the single-crossing reconnaissance case shrinks the final score substantially (≈0.0109), so the "quarter of the fused score" statement applies to `ScoreParts.raw`, not `final_score`; nevertheless the persisted `match_confidence` is 1.0 unconditionally, the progressive D2 dimension is ungated, and the frontend consumes the field as a confidence value (frontend/lib/trace-workbench.ts:253), so the calibration defect and the 100%-confidence record are real. High severity remains defensible given the ungated progressive path and persisted verdict, though the evidence gate limits how often the inflated fused term survives into the final alert score.

confirmed.title: Traceback can be built from an unrelated policy-boundary edge
confirmed.evidence: `find_boundary_edge_for_claim` scores +2 for a source-agent match and +1 per overlapping evidence ref (traceback.rs:208-227), the reverse of the priority documented immediately above (traceback.rs:189-192). When no edge scores above zero it falls back to `pbc_edges.first()` (traceback.rs:230-231). Claims whose PBC source node has no agent id get subject `unknown` (claim_builder.rs:169-172), so their own edge scores 0 and an arbitrary edge from a different agent is selected.
confirmed.impact: chain_node_ids, root_cause_node_id and the explanation summarize a different agent's crossing than the claim asserts, silently falsifying causal attribution in persisted tracebacks.
confirmed.fix: Rank evidence overlap above agent match, bind the claim to its originating edge (pass the EdgeId or require an evidence-ref overlap), and return None rather than a first-edge fallback when nothing relates.

verification.reason: I re-read the cited code and could not refute the claim. `find_boundary_edge_for_claim` (traceback.rs:193-232) scores each PBC edge as +2 for a source-agent match (212-218) and +1 per overlapping evidence ref (219-223), which is not the priority documented at 189-192 (evidence overlap first, agent match second); with these weights a single agent match (2) outranks one evidence overlap (1). `best` is only assigned when `score > best_score` (224), so ties keep the earliest-inserted edge (`add_edge` appends to `edges_by_type`, graph.rs:269-290; `edges_of_type` returns that slice, graph.rs:556-561), and when every edge scores 0 line 231 falls back to `pbc_edges.first()`. The `unknown`-subject path is reachable as claimed: claim_builder.rs:168-172 sets subject to `AgentId::from("unknown")` whenever the PBC source node has no `agent_id`; claim_builder.rs:208 clones the edge's evidence refs, and provisional PBC edges are created with `evidence_refs: vec![]` (graph_builder.rs:159-175), while PBC sources can be non-Agent resource nodes via `action_agent_node_id.unwrap_or(src_node_id)` / `intent_agent_node_id.unwrap_or(src_node_id)` where `src_node_id` itself falls back to `resource_node_id` (graph_builder.rs:434-439, 529, 640, 687, 765). Such a claim's own edge therefore scores 0-1, any other agent's edge scores 2, and `TracebackBuilder::build` then uses that edge's source as the chain start (traceback.rs:53-54, 84-88) and root cause (108-111), while the claim's own boundary (derived from its own edge target, claim_builder.rs:511-530) is never compared to the chosen edge's target. Tracebacks are built for every claim and persisted with no warning (runtime.rs:1510-1517, 1889-1897), so the misattribution is silent. The same tie-break also misbinds claims among multiple edges from a shared placeholder agent node (graph_builder.rs:1309-1333, used at 526/951/979), making this a real, not hypothetical, defect; I did not refute it and keep severity high.

confirmed.title: Phase-2 authoritative alerts always persist an empty pattern_verdicts list
confirmed.evidence: The `final_verdict` branch of `resolve_alert_judgment` returns `Vec::new(), Vec::new()` for rule and pattern verdicts (alert_builder.rs:284-285) instead of `classification_result.pattern_verdicts`, which is populated by the engine (classification/engine.rs:200, 222, 303, 444). confirmed.fix: Return `classification_result.pattern_verdicts` and the engine's rule verdicts from the final-verdict branch, or add an explicit patch in runtime phase 2 mirroring the rule-verdict patch.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what the claim states. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/claims/alert_builder.rs, `resolve_alert_judgment`'s `final_verdict` branch (lines 260-287) returns the tuple ending with `Vec::new(), Vec::new()` at lines 284-285, so both rule and pattern verdicts are empty; those values flow into `build_engine_section` via lines 141-155 and become `EngineSection.rule_verdicts/pattern_verdicts` (lines 496-497), which is what gets persisted as engine_section_json (writer.rs:829, schema.rs:457). confirmed.title: UnauthorizedCapabilityUse claim type is unreachable in the live graph
confirmed.evidence: `classify_claim_type` returns UnauthorizedCapabilityUse only when an IntentCausesAction edge satisfies `e.source == edge.source && e.target == edge.target` (claim_builder.rs:358-369). Every PBC target is created by `ensure_policy_boundary_node`, which always sets `node_type: PolicyBoundary` (graph_builder.rs:1272-1300; call sites include 636, 663, 763, 951, 979, 1072), while every ICA target is a Resource node from `ensure_resource_node` (graph_builder.rs:448-456), an Agent node, or the placeholder agent. The same NodeId can therefore never be both an ICA target and a PBC target.
confirmed.impact: One of six claim types, plus its severity/text/action-hint branches, can never be produced; capability crossings are misclassified as PolicyViolation/BlockedAttempt or, because of the graph-wide delegation test at claim_builder.rs:346-354, as SuspiciousDelegation.
confirmed.fix: Match the ICA edge to the crossing by resource identity (compare the target node's NormalizedResource or evidence refs) and scope the delegation test to edges whose evidence overlaps the claim.

verification.reason: Attempts to refute the claim fail. In claim_builder.rs the classifier is only invoked for PolicyBoundaryCrossing edges (lines 154-181, `classify_claim_type(graph, &edge, ...)`), and lines 358-369 require an IntentCausesAction edge with `e.source == edge.source && e.target == edge.target`. The live classifier always receives the GraphBuilder's in-memory graph (runtime.rs:1377 and 1822, replay/executor.rs:260), and every production IntentCausesAction edge is created only at graph/graph_builder.rs:433-456; its target is `resource_node_id` from `ensure_resource_node` (a `ResponsibilityNodeType::Resource`, graph_builder.rs:1243-1265, with `find_resource_node` restricted to Resource-type nodes, graph.rs:572-588), `action_agent_node_id` from `ensure_agent_node` (type Agent, graph_builder.rs:1217-1241), or `create_placeholder_agent_node` (type Agent, graph_builder.rs:1309-1332). Every PolicyBoundaryCrossing target, by contrast, is the node returned by `ensure_policy_boundary_node` (graph_builder.rs:1272-1300, which always sets `node_type: PolicyBoundary`, line 1286) at all call sites (517-535, 636-650, 663-687, 754-780, 934-951, 969-990, 1064-1072); there are no other production constructions of PolicyBoundaryCrossing edges, and the DB loader `get_graph` (reader.rs:609-661) is consumed only by the web API (web.rs:1291), never by the claim builder. NodeIds are fresh UUIDv4 values (ids.rs:59 via the `newtype_id!` macro), and phase-2 identity remapping changes only the `agent_id` field, never `node_id` or node type (graph_builder.rs:237-260; graph.rs:137-153), so no ID aliasing lets a boundary node coincide with a resource/agent node. The equality at claim_builder.rs:365 can therefore never hold, making `UnauthorizedCapabilityUse` and its severity/text/action-hint branches (claim_builder.rs:414, text.rs:115/236/270, traceback.rs:265) dead in the live graph. The claim's secondary line citations are slightly imprecise (ensure_resource_node is at 1243, not 448, and one call site is 754 rather than 763), but the core assertion is correct.

confirmed.title: Phase-2 graph refinements cite ids that exist in no other id domain
confirmed.evidence: Evidence refinements set `affected_edges` to `EdgeId::from(evidence_id)` (graph_builder.rs:1159-1164), casting an EvidenceId into the EdgeId domain, so no graph_edges row can match. Identity refinements filter nodes by `n.agent_id == Some(phase1_agent_id)` (graph_builder.rs:1093-1107), but the live path reassigns nodes to authoritative ids in `remap_agent_identities` (graph_builder.rs:238-263) before `finalize` is called (runtime.rs:1694-1697 then 1743), and replay builds nodes with authoritative ids directly (executor.rs:171-175), so the provisional id never matches and affected_nodes (and the edges derived from it) are empty.
confirmed.impact: Every graph_refinements row is unusable for audit: evidence refinements point at non-existent edges and identity refinements identify no affected nodes or edges, breaking replay diffing and any UI that resolves refinements against graph_nodes/graph_edges.
confirmed.fix: Capture affected node/edge ids before remapping (or retain a provisional→NodeId map), and translate evidence refinements by looking up graph edges whose evidence_refs contain the evidence id instead of casting ids.

verification.reason: The claim holds up. In graph_builder.rs the evidence-refinement loop (1140-1167) builds `affected_edges` from `ev_refinement.phase2_evidence_id.iter().map(|eid| EdgeId::from(eid.as_str()))` at exactly 1159-1164; since EdgeId and EvidenceId are both plain `String` newtypes (types/ids.rs:27-53), this silently relabels an EvidenceId as an EdgeId. `phase2_evidence_id` is populated with `ev.evidence_id` (evidence/correlator.rs:357, 410-411), while every graph edge uses a fresh UUID (`edge_id: EdgeId::new()` at graph_builder.rs:160, 219, 336, 449, 800, 819, 880), so no `graph_edges` row can ever match. For identity refinements, the filter at 1095-1101 compares `n.agent_id` to `id_refinement.phase1_agent_id`; union_find.rs:651-663 is the only constructor and sets `phase1_agent_id` to a provisional UUID while `phase2_agent_id` is the authoritative `agent-<sha8>` id (union_find.rs:254-264). The live path remaps every one of those provisional ids to the authoritative id first: runtime.rs:1695-1696 calls `remap_agent_identities` (graph_builder.rs:238-263, which uses `reassign_agent` to overwrite `node.agent_id`, graph.rs:137-153) and the same builder's `finalize` runs at runtime.rs:1741-1743; live `handle` used the provisional `IdentityResolver` (runtime.rs:891-895, resolver.rs:267-271), so the provisional id that finalize searches for has already been erased from every node. Replay does not remap at all, but executor.rs:171 builds an `AuthoritativeIdentityProvider` from `agent.agent_id` (executor.rs:666-677) and feeds it through `handle` at 185, so replay nodes carry authoritative ids from creation; finalize at 200-201 therefore also finds nothing for the provisional `phase1_agent_id`. Because refinements are only emitted for exactly the provisional refs that populate the remap map, affected_nodes/affected_edges are always empty there. The persistence layer serializes these arrays verbatim (writer.rs:954-973, schema.rs:410-417), and there is no post-processing that translates them, so the audit weakness is real. Minor overstatements in the claim: it cites runtime.rs rather than runtime/runtime.rs, and "breaking replay diffing" is unsupported because diff_runs/diff_snapshot (run_diff.rs:38, snapshot.rs:101-117) use alert JSON and snapshot node/edge ids, not refinements; the only non-Rust consumer merely counts rows (frontend/lib/db-import.ts:527). The core defect and proposed fix (capture ids before remap, or resolve evidence refinements via `evidence_refs`) are accurate, so I keep the severity at medium.

confirmed.title: Final-verdict alert confidence is computed and then discarded
confirmed.evidence: `resolve_alert_judgment` returns a verdict-derived confidence for the final verdict (alert_builder.rs:271-276: Safe 1.0, Unsafe/Authoritative 0.95, Unsafe/other 0.80, Uncertain 0.50), but `compose_with_context` uses that value only when `observer_output.is_some()` (alert_builder.rs:196-198). Phase 2 passes `observer_output: None` with `final_verdict: Some(...)` (runtime.rs:1860-1874), so the alert stores `engine_confidence` computed from `classification_result.score` instead (alert_builder.rs:203-211).
confirmed.impact: The authoritative alert can persist a Safe decision with confidence 1.0 - score (e.g. 0.2 at score 0.8), or an Unsafe verdict with a confidence unrelated to its authority, contradicting the same run's final verdict and phase-1 alert.
confirmed.fix: Branch on `final_verdict.is_some()` (or simply use the returned confidence whenever the final-verdict or observer branch produced it) instead of keying on observer_output.

verification.reason: The code says exactly what the claim states. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/claims/alert_builder.rs, `resolve_alert_judgment`'s `final_verdict` branch (lines 251-287) computes a verdict-derived confidence at lines 271-276 (Safe -> 1.0, Unsafe/Authoritative -> 0.95, Unsafe/other -> 0.80, Uncertain -> 0.50) and returns it at line 281. In `compose_with_context`, that returned value is bound to `confidence` at line 138 and is consumed only at lines 196-197, guarded by `if observer_output.is_some()`. Phase 2 at runtime.rs:1860-1874 passes `None` for `observer_output` (line 1862) and `final_verdict: Some(&final_verdict)` (line 1874), so the predicate is always false on that path and `final_confidence` comes from the engine branch at lines 203-211; the returned verdict confidence is therefore dead on every actual final-verdict caller (the only other caller, runtime.rs:1477, passes `final_verdict: None`). No later code overwrites `alert.confidence` (no such assignment in runtime.rs), and the tests cover only the observer path (alert_builder.rs:716) and the decision/authority fields of the final-verdict path (lines 889-947), never its confidence. One correction to the claim's impact wording: the "1.0 - score" branch applies only for score < 0.15 (line 203), so a Safe verdict at score 0.8 would persist 0.8, not 0.2; the sharper real case is an `Uncertain` final verdict (intended 0.50) persisted with engine confidence 0.85-1.0 for a high score, or a Supporting Unsafe (intended 0.80) persisted at the engine score. The defect and the proposed fix (branch on `final_verdict.is_some()`, or have `resolve_alert_judgment` signal which branch produced the confidence) are both valid.

confirmed.title: ResponsibilityClaim.traceback_ref is documented as filled later but is never written
confirmed.evidence: Claims are built with `traceback_ref: None // filled later by TracebackBuilder` (claim_builder.rs:210). `TracebackBuilder::build` only constructs a ResponsibilityTraceback carrying `claim_id` (traceback.rs:173-181) and never mutates the claim; the only other occurrences of the field are the SQL writer/reader and test fixtures. Runtime persists the claim first (runtime.rs:1501-1508) and only then builds the traceback (runtime.rs:1510-1516), and phase 2 repeats the same order (runtime.rs:1885-1900).
confirmed.impact: responsibility_claims.traceback_ref is NULL in every database, so the documented bidirectional claim↔traceback link does not exist and consumers joining on that column get nothing.
confirmed.fix: Set traceback_ref on the claim and re-persist the claim after the traceback is created, or remove the column/field and document the reverse foreign key as the only link.

verification.reason: I could not refute this. `claim_builder.rs:210` sets `traceback_ref: None` with the comment "filled later by TracebackBuilder", and no code ever assigns the field: grep over the whole repo shows the only construction sites are claim_builder.rs:210, traceback.rs:464, text.rs:321 and alert_builder.rs:639, and every one is `None` (the latter three are test fixtures). `TracebackBuilder::build` takes `&ResponsibilityClaim` (traceback.rs:42-45) and returns a `ResponsibilityTraceback` built at traceback.rs:173-181 that only carries `claim_id`; it never mutates the claim. Persistence order is exactly as claimed: runtime/runtime.rs:1501-1508 writes `PersistRecord::Claim(claim.clone())` and only then runtime.rs:1510-1516 builds/persists the traceback, and phase 2 repeats it at runtime.rs:1885-1900 (note the real path is runtime/runtime.rs, not runtime.rs, but the behavior is identical). There is no second claim write, no `UPDATE responsibility_claims` statement, and no setter anywhere; `writer.rs:854-878` only reads `claim.traceback_ref`, so the value written to `responsibility_claims.traceback_ref` (schema.rs:480) is always NULL. The frontend explicitly works around this (`frontend/lib/traceback-index.ts:6`, `db-import.ts:348`), and archived specs/plans record the observed "22 claims all NULL", corroborating the impact. The reason I am lowering severity from medium to low is that the reverse foreign key `responsibility_tracebacks.claim_id` (schema.rs:490-497, indexed by idx_tracebacks_claim) is fully populated and is what consumers actually use, so nothing is functionally broken today — the defect is a dead schema column plus a false "filled later" comment that will mislead future developers.

confirmed.title: CorrelationEvidence.matched_fields is always empty
confirmed.evidence: Both evidence producers fill `matched_fields` with a NormalizedArgs whose every field is None/empty (correlator.rs:506-518 for streaming and correlator.rs:362-369 for batch), even though `match_args` knows which intent/action arguments matched. The value is persisted as matched_fields_json (writer.rs:666-671) and read back (reader.rs:499-511). The L4/L5 quality gate is also fed `format_matched_string`, which returns the first path/command in the action rather than the matched argument (correlator.rs:64-83, 466-474).
confirmed.impact: No evidence row records which argument linked an intent to an action, so evidence cannot be audited or explained, and replay/run_diff comparisons that key on matched_fields are meaningless.
confirmed.fix: Return the matched arg pair from match_args and populate matched_fields from it; pass the actually matched string to `passes_quality_gate`.

verification.reason: The claim is supported by the code. The only two CorrelationEvidence producers in the collector are correlator.rs:356-369 (batch) and correlator.rs:505-518 (streaming); both literally construct `matched_fields: NormalizedArgs { canonical_path: None, host: None, port: None, command: None, raw_args: Vec::new() }`, so the field is always empty. argument_matcher::match_args (argument_matcher.rs:52-73) returns only `Option<(MatchLevel, f32)>` and discards which argument pair produced the match, so callers at correlator.rs:308 and 464 cannot populate the field without changing that signature. The empty value is persisted verbatim: writer.rs:666-671 serializes `ev.matched_fields` into `matched_fields_json`, and reader.rs:496-512 deserializes it back. run_diff.rs:35-45 additionally keys on `matched_fields.candidate_type`, a key that does not exist in the NormalizedArgs schema (evidence_types.rs:37-43), so those comparisons collapse to "unknown" — reinforcing the stated impact. The secondary point also checks out: at correlator.rs:466-474 `format_matched_string` (defined at 64-83) returns the first Path/Command/Url arg of the action (or fallback intent), not the actually matched argument, and that string is passed to passes_quality_gate (quality.rs:26), so the L5 min-length check measures an arbitrary argument rather than the matched substring. No post-construction code mutates matched_fields, so nothing refills it downstream. Severity medium is appropriate: this is an auditability/explainability and diff-key defect rather than a corruption of match_level/confidence, which are computed independently.

confirmed.title: detection_evasion template fires on any file access plus any boundary crossing
confirmed.evidence: The `detection_evasion` template (pattern_matcher.rs:318-328) requires only an IntentCausesAction edge targeting a File, the presence of a File resource kind, and any PolicyBoundaryCrossing in the same component. Neither the template nor `try_match` contains any log-file, log-deletion, or log-tampering constraint; the evidence it accepts is a strict superset of what `reconnaissance` accepts (pattern_matcher.rs:298-317).
confirmed.impact: Ordinary file activity with any boundary crossing persists a Warning-severity "attempts to evade detection through log manipulation" verdict, inflating false positives in every alert that carries engine.pattern_verdicts.
confirmed.fix: Anchor the template to detection-relevant resources (log paths, shell history, audit configuration) and add a resource constraint in the matcher before allowing the template to fire.

verification.reason: The cited template is exactly as described: `detection_evasion` at pattern_matcher.rs:318-328 requires `required_edge_types: [IntentCausesAction, PolicyBoundaryCrossing]`, `required_resource_kinds: [File]`, and `required_edge_target_kinds: [(IntentCausesAction, File)]` with `min_matches: 2, min_distinct_agents: 1`. The only generic constraints in `try_match` (pattern_matcher.rs:59-213) are connectivity among required edges, node-type presence, resource-kind presence on endpoint nodes (126-138), edge-target resource kinds (140-158), distinct edge-type count, and agent distinctness; there is no path, log-file, deletion, history, or audit-config check anywhere, and `detection_evasion` is the only place the template id appears in production code (grep of collector/src, collector/tests, docs returns only pattern_matcher.rs:319). Compared with `reconnaissance` (296-317), which additionally requires `(PolicyBoundaryCrossing, File)` at 311-314, detection_evasion accepts a strict superset: any graph satisfying reconnaissance also satisfies detection_evasion. The reachability is real, not hypothetical: graph_builder.rs:433-452 creates an `IntentCausesAction` edge to a File resource for every correlated file action, and graph_builder.rs:600-640 creates a `PolicyBoundaryCrossing` from the same agent node to a `PolicyBoundary` node carrying that resource (ensure_policy_boundary_node at 1272-1299), so benign file activity that trips the policy engine yields both edges in one component; docs/superpowers/TOP-TIER-AUDIT-2026-10-20.md:159-170 records this exact false positive on the benign `credential-rotation-plan` scenario. The consequence is somewhat weaker than the claim's wording: the persisted `PatternVerdict` (alert_types.rs:146-151) carries only `template_id` and `match_confidence`, not the Warning severity or the "log manipulation" description, and engine.rs:169-186's `pattern_requires_observer` arbitration already stops pattern-only matches from becoming direct_unsafe. However, the spurious `detection_evasion` id still persists in `engine.pattern_verdicts` (engine.rs:39-48, alert_builder.rs:440-450) and a match's confidence is hard-coded to 1.0 (pattern_matcher.rs:191), feeding the D2/pattern subscore (scoring.rs:247-251). The defect is therefore genuine at the stated location; only the severity phrasing is slightly overstated, which does not warrant refutation.

confirmed.title: Graph traversal/merge APIs have no production caller and the mutators corrupt indexes
confirmed.evidence: `bfs_from` (graph.rs:365), `walk_backward` (416), `connected_agents` (460), `merge_nodes` (235), `update_node` (125), `nodes_for_agent` (516) and `edges_for_agent` (524) have no caller outside graph.rs's own tests (`edges_for_agent` has none at all), and `diff_snapshot` (snapshot.rs:101) is only used by its test. `update_node` replaces the node without updating `agent_nodes`/`nodes_by_type` (graph.rs:125-129), and `merge_nodes` rewrites edge endpoints without updating `agent_edges` (graph.rs:237-263). `walk_backward` also contains an empty conditional block (graph.rs:448-451) and never returns the root node its doc comment promises.
confirmed.impact: A large, unaudited API surface can be called by future code and silently corrupt indexes; the dead traversal is also the kind of code that makes the graph module look more capable than the production path uses.
confirmed.fix: Delete the unused traversal/merge/snapshot APIs (or wire them into a real consumer), and if update_node/merge_nodes are retained, rebuild the affected indexes inside them.

verification.reason: I re-read /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/graph/graph.rs and the sibling modules and could not refute the claim. The definitions exist exactly where cited (bfs_from:365, walk_backward:416, connected_agents:460, merge_nodes:235, update_node:125, nodes_for_agent:516, edges_for_agent:524), and a repo-wide grep (excluding target/.git) finds only in-file test references for bfs_from (915), walk_backward (933), connected_agents (966), merge_nodes (994) and nodes_for_agent (860), all inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` starting at 803-804; update_node and edges_for_agent have zero references anywhere, not even tests. diff_snapshot (snapshot.rs:101) appears only in the mod.rs:27 re-export and its own test at snapshot.rs:186, and no production consumer (claims/text.rs, claims/traceback.rs, claims/claim_builder.rs, claims/alert_builder.rs, classification/engine.rs, replay/executor.rs) calls any of them. The index-corruption half also holds: update_node's body (125-129) is just `self.nodes.insert(node_id, node)`, leaving agent_nodes (field 39), nodes_by_type (46) and node_order (51) stale, in contrast to add_node (99-105) and reassign_agent (137-155) which maintain them; merge_nodes (235-263) rewrites edge.source/edge.target and the outgoing/incoming maps but never touches agent_edges, and the trailing remove_node at 264 cannot clean it up because the outgoing/incoming entries for `remove` were already taken at 237/248, so remove_node (157-207) sees no incident edges and its agent_edges cleanup at 169-177 never runs. Finally, walk_backward's only-if block at 448-451 contains just a comment, and since path.push((current.clone(), edge_id)) at 439 runs before advancing to prev_node, the root node is never returned despite the doc at 412-414 promising "root cause last." The claim is factually accurate; severity low is apt because the whole traversal/merge surface is unreachable from production code, so no live corruption occurs today.

confirmed.title: Capability envelope compares numeric IPs against hostnames parsed from the prompt
confirmed.evidence: handle() runs envelope.check_network(host) on the action resource (graph_builder.rs:471-481). For NETWORK_CONNECT/SEND the host is the producer's net_op.host, formatted as a numeric address (bpftools/process/process_json.h:123-134; routing.rs:826-846). CapabilityEnvelope::network_hosts comes only from dotted tokens in the user prompt (envelope.rs:142-167), and graph_builder fabricates host "unknown" when no URL argument parses (graph_builder.rs:1601-1616).
confirmed.impact: Any egress from a non-curl client (python/node/go clients issue plain connect()) is reported as CapabilityExpansion network:<ip> even when the user named that host, and the resulting PolicyBoundaryCrossing feeds claim_builder (claim_builder.rs:154) and the boundary score (classification/scoring.rs:258-273). This is a systematic false positive that inflates claims/alerts on benign runs, exactly the risk the design flags as unmeasured (docs/design/mechanism-upgrade-2026-10-21.md:211).
confirmed.fix: Match on a name, not an address: use TLS SNI / HTTP Host when available, keep an observed DNS/IP-to-host map, and skip the check (or record an explicit unknown) when only an IP literal exists; never emit an expansion for the fabricated "unknown" host.
