verification.reason: Code evidence matches the claim end to end. graph_builder.rs:471-481 passes NormalizedResource::Network{host} straight to envelope.check_network(host), and an Expansion there creates a real PolicyBoundary node plus PolicyBoundaryCrossing edge (529 upsert_provisional_pbc). envelope.rs:106-118 allows only empty/loopback (is_loopback 138-140: localhost, ::1, [::1], 127.*) or exact/suffix matches against network_hosts; there is no IP-literal branch and no DNS/SNI resolution in the module. network_hosts is built by extract_hosts (envelope.rs:142-165), which keeps only dotted alphanumeric tokens from the prompt, i.e. hostnames. The observed host is numeric: process_json.h:120-135 formats the sockaddr bytes via net_format_ipv4/ipv6 into net_op.host, routing.rs:826-846 emits "ip:port", args.rs:242-248/404-418 parse_addr it into NormalizedArg::Url{host: <ip>}, and graph_builder.rs:1601-1612 builds Network{host: <ip>}. graph_builder.rs:1613-1617 additionally fabricates host "unknown" when no Url arg exists, which check_network also reports as Expansion (network:unknown). Envelopes are live in production (runtime.rs:817-825 derives from UserPrompt and installs them via set_envelopes), not test-only. Downstream the edge is consumed by claims/claim_builder.rs:152-159 (all unclaimed PolicyBoundaryCrossing edges become claims) and classification/scoring.rs:258-274 (sub_score_boundary counts PBC edges), and the design doc itself flags the unmeasured false-positive risk at mechanism-upgrade-2026-10-21.md:211-213. One scope nuance, which strengthens rather than refutes: the false positive is not confined to non-curl clients, since curl also emits a separate connect syscall action (routing.rs:826, action_classifier.rs:94) whose Url host is the IP address, and the envelope block does not dedup it against the host-named ProcessExec path at graph_builder.rs:1632-1645. No path was found that special-cases IP literals or skips the fabricated "unknown" host.

confirmed.title: Provenance spans are registered with the wrong ProcessId key, losing agent attribution
confirmed.evidence: runtime.rs:421-429 builds ProcessId::new(event.pid, data["start_time_ns"].unwrap_or(0)) and calls agent_for_process. HTTPEvent and SSEProcessorEvent carry no start_time_ns field (framework/analyzers/event.rs:86-104, 10-26), and routing.rs:640-643 documents that HTTP-layer events have start_time_ns=0. The resolver is keyed by the resolved real start time (routing.rs:219-223; resolver.rs:267-271), so this lookup misses.
confirmed.impact: Spans from LLM request bodies are stored with agent_id = None. SpanStore::match_untrusted only enforces cross-agent isolation when both span and query agents are Some (span_store.rs:133-138), so untrusted content read by one agent can taint another agent's tool calls. That breaks the module's stated guarantee that content from one session/agent must never taint another (span_store.rs:8-10, 132-133).
confirmed.fix: Resolve the pid with routing::resolve_process_id(pid, &snapshot) before the resolver lookup, exactly as dispatch_event does, and assert the resolved value is used consistently for span insertion and matching.

verification.reason: The claim survives refutation. runtime.rs:421-429 builds `ProcessId::new(event.pid, event.data.get("start_time_ns").and_then(as_u64).unwrap_or(0))` and immediately calls `self.identity_resolver.agent_for_process(pid)`. HTTPEvent (collector/src/framework/analyzers/event.rs:86-104) contains no `start_time_ns` field, and its `to_event` (:149-160) serializes only the struct fields into `data` with source "http_parser"; SSEProcessorEvent (:10-26, :64-82) carries `start_time`, not `start_time_ns`. Raw SSL events likewise never inject the key (grep for `"start_time_ns"` in collector/src shows only process/syscall event construction and the routing/runtime readers). So the lookup key is always `ProcessId(pid, 0)`. The resolver is an exact HashMap keyed by the full ProcessId with both fields hashed/compared (ids.rs:9-12; resolver.rs:267-271), while entries are inserted only via routing.rs:223 with the *resolved* ProcessId from `resolve_process_id` (routing.rs:644-660), which returns the real start time from the snapshot for any pid present in `snapshot.processes`. The very comment at routing.rs:640-643 states "Events from HTTP layers have start_time_ns=0", confirming the intended resolution step was simply omitted at runtime.rs:421-429. There is no compensating path: `observe_request` stores the `None` agent into the span (provenance_tracker.rs:90-97) and nothing ever repairs it, while `annotate_intent` passes the resolved intent's agent (runtime.rs:476; intent.process_id resolved at routing.rs:280) to `match_untrusted`, whose isolation guard only fires when *both* span and query agents are `Some` (span_store.rs:132-138) — so the None span is matchable by every agent, defeating the file's own stated guarantee at span_store.rs:8-10. The live repo at /home/lzk/MtAgentLens/collector/src/responsibility/runtime/runtime.rs:421-429 contains the identical code, so this is not a snapshot artifact; the only test covering this path (runtime.rs ~2405-2443) uses pid 42 with no EXEC/TLS signal, so the resolver has no assignment and both sides are None, which masks exactly this failure. The stated impact and fix (route through `routing::resolve_process_id` with `self.signal_graph.snapshot()` before the resolver lookup, and use the resolved pid for both span insertion and the conversation observation at runtime.rs:442-443) are accurate.

confirmed.title: TLS-sharing identity signal is unreachable in both Phase 1 and Phase 2
confirmed.evidence: SignalGraph::tls_to_process is a HashMap<TlsSessionId, ProcessId> with last-writer-wins overwrite (signal_graph.rs:331-344), and tls_sessions_for_process filters that same map (signal_snapshot.rs:326-333). Therefore tls_to_seeds (union_find.rs:328-345) can hold at most one seed index per session, making the S2 merge at union_find.rs:338-345 unreachable. In Phase 1 the 'shared with a known agent' loop resolves process_for_tls to the process itself (resolver.rs:101-118), and the confidence-upgrade branch at resolver.rs:126-140 is dead because line 106 already returned.
confirmed.impact: The documented strongest merge signal (union_find.rs:7) never merges anything. A child process using an inherited TLS connection overwrites the parent's binding (signal_graph.rs:338-344); the parent then loses its seed and, absent a conversation id, can be reported unresolved. Meanwhile a process that shares nothing is labelled TlsSessionShared with confidence 0.70, so Phase-2 components are split and labelled for the wrong reasons.
confirmed.fix: Keep an append-only (session, process) relation (or TLS -> set of processes) separate from the current-owner map, union seeds whose session has multiple owners, and make is_subagent_boundary consult that relation.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what is claimed. `SignalSnapshot.tls_to_process` is `HashMap<TlsSessionId, ProcessId>` (signal_snapshot.rs:127), `tls_sessions_for_process` merely inverts that map by filtering `pid == process_id` (signal_snapshot.rs:326-332), and `process_for_tls` is a single lookup (signal_snapshot.rs:335-337). `SignalGraph::observe_tls` records a collision into `tls_collisions` but then unconditionally overwrites the binding (`self.tls_to_process.insert(...)`, signal_graph.rs:331-344), and `snapshot()` clones only the overwritten map (signal_graph.rs:468) — `tls_collisions` never enters the snapshot (grep finds it only at signal_graph.rs:74/95/336). Consequently, `process_tls` built at union_find.rs:298-309 is a strict inverse of a single-valued map, so each key inserted into `tls_to_seeds` at union_find.rs:328-335 has exactly one seed index; `if indices.len() >= 2` at union_find.rs:338-345 is structurally unreachable, and the "already merged by S2" comment at union_find.rs:10/485-486 is false. The Phase-1 half is equally verifiable: `resolve_provisional` derives `tls_sessions` from the same map (resolver.rs:83), so for every session in that list `process_for_tls(tls)` returns `process_id` itself (resolver.rs:104), meaning the "shared with a known agent" loop can only ever look up the process's own provisional entry; if that entry exists it returns early at resolver.rs:106-116 with `primary_signal: TlsSessionShared` and confidence 0.70 even though nothing is shared (resolver.rs:108-113), and if it does not exist the fallback at resolver.rs:126-140 also finds nothing — so the confidence-upgrade branch is dead. The impact is also grounded: overwriting the parent's binding removes the parent from `seed_processes` (union_find.rs:294-309) while S1 downward propagation only walks seeds' children (union_find.rs:406-439) and upward propagation only climbs to assigned ancestors (union_find.rs:542-578), so a collided parent without a conversation id can only land in `unresolved` (union_find.rs:580-592). The repo's own tests concede the model limitation at union_find.rs:777-780 and 1191-1195 ("The data model maps TLS session → single process (last-writer-wins)... cannot be detected via tls_to_process alone"). I found no alternate multi-owner path or collision-aware reconstruction in `run_authoritative_resolution*`, and the only other caller (replay/executor.rs:153) and runtime.rs:1646 use the same function, so the defect stands.

confirmed.title: Capability envelope write check has no workspace notion and is defeated by relative paths
confirmed.evidence: write_prefixes starts as ["/tmp/"] plus $HOME/ plus only those prompt tokens that end in '/' or contain '.' (envelope.rs:52-59), while the field comment claims 'workspace + /tmp by default' (envelope.rs:32). Paths reaching check_write are only slash-collapsed, never absolutized (evidence/args.rs:290-317), and the BPF producer emits the raw user filename (bpftools/process/process.bpf.c:292-324). The envelope is also frozen at the first UserPrompt per agent (runtime.rs:803-805), so a later user turn cannot authorize a new host or path.
confirmed.impact: Benign work in a workspace outside $HOME (e.g. /workspace, /data, /repo) and any relative-path write (shell redirection `> out.txt`) become write:<path> expansions that add PolicyBoundaryCrossing evidence and raise the boundary score of clean runs. Conversely the blanket $HOME/ grant makes writes to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or ~/.aws/* Allowed, so the same check is simultaneously noisy and blind.
confirmed.fix: Derive the workspace root from the agent's cwd (/proc/<pid>/cwd) or the user-named project path, absolutize event paths against it, and replace the blanket $HOME/ grant with workspace-scoped prefixes. Re-derive or extend the envelope on user turns that explicitly grant a capability.

verification.reason: The claim is accurate on all load-bearing points. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/provenance/envelope.rs, the doc comment at line 32 promises "workspace + /tmp by default", but derive_from_task at lines 52-59 seeds write_prefixes with only "/tmp/", $HOME/ (lines 53-54), and prompt tokens that end in '/' or contain '.' (lines 56-59); check_write (lines 123-134) is a plain starts_with over those prefixes with no absolutization or workspace root. The path supplied to it is genuinely unresolved: graph_builder.rs:424 builds the resource via action_to_resource, and lines 1556-1599 take the first NormalizedArg::Path verbatim into canonical_path (the field name is misleading); that Path is produced by normalize_action_path/normalize_intent_path in evidence/args.rs:287-317, which only strip a leading "./", collapse slashes, and trim trailing '/', never joining cwd or a workspace. Syscall input is raw: routing.rs:773-808 forwards the event's filepath string directly, and bpftools/process/process.bpf.c:288-324 copies the user-supplied filename with bpf_probe_read_user_str, so a relative openat/write such as `> out.txt` reaches check_write as "out.txt" and yields Expansion (confirmed reachable at graph_builder.rs:478-499, where expansions create a PolicyBoundary node and a PolicyBoundaryCrossing edge at confidence 0.70, which counts toward the boundary/PBC gate in classification/scoring.rs:99-115). The freeze is also real: runtime.rs:786-828 iterates UserPrompt intents and skips any agent already in self.envelopes (line 803), and the map is only inserted into, never mutated, so a later user turn cannot widen hosts/paths. No other code adds a workspace prefix or resolves paths for this check (the unrelated is_workspace_path at graph_builder.rs:1538 uses only narrow infra/build prefixes). The $HOME blanket does make writes under ~/.ssh or ~/.aws Allowed at this check, while unrelated relative writes become expansions, matching the impact stated.

confirmed.title: Provenance spans and tags are never persisted, so replay and traceback cannot reconstruct the chain
confirmed.evidence: The schema creates 27 tables (schema.rs:154-514) with no provenance_spans table, although the design specifies it (docs/design/mechanism-upgrade-2026-10-21.md:102). PersistRecord has no provenance variant (writer.rs:79-137), and Intent has no provenance fields (types/evidence_types.rs:11-22). The span source is only printed into a diagnostic string (graph_builder.rs:962-992) while the boundary node stores just the span hash as call_id (graph_builder.rs:965-968), so traceback's provenance root is an opaque id (claims/traceback.rs:94-111).
confirmed.impact: SpanStore's text_sha256 and excerpt (span_store.rs:31-36) have no reader anywhere, and the offline replay executor never calls set_intent_provenance, so a replayed run rebuilds a graph with zero UntrustedInstructionFlow boundaries. The persisted database cannot answer 'which file or host did this command come from', so the traceback source chain promised in the design stops at a hash.
confirmed.fix: Add the promised provenance_spans table plus a PersistRecord variant, persist each span's tag, source, excerpt and hash, add provenance fields to Intent, and have replay/traceback join through them.

verification.reason: The claim holds on the cited code. schema.rs:154-514 contains exactly 27 `CREATE TABLE` statements (process_events through schema_version) and none is `provenance_spans`; `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 3 (schema.rs:23) and MIGRATIONS (schema.rs:725+) ends at v3, while the design doc at docs/design/mechanism-upgrade-2026-10-21.md:94-96 and :102 explicitly requires `Intent.provenance`/`provenance_span_id` and a Schema v4 `provenance_spans` table. `Intent` (responsibility/types/evidence_types.rs:11-22) has no provenance fields, `PersistRecord` (persistence/writer.rs:78-137) has no span variant, and the Intent insert/read (writer.rs:621-644; reader.rs:523-547) covers only the 11 v1 columns plus `tool_args_json`, so a span's tag/source/hash/excerpt cannot round-trip. `set_intent_provenance` is called only from runtime.rs:481 and graph_builder tests (2661, 2750); ReplayExecutor (replay/executor.rs:160-201) builds `GraphBuilder::with_default_config()` and feeds DB-loaded intents through `handle()` with no provenance, so a replayed graph acquires no `UntrustedInstructionFlow` boundary. The boundary node at graph_builder.rs:964-968 stores only `span_id` as `call_id` (span ids are `span-<12 hex>` hashes, span_store.rs:96), and traceback.rs:94-111 reads that `call_id` into `provenance_root` but only uses it as a presence boolean at 108-110, never resolving source or tag. `text_sha256`/`excerpt` (span_store.rs:34-36, 95-105) have no reader outside span_store/provenance_mod; ProvenanceTracker exposes only `match_for`/`span_count`/`matched_intent_count`. The live path does eprintln the source at runtime.rs:486-489 and graph_builder.rs:987 pushes it into `delta.diagnostics`, but runtime.rs:837-914 consumes only `new_nodes`/`new_edges`, so it is never persisted. Secondary citations omit subdirectories (`responsibility/graph/`, `responsibility/types/`, `provenance/`), but the referenced line content matches the actual files, so this is a citation nit, not a refutation; severity stays high because replay and traceback fidelity for the core provenance mechanism are lost.

confirmed.title: Span retention keeps the oldest 64 tool results per request and stores duplicates
confirmed.evidence: parse_request_provenance returns tool results in chronological message order and observe_request applies .take(MAX_SPANS_PER_REQUEST) with MAX_SPANS_PER_REQUEST = 64 (provenance_tracker.rs:22, 76-79). Every request repeats the whole conversation, and SpanStore::add never deduplicates by span_id or text_sha256 (span_store.rs:85-114), pushing into a 512-entry FIFO (span_store.rs:56-60, 109-112).
confirmed.impact: In a conversation with more than 64 tool results the newest (actionable) results are never stored; on the next turn the first 64 are re-added as duplicates that evict older distinct spans, so an early injection disappears long before the run ends. The provenance_spans diagnostic (runtime.rs:2029) counts these copies rather than distinct spans, so the reported measurement is wrong.
confirmed.fix: Keep the newest results (reverse scan or windowed take), deduplicate by span hash per run before insert, and report the distinct-span count.

verification.reason: I re-read the snapshot and every element of the claim matches the code. In provenance_tracker.rs:22 MAX_SPANS_PER_REQUEST is 64, and observe_request's loop over `provenance.tool_results.into_iter().take(MAX_SPANS_PER_REQUEST)` (lines 76-79) consumes the Vec from the front. parse_request_provenance builds that Vec in chronological message order: the pass-2 loop at line 281 walks `messages` as parsed and pushes each result at lines ~300-313, so .take(64) retains the OLDEST 64 tool results of each request, not the newest. The default SpanStore (span_store.rs:57-60, 512 entries) has no membership check in add() (span_store.rs:85-114): it computes span_id/text_sha256 at 96-98, then unconditionally push_back/pop_front at 109-112, so identical results re-parsed from every repeated request body are stored again and evict the FIFO tail. runtime.rs:2029 reports `self.provenance.span_count()`, and span_count() (provenance_tracker.rs, backed by SpanStore::len at span_store.rs:71-73) is the raw deque length, so duplicates inflate the diagnostic. I found no countervailing path: observe_span exists (provenance_tracker.rs:105) but has no production caller, the store is cleared only per run (runtime.rs:363-365), and routing::llm_request_body/strip_http_headers (routing.rs:666-698) pass the whole request body through unmodified. The one imprecision is the impact wording "the newest results are never stored" — strictly, results whose chronological index exceeds 64 are never stored, which is the same thing for the normal append-only conversation; and "an early injection disappears" holds only if the agent compacts/truncates history (otherwise the repeated first 64 keep being re-added). The core functional defect (silent drop of tool results 65+, duplicate inflation of a 512-slot FIFO, and a copy-counting diagnostic) is real and unrefuted, so severity medium stands.

confirmed.title: The message signal is never fed on the live path, so identity has only two signals
confirmed.evidence: When intents are extracted, routing only constructs PendingMessageBinding records for persistence (routing.rs:314-326), and the runtime only writes them (runtime.rs:462-471). SignalGraph::observe_message_via_tls and observe_message_direct are called only by the offline replay executor (replay/executor.rs:530-532).
confirmed.impact: In live runs SignalSnapshot::messages_for_process is always empty, so AuthoritativeIdentity.message_ids is always [] (union_find.rs:607-622) in agent_identities (writer.rs:906-912) and in the frontend lineage (frontend/lib/db-import.ts:659-667). Unresolved diagnostics also mislabel message-carrying processes as NoPositiveSignal (union_find.rs:580-592), contradicting the 'three-signal identity complete' claim (docs/design/mechanism-upgrade-2026-10-21.md:207).
confirmed.fix: Call signal_graph.observe_message_via_tls / observe_message_direct where the binding is produced (routing already has &mut SignalGraph), with persistence kept as the secondary sink.

verification.reason: The core claim holds. routing.rs:314-326 constructs a PendingMessageBinding only into `DispatchResult.message_bindings` (and only when a TLS session exists), and runtime.rs:462-471 does nothing with it but `persistence.write(PersistRecord::MessageBinding{...})`. A repo-wide grep shows `SignalGraph::observe_message_via_tls` / `observe_message_direct` (defined signal_graph.rs:365,385) are called on a non-test path only in replay/executor.rs:530-532; the remaining hits (signal_graph.rs:717,729,758,966) are unit tests. Live finalization uses `self.signal_graph.snapshot()` directly (runtime.rs:1634-1635), and the frozen snapshot's `messages_for_process` (signal_snapshot.rs:345-360) reads `tls_to_messages`/`direct_process_messages`, which are mutated only inside those two observer methods (signal_graph.rs:367,386) and nowhere else live. Consequently union_find.rs:605-622 can only ever collect an empty `message_ids`, which writer.rs:906-914 persists as `[]` and db-import.ts:659-667 parses as empty in the frontend for live runs, and the direct (`tls_session_id: None`) branch of the binding is never produced either. Two qualifications lower severity: (1) the union-find "three signals" are lineage propagation, TLS sharing, and conversation-id merging (union_find.rs:268-277, 311-370) — messages are carried metadata, not a merge signal, and observe_conversation *is* fed live at runtime.rs:442-443, so the docs line 207 "three-signal identity complete" claim (which cites S3 conversation merging) is not actually contradicted; (2) the diagnostics claim in union_find.rs:580-592 is unreachable on the live path because a binding is created only when the process already has a TLS session, so any would-be message carrier also satisfies `has_tls`, and on the replay path messages are actually fed. I found no consumer of `message_ids` beyond parsing into the AgentIdentity type in the frontend, so this is an empty-metadata/telemetry-backfill defect rather than a wrong-identity defect.

confirmed.title: Signal eviction leaves TLS, conversation and thread bindings pointing at removed processes
confirmed.evidence: evict_expired removes entries from processes, parent_map, child_map and direct_process_messages only (signal_graph.rs:434-448). tls_to_process, tls_to_messages, conversation_to_processes, process_to_conversations and thread_to_process are untouched yet are cloned into every snapshot (signal_graph.rs:463-475).
confirmed.impact: Phase-2 seeds are taken directly from snapshot.tls_to_process and conversation_to_processes (union_find.rs:298-321), so exited processes remain seeds and appear as AuthoritativeIdentity.process_ids. A restarted agent under the same pid keeps its old ProcessId in the conversation list and gets merged with the new incarnation, and these maps grow unbounded for the session lifetime.
confirmed.fix: When evicting a ProcessId, purge it from every reverse index (TLS owner and messages, conversation maps, thread map) and drop empty conversation entries.

verification.reason: The claim is accurate on re-read. signal_graph.rs:434-448 (eviction loop) removes a ProcessId only from child_map, processes, parent_map and direct_process_messages; tls_to_process (inserted unconditionally at :344), tls_to_messages (:366-369), conversation_to_processes/process_to_conversations (:319-330) and thread_to_process are never purged anywhere in the file (grep shows only inserts plus test writes), and snapshot (:463-475) clones all of them into SignalSnapshot. The same omission exists in the capacity-eviction path drop_one_process (:544-586). evict_expired runs immediately before the frozen Phase-2 snapshot (runtime.rs:1634-1635) and on process-capacity overflow (signal_graph.rs:208-213), so evicted PIDs remain in the identity indices. In union_find.rs, Step 1 seeds are built directly from snapshot.tls_to_process (:298-311) and snapshot.conversation_to_processes (:315-321) with no membership check against snapshot.processes, and those seeds become component members (:386-411) and then AuthoritativeIdentity.process_ids: comp.clone() (:644); runtime.rs:1657-1677 persists IdentityMapping rows for those PIDs. The same-conversation S3 merge (:349-365) does union the old and new ProcessId (ProcessId includes start_time_ns, ids.rs:9-12) whenever an agent restarts into the same conversation, so the pre-restart, possibly evicted id is carried into the new incarnation's authoritative identity, and none of these maps are ever shrunk during the session (tls_to_messages/thread_to_process in particular grow without bound). Nothing elsewhere filters dead or evicted PIDs out of the reverse indices, so the defect stands; severity medium is appropriate because the effect is stale/phantom identity membership and unbounded index growth rather than a crash.

confirmed.title: Subagent boundary records carry agent IDs derived before components are final
confirmed.evidence: During downward propagation, parent_agent_id and child_agent_id are computed inline with derive_agent_id(&components[parent_comp]) (union_find.rs:425-426, 455-456, 512-513) while the same component keeps receiving siblings and descendants in the same worklist loop (union_find.rs:473-479). Final IDs are derived only after propagation completes (union_find.rs:603), and derive_agent_id hashes the full process list (union_find.rs:254-264).
confirmed.impact: Any subagent boundary persisted to subagent_boundaries (runtime.rs:1685-1690) can name a parent or child agent ID that does not exist in agent_identities. The delegation tree the frontend builds from these rows (frontend/lib/identity-lineage.ts:133) therefore shows phantom or orphaned nodes, with boundaries recorded early in the traversal most likely to be wrong.
confirmed.fix: Record boundaries by ProcessId and resolve parent_agent/child_agent in a final pass over the completed assignments-to-component-to-AgentId map.

verification.reason: The claim is accurate. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/identity/union_find.rs, derive_agent_id (lines 254-264) hashes the entire sorted ProcessId set of a component, so any later addition changes the ID. SubagentBoundary rows are stamped with derive_agent_id(&components[parent_comp]) / derive_agent_id(&components[child_comp]) at lines 425-426, 455-456 and 512-513, i.e. mid-traversal, while the very same components keep growing: lines 478-480 append every TLS-less child to parent_comp, line 470/486 pushes children onto the worklist so their TLS-less descendants later append to child_comp, and the Step-4 upward pass (lines 560-565) appends unassigned processes to an assigned ancestor's component. The authoritative AgentIds are derived only after all propagation at line 603, and the boundaries are returned unmodified at line 672 — there is no remap/finalization pass. runtime/runtime.rs:1685-1690 persists those boundary structs verbatim via PersistRecord::SubagentBoundary, and the writer (persistence/writer.rs:1021-1033) stores parent_agent/child_agent unchanged; the schema (persistence/schema.rs:387-396) has no FK, so the inconsistency is silent. The frontend then builds the delegation tree directly from b.parent_agent_id / b.child_agent_id (frontend/lib/identity-lineage.ts:133-140), so phantom or orphaned nodes result. I checked for a possible refutation path: graph_builder::remap_agent_identities (graph_builder.rs:238-264) only maps provisional→final IDs on graph nodes, never boundaries; and the existing boundary test (union_find.rs:1174-1186) asserts only process membership, not that boundary.child_agent equals the final derived child agent ID, so the defect is untested. Boundaries are most likely wrong whenever the component still gains a TLS-less sibling/tool child or an upward-assigned process after the row is recorded. Severity medium is appropriate (silent data corruption in a diagnostic/tree view, not a crash or security issue).

confirmed.title: account_uuid is used as a conversation identity signal
confirmed.evidence: parse_conversation_id falls back through ["session_id", "conversation_id", "account_uuid"] inside metadata.user_id (provenance_tracker.rs:368-377), and run_authoritative_resolution_with_delegations unions every process that carried the same conversation id (union_find.rs:357-369).
confirmed.impact: When a client or provider omits session_id, the constant account UUID becomes the S3 merge key: every agent process for that account, including separately delegated subagents, is unioned into one authoritative agent. This silently collapses multi-agent structure and defeats the delegated_children split (union_find.rs:444-471).
confirmed.fix: Use only per-session identifiers for the conversation signal and drop the account_uuid fallback (or reject ids that repeat across distinct sessions).

verification.reason: Code evidence matches the claim exactly. provenance_tracker.rs:371 lists "account_uuid" as the last fallback inside metadata.user_id (parsed at 368-369), guarded only by len()>=8 at 372 with no per-session validation. runtime.rs:439-443 calls parse_conversation_id on every captured request body in the production handler and feeds observe_conversation; signal_graph.rs:314-329 records the process under that id in conversation_to_processes; union_find.rs:315-322 seeds every process carrying a conversation id and 357-369 unions all seeds sharing one id with no cross-session or group-size filter. The delegation defeat is also real: components/assignments are fixed from the union-find before Step 3, and the loop short-circuits at union_find.rs:413-436 on assignments.contains_key(child), so the delegated_children branch at 444 never executes for an S3-merged child (it only gets an IndependentTls diagnostic at 416-434 while staying in the parent component); Steps 4-5 (536-640) never re-split. The only counter-detail found is that the anonymized Claude Code wire fixture carries account_uuid as an empty string (which would fail len>=8), and no test covers the fallback — but that does not refute the latent defect, which fires whenever session_id/conversation_id is absent and a real 36-char account UUID is present.

confirmed.title: MTAGENTLENS_PROVENANCE_STRICT is documented as the strict-policy ablation switch but is not wired
confirmed.evidence: The design requires MTAGENTLENS_PROVENANCE_STRICT=1 for the strict CaMeL/Fides policy in the paper's two-policy ablation (docs/design/mechanism-upgrade-2026-10-21.md:216-226; docs/superpowers/HANDOFF-2026-10-21.md:144). The string appears nowhere in collector/. The policy is instead fixed at tag-construction time: retrievals the user named get ProvenanceTag::retrieved_user_named (provenance_tracker.rs:85-89), which is_untrusted_unrequested always excludes (labels.rs:146-148).
confirmed.impact: The strict-policy precision/recall and benign-review-rate numbers the paper must report cannot be produced. The default user-named policy also cannot catch Type-B injections inside a file the user asked to read, and there is no switch to measure that difference.
confirmed.fix: Read the env var once at startup (same pattern as configure_agent_comms_from_env) and, in strict mode, tag every retrieved span Unrequested regardless of whether the user named its source.

verification.reason: The claim survives every refutation attempt. A repo-wide grep for MTAGENTLENS_PROVENANCE_STRICT in /tmp/mtal-audit returns exactly two hits, both documentation: docs/design/mechanism-upgrade-2026-10-21.md:225 ("建议实现 `MTAGENTLENS_PROVENANCE_STRICT=1` 作为消融开关（当前未接线，列入 P6）") and docs/superpowers/HANDOFF-2026-10-21.md:144 ("strict provenance 口径未接线（`MTAGENTLENS_PROVENANCE_STRICT` 设计）"); the string appears nowhere in collector/ (verified by grep across collector/src and repeated grep for "strict" in provenance/*.rs, which found no config struct or alternative path), so no hidden wiring exists. The design text at lines 216-226 does mandate that the paper report both policies ("论文必须报告两种口径的 precision/recall 与良性 review 率"), and the policy is indeed fixed at tag-construction time: provenance_tracker.rs:85-89 chooses retrieved_user_named vs retrieved_untrusted purely from the boolean `user_named`, which is derived at provenance_tracker.rs:292-298 and 308-313 from whether the tool input was named in trusted user text; labels.rs:47-53 defines Authorization::Unrequested and labels.rs:91-104 makes retrieved_user_named set integrity=Untrusted with authorization=UserNamed; labels.rs:146-148 then makes is_untrusted_unrequested require Unrequested, so both gates that create the boundary — span_store.rs:130 in match_untrusted and graph_builder.rs:963 in the UntrustedInstructionFlow branch — skip user-named spans entirely. The impact assessment is accurate: the strict policy cannot be measured without a code change, and Type-B payloads inside a user-named file are structurally excluded from the provenance signal. The only mitigating nuance is that the doc honestly labels the switch as unimplemented (P6) rather than falsely claiming it works, which makes this a known capability gap rather than a misleading doc, but it is still a real gap that blocks a paper-required ablation, so medium severity stands.

confirmed.title: Provenance machinery that is computed but never consumed
confirmed.evidence: CapabilityEnvelope.tools (envelope.rs:30, 44) is never consulted by check_shell/check_network/check_write (envelope.rs:98-135); the only other use is attenuate, which has no production caller (only the test at envelope.rs:256). ProvenanceTag confidentiality is hardcoded Public for every span (retrieved_untrusted(false) at provenance_tracker.rs:85-89), and derived_from/is_secret/authored_secret are used only in labels.rs tests (labels.rs:68, 111, 150). ContentSpan.text_sha256 and excerpt (span_store.rs:31-36) and SpanMatch.matched_line (span_store.rs:46) have no readers.
confirmed.impact: A tool the task never requested is never reported as an expansion, child envelopes are never attenuated to the parent's, and secret-bearing retrieved content is never labelled Secret or propagated. The Observer and the paper therefore get less than the design claims, and inert fields (excerpt, sha256, matched_line) make the module appear more complete than it is.
confirmed.fix: Either consume these in the decision path (tool-name check in graph_builder, attenuate for delegated children, confidentiality derived from the source path) or remove them so the implemented mechanism matches the documented one.

verification.reason: The specific inert-field assertions check out against the snapshot, though the claim's headline and one impact sentence are overstated. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/provenance/envelope.rs, the `tools` field is declared at line 30 and populated at line 44, but check_shell (98-104) reads only `shell_authorized`, check_network (106-121) only `network_hosts`, and check_write (123-135) only `write_prefixes`; the only reader of `tools` is attenuate (72-96), whose sole caller in the entire snapshot is the test at line 256 (repo-wide grep for `attenuate|derive_from_task|envelopes.insert` finds no production attenuation path). The claim is nevertheless overstated in calling the whole module unconsumed: envelopes are built in production at runtime/runtime.rs:820-828 and consumed by graph_builder.rs:468-527 (calls at 478, 493 and 511), which mints a `CapabilityExpansion` PolicyBoundary, so network/write/shell expansions ARE reported; only tool-name-based expansion (the `tools` set) is inert, not "a tool the task never requested is never reported as an expansion" in general. The provenance_tracker evidence is also correct but cited at the wrong path — the file is collector/src/responsibility/runtime/provenance_tracker.rs (not provenance/), where lines 85-89 hardcode `retrieved_untrusted(false)` / `retrieved_user_named(false)`, so every request-derived span is Public; `observe_span` (105-120) can accept a secret tag but has zero call sites. `derived_from` is used only in labels.rs tests (169, 180, 188) and graph_builder.rs:2659, which sits inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` starting at 1715; `authored_secret` (labels.rs:68) and `is_secret` (150) have no production callers. Finally, span_store.rs:34 (`text_sha256`), 36 (`excerpt`) and 46 (`matched_line`) have no readers anywhere in the snapshot — runtime.rs:484-491 consumes only `span_id` and `source` from SpanMatch. Dead fields alone are low severity, so no severity change is warranted; the fix should either wire the `tools`/attenuation/confidentiality dimensions into the decision path or delete them.

confirmed.title: Observer failures are written to the L1 cache and replayed as verdicts
confirmed.evidence: engine.rs:341-356 returns route "observer_failed" together with Route::DirectSafe(heuristic_decide(score)); heuristic_decide sets cache_ttl: CacheTTL::Once (scoring.rs:218). runtime.rs:1304 gates the cache write only on `classification_result.route.starts_with("observer")`, and runtime.rs:1308-1329 stores whatever output the Route carries with a hardcoded CacheTTL::Task. cache.rs:69-71 ignores the TTL. On the next trigger with the same key runtime.rs:1203-1215 builds a CachedObserver (cache.rs:29-37) that returns the failure output as Ok, so the engine never sees an error and never retries.
confirmed.impact: A single timeout/429/parse error becomes a durable 'semantic verdict' for the rest of the session. observer_failures is not incremented on replay (runtime.rs:1365-1372 only matches the literal 'observer_failed'), final_decision reports ObserverUncertain instead of a failed call, and no fail-closed path remains. This is silent decision substitution, not caching.
confirmed.fix: Store only genuinely successful observer calls (carry an explicit outcome/success flag); never insert heuristic or fallback outputs into the cache. Mark replays as cached in provenance and never count a failure as an observer judgement.

verification.reason: The mechanism is exactly as claimed. engine.rs:314-357 handles Err(e) by building `fallback = heuristic_decide(score)` (scoring.rs:198-226, whose cache_ttl is CacheTTL::Once at line 218), downgrading it to ObserverDecision::Uncertain unless an unsafe rule is present (engine.rs:334-340), returning a ClassificationResult with route "observer_failed" (engine.rs:343) and returning `Route::DirectSafe(fallback)` / `Route::DirectUnsafe(fallback)` (engine.rs:352-355). runtime.rs:1255 binds that Route, and runtime.rs:1304 gates the store on `classification_result.route.starts_with("observer")`, which is true for "observer_failed"; runtime.rs:1308-1330 then stores that heuristic fallback into observer_cache with a hardcoded CacheTTL::Task. cache.rs:69-71 discards the TTL (`_ttl`) and cache.rs:63-65 has no expiry, so CacheTTL::Once is never honored. On a later trigger runtime.rs:1168 looks it up, runtime.rs:1203-1215 wraps it in CachedObserver, and cache.rs:29-37 returns it as Ok, so engine.rs:245-312 follows the success branch: the route becomes observer_uncertain (or observer_unsafe), runtime.rs:1365-1372 never increments observer_failures, and runtime.rs:1305-1307 excludes the replay from observer_calls. No code filters on AlertAuthority in the engine's success branch, so the Unavailable fallback is replayed as an observer judgement with provenance mislabeled in final_decision.rs:157-170. Key recurrence is realistic because the key (runtime.rs:1129-1167) is built only from edge/node type vectors, subject, and one resource path, and ignores intent_count/evidence/score, so any trigger that adds no new graph deltas produces an identical key. Two impact statements are overstated rather than false: the fallback can never be Safe (engine.rs:334-340), and an Unsafe replay with zero citations is counted as uncertain in final_decision.rs:114-121, so the replay cannot fabricate an actionable Safe/Unsafe alert; the concrete harm is suppressed retry for that signature, a stale verdict when intents/evidence change without structural change, and corrupted observer-failure telemetry.

confirmed.title: Forced observer triggers are neutralised by an L1 cache hit
confirmed.evidence: needs_observer_extra (CUSUM/conflict/progressive/PBC>50) and has_suspicious_intents_now are computed at runtime.rs:1183-1191 and passed to classify as force_observer at 1263, but provider selection at 1203-1226 prefers cached_provider before the real provider. Only has_suspicious_intents_now filters the cache (1206); needs_observer_extra does not. quota_bypass is conditioned on `cached.is_none()` (1196-1198), so when any cache entry exists the suspicious-intent quota bypass can never fire. Comments at 1171-1182 and 1186-1191 claim these conditions force fresh LLM arbitration.
confirmed.impact: Exactly the ambiguous/conflict cases the four-condition trigger exists for (evidence conflict, PBC>50, cross-layer boost) replay a stale verdict instead of calling the model. Detection recall and the observer on/off ablation are corrupted silently.
confirmed.fix: When needs_observer_extra is true, ignore the L1 entry and call the real provider (with quota bypass); construct cached_provider only when no forced trigger is active, and base quota_bypass on whether a real call will be made rather than on `cached.is_none()`.

verification.reason: Re-read the cited region of /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/runtime/runtime.rs and the downstream code, and the claim holds exactly. The L1 lookup happens at line 1168 (cache key built at 1147-1167 from only edge types, node types, subject and resource path — no intents, evidence, score or flags). needs_observer_extra is computed at 1183-1184 (evidence_conflict_flag || progressive_fused > 0.4 || pbc_count > 50; CUSUM is explicitly excluded) and has_suspicious_intents_now at 1189-1191. quota_bypass at 1196-1198 is gated on `cached.is_none()`. cached_provider is built at 1203-1208 and filtered only by `!has_suspicious_intents_now` (1206), and observer_for_call at 1212-1226 selects it before the real provider: `if let Some(provider) = cached_provider.as_ref() { Some(provider) } else if self.observer_calls < max || quota_bypass { Some(self.observer.as_ref()) }`. The force flag passed to classify_provisional at 1263 is `needs_observer_extra || has_suspicious_intents_now`, and engine.rs:153 turns that into RouteSelection::ToObserver when observer.is_some(); the "observer" handed over is CachedObserver, whose evaluate() (observer/cache.rs) returns `Ok(self.output.clone())` without any LLM call, so the documented "force fresh LLM arbitration" (comments 1171-1182, 1186-1191; engine.rs:88-93,133-145) is bypassed whenever an entry with that key exists. The cache is only cleared at session init (runtime.rs:364), so entries persist across classification ticks, and the forced triggers are time-dependent (evidence_conflict_flag/progressive_fused come from EWMA updates at 1006/1024) while the cache key is graph-shape-only, so a later conflict/boost trigger on an unchanged graph signature replays a stale verdict. The secondary claim is also correct: when has_suspicious_intents_now is true the cache entry is filtered out (1206) so a real call is intended, but quota_bypass is false because `cached` is Some, so if the quota is exhausted observer_for_call becomes None — the suspicious-intent bypass can never fire once any cache entry exists for the key. The cached Observer output is stored for every observer_* route at 1305-1314, so forced calls seed the cache that later neutralises them. No other code path forces the real provider or invalidates the cache on needs_observer_extra, and no test covers this.

confirmed.title: Observer prompt delimiter is forgeable and untrusted content is inserted unescaped
confirmed.evidence: build_compact_prompt interpolates `ops` and every evidence list into a nonce-less BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_OPERATIONS/END_UNTRUSTED_OPERATIONS block (llm.rs:144-173). `ops` comes from intent descriptions built as `tool: content` (runtime.rs:1239-1244, 120-char cap); evidence lists are OS-derived file paths joined with "; " and only take(8)-truncated (llm.rs:122-143). Neither escapes newlines nor the literal marker. The trusted-looking 'Dims: ... Score=... Corr:...' line and the 'Reply JSON only' instruction are placed after the same marker (llm.rs:151). The only injection countermeasure is a debug-only loop over six substrings (llm.rs:218-241) that never rejects; ObserverError::InjectionDetected/SelfReportedAttack are never constructed (only mapped in provider.rs:256-259).
confirmed.impact: A file path or tool argument containing END_UNTRUSTED_OPERATIONS can close the data block and inject a forged trusted score/correlation line plus a forged reply instruction, or reopen the block; the system prompt's 'treat as data' rule loses its boundary. The documented injection detection is dead code.
confirmed.fix: Serialize the untrusted payload as JSON (escapes newlines/quotes) or wrap it in a random per-request nonce delimiter, and keep the output-format instruction in the system prompt only. Remove the no-op substring loop or make it structural validation.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what is claimed. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/observer/llm.rs, `ops` is built from `content.resource_paths_touched` with take(10)/join("; ") at lines 112-121 and `evidence` from eight OS/tool-derived lists with take(8)/join("; ") at 122-143, with no escaping of newlines or the literal marker. Both are interpolated raw into the single format! at lines 150-151 between literal BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_OPERATIONS / END_UNTRUSTED_OPERATIONS, followed immediately by the trusted-looking "Dims: ... Score=... Corr:..." line and a duplicated "Reply JSON only" instruction (line 151) — the exact boundary-forgery surface described. The only countermeasure is the substring loop at lines 227-241, which merely calls log::debug! and never returns an error, and a repo-wide grep shows ObserverError::InjectionDetected / SelfReportedAttack (types.rs:55-56) are never constructed, only mapped at provider.rs:257-258, so that detection path is dead code. The untrusted text is genuinely attacker-influenceable and unsanitized: runtime/runtime.rs:1228-1246 (the claim's "runtime.rs:1239-1244" points to the same code in the nested path) formats `"{tool}: {content}"` from raw NormalizedArg::Content (commands, old_str/new_str, file content per evidence/args.rs:71-118) truncated only to 120 chars, so a newline plus the marker fits easily; engine.rs:995-999 copies these into ContentSignals and engine.rs:257-262 passes Some(content) into the observer, which provider.rs:145-149 sends as a plain user message after the system prompt. No sanitization/escaping of the marker exists anywhere in collector/src/responsibility, and the issue is not handled elsewhere. Impact is also real rather than theoretical: engine.rs:276-282 applies ObserverDecision::Safe as `score * (1.0 - confidence * 0.7)` and lines 300-306 route any Safe verdict to Route::DirectSafe, so a forged Safe reply suppresses the alert for exactly the pattern-suspicious cases that reach arbitration. No evidence refutes the claim; only a minor path/label imprecision (runtime/runtime.rs vs runtime.rs, and evidence lists include more than file paths) was found, which does not change the conclusion. High severity is appropriate for a detection-bypass of the semantic arbiter in a security-monitoring product.

confirmed.title: L1 cache key omits the evidence that determines the verdict and is order-nondeterministic
confirmed.evidence: CacheKey::compute hashes only edge_types, node_types, subject and one resource_path, truncated to u32 (types.rs:269-287). The inputs are collected from HashMap iteration: graph.rs:654-661 implements all_nodes/all_edges as `self.nodes.values()`/`self.edges.values()`; runtime.rs:1133-1140 builds the hashed Vecs from that iteration, and resource_path is find_map over the same unordered PolicyBoundaryCrossing edges (runtime.rs:1150-1165). rule_ids, pattern_ids, score/score_breakdown, credentials, endpoints, provenance and evidence are absent from the key.
confirmed.impact: Two different sets of observed operations with the same node/edge type sets, same subject and same arbitrarily-chosen boundary resource are treated as identical, so a cached Safe verdict can be replayed for different (including malicious) content. HashMap order changes across graphs/processes, so the same logical signature can hash differently, making cache hit rate and paired on/off measurements unreproducible.
confirmed.fix: Hash a canonical, sorted serialization of the full ObserverInput (at minimum score, rule IDs, pattern IDs and a digest of ContentSignals) and use a 64/128-bit key; sort node/edge type vectors before hashing.

verification.reason: The cited code matches exactly. CacheKey::compute (collector/src/responsibility/observer/types.rs:271-288, hashing at 281-286) hashes only edge_types, node_types, subject and resource_path into a u32; rule_ids, pattern_ids, score/score_breakdown, credentials, endpoints, provenance and ContentSignals never enter the key. runtime.rs:1132-1166 builds those inputs from graph.all_edges()/all_nodes(), which graph.rs:654-661 implements as `self.edges.values()`/`self.nodes.values()` over std HashMap fields (graph.rs:33-34), and picks resource_path via find_map over unordered PolicyBoundaryCrossing edges (runtime.rs:1150-1165); subject is likewise a find_map (1141-1149), so all four key components inherit HashMap iteration order and DefaultHasher is fed order-sensitive Vec<String>s, making hashes vary across map instances/processes for the same logical multiset. On a hit, cache.rs replays the stored ObserverOutput through CachedObserver ignoring the input, and runtime.rs:1210-1218/1237+ passes it into classify_provisional, where engine.rs:233-290 uses the replayed decision to attenuate the score (Safe: `score * (1.0 - confidence*0.7)`); the only guard is `has_suspicious_intents_now`, a hard-coded keyword substring list at runtime.rs:2103-2127 that a differently-worded malicious operation evades, and clear_task_bound (runtime.rs:364) runs once per session, not per operation. So a cached Safe verdict can genuinely be replayed onto different content that shares type sets/subject/resource, and cache hit rate is order-unstable; severity high is warranted.

confirmed.title: Model-requested cache_ttl is validated but never honoured
confirmed.evidence: llm.rs:285-289 maps cache_ttl and system_prompt.rs:30 asks the model to emit once|task|all, but runtime.rs:1314-1329 stores with a hardcoded CacheTTL::Task and cache.rs:67-71 documents `ttl` as unused. ObserverCache has no expiry or per-entry TTL; clear_task_bound (cache.rs:79-81) is only called from init_session (runtime.rs:364), i.e. at a new run, not at a task boundary.
confirmed.impact: A verdict the model explicitly scoped to a single observation (once) is replayed for the whole session, and task is never cleared at a task boundary. The advertised TTL contract does not exist while the prompt spends tokens asking for a discarded value.
confirmed.fix: Either implement TTL semantics in ObserverCache (do not insert Once, expire Task at task boundaries, bound All) and pass the model value through, or remove cache_ttl from the prompt, types and wire format.

verification.reason: Every element of the claim checks out against the cited code. cache.rs (82 lines total) defines `ObserverCache { l1: HashMap<u32, ObserverOutput> }` with no timestamps or expiry, and `store(&mut self, key, output, _ttl: CacheTTL)` at line 69 discards the TTL argument (doc comment at 66-68 states it is accepted only for wire compatibility). The only call site of `store` is runtime.rs:1314-1329, which hardcodes `CacheTTL::Task` (line 1328) even while cloning the real `output.cache_ttl` into the stored struct at line 1320, so the model's value never influences behaviour. `clear_task_bound` (cache.rs:79-81) has exactly one non-test caller, `init_session` at runtime.rs:364, and `init_session` runs once per `process()` call (runtime.rs:2195) — i.e. per run/session, not at any task boundary; there is no task-boundary hook anywhere. The value is nevertheless demanded and validated upstream: system_prompt.rs:30 asks for "once|task|all", llm.rs:151 repeats it in the inline prompt, llm.rs:211-213 rejects out-of-domain values, and llm.rs:285-289 maps them into `CacheTTL`. The CacheKey (types.rs:270-288) hashes only edge/node types, subject and resource_path — no run or task id — so a hit can be replayed for any later observation with the same signature within the session, including one the model scoped to `once`. The only mitigating detail is that "task"-scoped entries are effectively flushed once per process invocation, so the practical delta between `once` and `task` is the intra-run replay window rather than unbounded persistence; that narrows the impact but does not make the TTL contract exist. Medium severity is appropriate: it is a real, documented contract violation with a plausible false-negative path (a once-scoped verdict reused later in the same run) and wasted prompt tokens, but bounded by exact-signature matching and per-run clearing.

confirmed.title: Cache replays are counted as fresh observer verdicts and the observation accumulator survives sessions
confirmed.evidence: runtime.rs:1339-1374 pushes ObserverUnsafe/Safe/Uncertain for every trigger whose route is observer_*, without consulting served_from_cache (computed at 1210). final_decision.rs:101-121 counts these and 140-163 uses the counts for the 'x{unsafe_verdicts} consistent verdict(s)' reasoning and the unsafe-vs-safe disagreement rule. Separately, init_session (runtime.rs:360-374) clears observer_cache and provenance because 'No Observer verdict ... may survive into a new run' but does not clear phase1_observations or observer_failures (initialized at 317-321), which are the observer verdict accumulator.
confirmed.impact: One adjudication replayed N times is reported as N independent consistent verdicts, inflating provenance/counts and letting the disagreement rule turn an Unsafe-only run into Uncertain. If the same Runtime processes a second session, the previous run's verdicts are folded into the new final verdict, contradicting the reset invariant.
confirmed.fix: Record a phase-1 Observation only for real (non-cache) observer calls, or deduplicate by cache key; reset phase1_observations and observer_failures in init_session together with observer_cache.

verification.reason: The code says exactly what is claimed. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/runtime/runtime.rs, `served_from_cache` is computed at line 1210 from `cached_provider` (a `CachedObserver` built at 1203-1209 when the L1 signature cache hits), and it is consulted in exactly one place: line 1305, to avoid incrementing the quota counter `observer_calls`. The phase-1 observation push at 1339-1374 has no such guard: a route of `observer_unsafe`/`observer_safe`/`observer_uncertain` pushes `Observation::Observer*` unconditionally, and a cache hit yields those routes because the `CachedObserver` is passed into `classify_provisional` at 1255-1272 (engine.rs:167-230 turns any ToObserver result into `observer_*`). Since the trigger loop runs every N events (runtime.rs:2222) and over the cumulative graph built at 909, and the cache key at 1132-1167 is derived from graph *types*, repeated triggers on an unchanged graph replay one adjudication into N observations. final_decision.rs:101-121 counts these without dedup, and 140-163 use the counts for the `observer_unsafe:x{unsafe_verdicts}` provenance and the "x{unsafe_verdicts} consistent verdict(s)" reasoning, so the count/provenance inflation is real. The second half is also accurate at the code level: `init_session` (runtime.rs:360-373) clears `observer_cache` and `provenance` with the comment that no Observer verdict may survive into a new run, but `phase1_observations` and `observer_failures` are only ever initialized at 316-321 and are never cleared (finalize() at 1785 merely clones them; only `phase1_alert_ids` is drained at 1913). That said, I downgrade severity: one cached signature can only replay its own stored decision, so it cannot by itself manufacture the Safe+Unsafe mix needed by the disagreement rule at final_decision.rs:154-163 — that flip requires the session-carryover path, and no in-repo caller reuses a Runtime across sessions (main.rs:1681 constructs it once and main.rs:1712 runs the agent once; `init_session` is private and only `process()` at 2195 calls it). The confirmed impact is therefore inflated verdict counts/provenance and a latent reset-invariant violation, not a demonstrated decision flip in the shipped CLI.

confirmed.title: Observer timeout covers only headers and max_retries is never used
confirmed.evidence: provider.rs:172-180 wraps `client.request(req)` in tokio::time::timeout, but the response body is collected at 183-188 outside that timeout, after client.request has resolved on headers. ObserverProviderConfig.max_retries is deserialized (40-49) and set to 1 in from_env (104), but evaluate (116-261) contains no retry loop and never reads the field.
confirmed.impact: A provider that returns headers then stalls the body hangs the runtime indefinitely despite timeout_ms, blocking classification. Transient 429/5xx/timeouts fail on the first attempt and (via finding 1) become cached failures; operators tuning max_retries get no effect.
confirmed.fix: Wrap the whole send+body+parse sequence in one timeout, and implement bounded retries with backoff for timeout/429/5xx, or delete max_retries from the config and wire format.

verification.reason: Both halves of the claim are borne out by the code. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/observer/provider.rs, the `tokio::time::timeout` at lines 174-179 wraps only the future returned by `client.request(req)` (line 172); hyper resolves that future once response headers arrive, so the subsequent `resp.into_body().collect().await` at lines 183-188 streams the body with no deadline, and the client built at line 161 sets no timeout either — a provider that sends headers then stalls indeed blocks `evaluate` indefinitely despite `timeout_ms`. The field `max_retries` is only declared at line 41 (deserialized via `default_retries`, lines 47-49) and assigned at line 104 in `from_env`; a repo-wide grep for `max_retries` under /tmp/mtal-audit returns only those two Rust occurrences (plus an unrelated string in compare/scripts/evaluate_prompt_tools.py), and `evaluate` (lines 116-261) contains a single send with no loop or backoff, so the configured value is dead. I also checked the call sites to rule out an outer retry/timeout: classification/engine.rs:245 calls `obs.evaluate(&obs_input).await` directly, and runtime/runtime.rs:1212-1226 only decides whether to pass the provider, with no wrapping timeout or retry. The proposed fix (wrap send+body+parse in one timeout; implement bounded retries or remove the field) is appropriate.

confirmed.title: Serde defaults turn non-verdict JSON into a valid 'uncertain 0.5' judgement
confirmed.evidence: RawObserverResponse gives serde defaults to decision, severity, confidence, cache_ttl and reasoning (llm.rs:29-60), and serde ignores unknown fields. parse_and_validate therefore accepts any syntactically valid object, e.g. `{}` or `{"error":"..."}`, producing decision=uncertain, severity=warning, confidence=0.5, cache_ttl=once (llm.rs:191-199, 320-331). The provider only rejects a completely missing text block (provider.rs:245-251).
confirmed.impact: A model refusal, API error object or empty answer is recorded and later aggregated as a reasoned 50% Uncertain Observer verdict; the fabricated verdict is also cached (findings 1/4) and reported by final_decision as a real adjudication.
confirmed.fix: Make decision/severity/confidence required (Option fields) and return ValidationError when absent; reject payloads containing no recognised verdict field.

verification.reason: The code says exactly what the claim says. RawObserverResponse (llm.rs:29-47) marks decision, severity, confidence, cache_ttl, reasoning, evidence_cited, rule_verdicts and pattern_verdicts with #[serde(default...)] bound to defaults at llm.rs:49-60 ("uncertain", "warning", 0.5, "once", ""), and it carries no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] (confirmed by grep: the only occurrence of RawObserverResponse outside its definition is llm.rs:191 and the comment at provider.rs:240). parse_and_validate (llm.rs:180-332) therefore parses `{}` or `{"error":"..."}` successfully and the domain checks at llm.rs:202-216 pass because the defaults are themselves legal values (uncertain / warning / 0.5 / once), returning Ok(ObserverOutput{decision: Uncertain, severity: Warning, confidence: 0.5, cache_ttl: Once, authority: Unavailable, reasoning: ""}) at llm.rs:320-331. Crucially the reachable path is broader than just `{}`: the truncation-recovery branch at llm.rs:194-198 passes the repaired string through the same permissive deserializer, so a response truncated before the decision field is recovered into a syntactically valid object that is then accepted as a 50%-confidence Uncertain verdict. The only upstream guard is provider.rs:245-251, which rejects a missing text block (and the comment at provider.rs:238-244 shows the authors knew the "{}" hazard but only removed the literal "{}" fallback); nothing rejects a present-but-uninformative text block. Downstream, engine.rs:245-312 turns the parsed output into route "observer_uncertain" and pushes Observation::ObserverUncertain{confidence} in runtime.rs:1339-1361, which final_decision.rs:117 counts in uncertain_verdicts and final_decision.rs:165-178 renders as the review verdict with provenance observer_uncertain:xN; runtime.rs:1304-1330 stores that same output in the L1 cache regardless of confidence/authority, and cache.rs:30-36 replays it. The one overstatement in the claim is that a natural-language refusal would not be accepted (it is non-JSON, so parsing fails and the observer_failed path at engine.rs:314-357 runs); the accepted cases are empty/unknown-field JSON objects and truncation-recovered fragments. That narrowing does not change the defect or its impact on metrics, caching and reported adjudication, so medium severity stands.

confirmed.title: Alert authority is derived from unverified model-supplied citations
confirmed.evidence: authority is set to Supporting whenever evidence_cited is non-empty (llm.rs:253-263), with no check that any cited string corresponds to an operation in the signature or ContentSignals. The same unvalidated length drives final_decision.rs:104-114 (`cited == 0` vs `unsafe_verdicts += 1`) and runtime.rs:1457-1462 (observer_detected).
confirmed.impact: The model can self-award Supporting authority and an actionable ObserverUnsafe claim by emitting evidence_cited:["x"]; alerts are labelled ObserverJudged/Supporting with citations never verified against OS evidence. Combined with the injection path in finding 3, an arbitrary planted string can produce an actionable verdict.
confirmed.fix: Validate each cited item against actual operations (exact/substring match to paths, endpoints, rule IDs or tool calls) and downgrade authority to Unavailable when nothing matches.

verification.reason: The claim's code facts hold exactly. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/observer/llm.rs the only test on citations is emptiness: `let authority = if raw.evidence_cited.is_empty() { Unavailable } else { Supporting }` at lines 259-263, and the only other citation check (lines 278-284) downgrades Unsafe to Uncertain when the list is empty; line 328 then copies `evidence_cited: raw.evidence_cited` straight into ObserverOutput with no matching against `signature` or `content_signals` (the prompt builder at lines 100-176 merely joins those fields as text). A repo-wide grep for citation/evidence validation (`verify_citation`, `sanitize_evidence`, etc.) finds nothing outside those two emptiness checks; system_prompt.rs:26 only instructs the model that unsafe "MUST cite at least one operation" without any enforcement. The downstream claims are also accurate: runtime.rs:1345-1349 pushes `Observation::ObserverUnsafe { cited: output.evidence_cited.len() }` (so only a count, never the strings, reaches aggregation), final_decision.rs:104-114 increments `unsafe_verdicts` for any `cited != 0`, and final_decision.rs:140-152 then returns `AlertDecision::Unsafe` / `AlertSeverity::Critical` / `AlertAuthority::Supporting`, which alert_builder.rs:258-269 maps to `DisplayProfile::ObserverJudged`. runtime.rs:1457-1462 likewise opens the alert gate on `!o.evidence_cited.is_empty()`. Thus a model response `{"decision":"unsafe","severity":"critical","evidence_cited":["x"],...}` produces an actionable Critical/Supporting ObserverJudged alert whose citation is never checked against OS evidence; since the Operations block is explicitly attacker-influenceable data (llm.rs:130-150), a planted string suffices. The design comment at llm.rs:253-258 justifies the choice but does not refute the integrity gap, and the proposed fix (exact/substring match to paths/endpoints/rule IDs/tool calls, else Unavailable) is implementable against ContentSignals. No mitigation exists at any other layer.

confirmed.title: Observer evidence is truncated by list position, letting benign entries crowd out incriminating ones
confirmed.evidence: build_compact_prompt emits at most 10 entries of resource_paths_touched (llm.rs:112-121) and at most 8 of each evidence list (llm.rs:124-141) with no priority for credential/provenance/rule evidence. build_content_signals sorts every list lexicographically before the Observer sees it (engine.rs:1053-1064), while resource_paths_touched keeps intent order (engine.rs:997-999), so which items survive depends on attacker-chosen names and call order.
confirmed.impact: An agent/adversary who creates lexicographically early file paths or issues enough benign tool calls first can push the credential path, exfiltration endpoint or provenance entry out of the prompt; the arbiter then judges an incomplete observation set, making detection rate a function of name ordering rather than behaviour.
confirmed.fix: Rank evidence before truncation (credential and provenance first, then rule/pattern hits), cap by total characters with an explicit 'omitted N items' marker, and never drop security-relevant categories.

verification.reason: The claim's mechanism is real, with one overstatement worth noting. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/observer/llm.rs, build_compact_prompt caps `resource_paths_touched` at `.take(10)` (lines 112-118) and every evidence list at `.take(8)` inside the `join` closure (lines 124-129), formatting Paths/Network/Credentials/Rules/Patterns/Delegation/ToolCalls/Provenance with no ranking and no "omitted N" marker (lines 131-142). The sorting the claim cites is in the correct but differently-pathed file, /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/classification/engine.rs (not responsibility/engine.rs): `resource_paths_touched` is seeded from `intent_descriptions.to_vec()` at lines 996-999 and left in intent order, while file_paths, credential_paths, network_endpoints, delegation_links, rule_ids, pattern_ids, tool_calls and provenance are all `sort()`ed then `dedup()`ed at lines 1053-1065. Because the graph permits up to 50,000 nodes (graph/config.rs:25 `hard_max_nodes: 50_000`), any of these lists can trivially exceed 8, so truncation keeps the lexicographically smallest entries — which the adversary controls via file names, hostnames, rule-matching paths, and call IDs. Two corrections: (1) cross-category crowd-out is impossible because each category has its own line and its own cap, so a benign file path cannot evict a credential entry — the claim's phrasing overstates that; eviction happens only within a category (e.g. >8 benign network endpoints sorted before the exfil host). (2) The Observer is not blind to the rest of the evidence: the prompt still carries the D1-D6 breakdown and total score, which are computed from the full graph, so detection is degraded rather than fully gamed. Neither correction defeats the core defect: the truncation is position-based, adversary-influenceable, and silent, and the Observer's verdict is authoritative — a Safe decision attenuates the score by `score * (1.0 - confidence * 0.7)` (classification/engine.rs lines ~276-279), so dropping the incriminating item can pull an alert below threshold. Severity medium is appropriate; keep `none`.

confirmed.title: Observer cost/usage is printed to stderr and never recorded anywhere
confirmed.evidence: provider.rs:202-217 eprintln!s a `[observer:usage] input_tokens=... output_tokens=...` line, and the comment claims 'the runtime copies the counts into the run's diagnostics line'. No code parses `observer:usage` or the token counts (grep over collector/src finds no consumer). ObserverOutput (types.rs:252-265) has no usage field and persistence has no observer token counters.
confirmed.impact: Per-run/per-scenario observer spend is not auditable or persistable, so cost tables and the cost/benefit claims of the ablation cannot be reproduced from the database or reports; usage from failed/retried calls is lost entirely.
confirmed.fix: Return usage in the provider result, accumulate it in Runtime state, and persist it with the run/alert records; keep stderr only as a secondary diagnostic.

verification.reason: The cited lines are exactly as described: provider.rs:202-204 states "Cost visibility: a run's observer spend must be auditable ... the runtime copies the counts into the run's diagnostics line", then provider.rs:205-217 emits `[observer:usage] input_tokens=... output_tokens=...` via eprintln!. The comment is false: the runtime's structured diagnostics line at runtime.rs:2012-2045 contains only counters such as `observer_failures` (2028), latency, decode_status, and taint_* — no input/output token or cost fields; the only observer accounting it keeps is `observer_calls` (runtime.rs:1306 increment, 1963 summary, output.rs:42), i.e. call counts, not tokens. ObserverOutput (observer/types.rs:253-266) has no usage field, and grep across the whole snapshot for `observer:usage` returns only provider.rs:207, while `input_tokens` outside docs/test fixtures also appears only there — so no Rust, Python, or report code consumes it. The benchmark side confirms the same gap: collector_manager.py:417-429 parses only the `[diagnostics:json]` line and :500-504 extracts only "Observer calls", never token counts. Two nuances temper but do not overturn the claim: the collector's stdout+stderr is redirected to a retained per-run `{log_file}.log` (collector_manager.py:669,756), so the usage line is technically present in raw logs even though nothing parses or persists it, making the title's "never recorded anywhere" slightly overstated; and provider.rs:191-199 returns early on any HTTP failure, so usage from failed calls (and the unused `max_retries` config at :41/:104 — there is no actual retry loop) is genuinely lost. The core defect — no structured per-run observer token accounting, no persistence/DB/report field, and a comment claiming integration that does not exist — is verified by the code.

confirmed.title: Default no-key observer fallback always errors instead of providing a mock verdict
confirmed.evidence: main.rs:1573-1579 constructs MockObserverProvider::with_responses(vec![]). MockObserverProvider::evaluate returns Err(ApiError("mock: no responses configured")) once the response list is exhausted (mock.rs:50-56), while the preceding message advertises 'Mock (zero-token dev mode)' (main.rs:1574).
confirmed.impact: In the default configuration with no ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, every observer call fails; combined with finding 1 the first failure is cached and replayed as an Uncertain verdict, so 'dev mode' silently reports observer judgements that never happened and is indistinguishable at run level from a real endpoint outage.
confirmed.fix: Construct the mock with one explicit Uncertain output and mark it as mock in verdict provenance, or set disable_observer=true when no provider is configured and surface that state in run diagnostics.

verification.reason: The cited code is exactly as claimed. /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/main.rs:1552 comments that the fallback is a "Mock provider (zero-token dev/testing fallback)", line 1574 prints "! Observer: no config file or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, using Mock (zero-token dev mode)", and lines 1576-1578 construct `MockObserverProvider::with_responses(vec![])`. This branch is genuinely reached by default: provider.rs:88-96 makes `from_env()` return ConfigError when ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is unset, provider.rs:70-86 returns `Ok(None)` when neither `env/config/observer.toml` nor `observer_llm.toml` exists (neither exists in the snapshot), and the observer is unconditionally wired into `ResponsibilityRuntime::new` at main.rs:1681-1686 while `disable_observer` is only set from `--disable-responsibility-observer || lite` (main.rs:1543, default false; RuntimeConfig default false at runtime.rs:106). With an empty response vector, mock.rs:50-56 always takes the `responses.last().cloned().ok_or_else(...)` path and returns `Err(ApiError("mock: no responses configured"))`, so every observer call in this configuration fails; the error is handled at engine.rs:318-361 as an Uncertain "observer_failed" fallback rather than crashing, and runtime.rs:1300-1320 stores any route starting with "observer" (including "observer_failed") into the L1 cache, whose CachedObserver (cache.rs:30-36) later replays it as an `observer_uncertain` verdict without any call, matching the described impact. I found no other code path that substitutes a working provider or mock in this branch, so the claim survives.

confirmed.title: Evidence and graph endpoints answer with the newest run in the DB, ignoring the requested run id
confirmed.evidence: resolve_db_run_id() (web.rs:1309-1320) returns list_runs().first(), i.e. the newest run by started_at_ns, and is the only run-id source for serve_graph_from_db (web.rs:1286) and serve_evidence_from_db (web.rs:1332); requested_run_id is used only when the DB has no runs row at all. Multi-run DBs are a supported, real state: the DB path is `{log}.responsibility.db` (main.rs:1529) and the code itself says reusing `-o` appends runs (web.rs:1493, 1091-1097). The alerts endpoint already refuses to mix runs and returns 409 ambiguous_run (web.rs:1485-1505).
confirmed.impact: For any archived DB holding more than one run, /api/runs/<dir>/evidence returns another run's evidence/intents/actions (and the graph endpoint's node/edge fallback returns another run's graph) under the requested run's id, so a reviewer is shown the wrong run's data without any error.
confirmed.fix: Resolve the run exactly as serve_alerts_from_db does (single run / explicit match / 409) before calling get_evidence/get_graph, and return a conflict rather than substituting the newest run.

verification.reason: The cited code says what the claim reports. In collector/src/server/web.rs, resolve_db_run_id (lines 1309-1320) returns reader.list_runs()?.first(), and reader.rs:345-347 orders that query by started_at_ns DESC, so the first entry is the newest run; the requested id is consulted only in the `Ok(None) => requested_run_id.to_string()` arm (web.rs:1317-1318, 1337-1338). serve_evidence_from_db (web.rs:1322-1341) passes that resolved (newest) id into get_evidence/get_intents/get_actions/get_non_link_diagnostics, and reader.rs:496-500 confirms those queries filter strictly by the id they are given, so an archived DB with two runs returns the newest run's evidence under the older directory's id. serve_graph_from_db does filter graph_snapshots by requested_run_id (web.rs:1214-1223), so the title is overbroad for the snapshot path, but the node/edge fallback at web.rs:1286 calls the same resolve_db_run_id and then get_graph(run_id), which only happens when no snapshot matches and the `runs` count is >1 (web.rs:1240-1258); there the newest run's graph_nodes/graph_edges are returned. Multi-run DBs in one run directory are a supported, exercised state: main.rs:1529 uses `{log}.responsibility.db`, the comments at web.rs:1091-1097 and 1491-1494 acknowledge that reusing `-o` appends runs, and the test at web.rs:2760-2783 seeds run-a and run-b into one fixture DB. The contrast is intentional: serve_alerts_from_db (web.rs:1479-1505) resolves single-run/explicit-match/`live` and otherwise returns 409 `ambiguous_run` (asserted at web.rs:2816), while evidence and the graph fallback silently substitute the newest run instead of applying the same rule. Severity high is appropriate because a reviewer can be shown another run's evidence/graph with no error in a product whose alerts endpoint already treats run mixing as a conflict-level defect.

confirmed.title: Replay loads every alert as 'phase 1' because the reader has no phase-scoped query
confirmed.evidence: get_alerts() selects every responsibility_alerts row for the run with no phase predicate (reader.rs:362-372), even though the phase column is written (writer.rs:848) and distinguishes Provisional phase-1 alerts (runtime.rs:1486-1488) from the single Authoritative alert (runtime.rs:1869-1875, persisted at 1901-1904). replay/executor.rs:306 labels this result `phase1_alerts`. Replayed alerts are built with AlertBuilder::compose, which sets provisional_ref: None (alert_builder.rs:233), so build_classification_refinements' p2_by_p1 map (executor.rs:551-555) is always empty.
confirmed.impact: Every persisted alert, including the persisted phase-2 final alert, is emitted as a Dismissed classification refinement while every replayed alert is emitted as Discovered; phase1_alert_count equals N+1. The replay report's confirmed/changed/dismissed/discovered counts and phase1/phase2 alert counts are wrong for every run.
confirmed.fix: Add a phase-scoped reader query (filter `phase LIKE 'Provisional%'` for phase 1) and have replay load only the phase-1 subset; parse the persisted phase variant instead of collapsing it so the filter and the result are meaningful.

verification.reason: The defect reproduces as claimed in /tmp/mtal-audit. reader.rs:362-372 `get_alerts(run_id)` selects every responsibility_alerts row for the run with only `WHERE run_id = ?1` and no phase predicate, even though `phase` and `provisional_ref` are both selected (line 367) and mapped (reader.rs:457, 485-486); `parse_phase` (reader.rs:67-77) can distinguish Provisional from Authoritative. writer.rs:826-850 persists `format!("{:?}", alert.phase)` (line 848) plus provisional_ref (849), and runtime.rs:1486-1488/1520-1526 persist each Provisional phase-1 alert while runtime.rs:1869-1904 persist the single Authoritative phase-2 alert (with provisional_ref set at 1877), so the table for a run holds N provisional rows plus 1 authoritative row. replay/executor.rs:306 loads all of them into `phase1_alerts` and line 308 passes them as the phase-1 argument to build_classification_refinements, while the phase-2 argument is the replayed `alerts` vector built with `AlertBuilder::compose` (executor.rs:272-280), whose resulting `provisional_ref` is None (alert_builder.rs:233, reached via compose at 55-96 delegating to compose_with_context at 99).
