Consequently p2_by_p1 (executor.rs:551-555) is empty, every loaded row — including the persisted Authoritative row — falls to the Dismissed branch (executor.rs:599-607), and every replayed alert hits the Discovered branch (executor.rs:609-626) since its provisional_ref is None; phase1_alert_count at executor.rs:315 equals `phase1_alerts.len()` = N+1, and the confirmed/changed/dismissed/discovered counts feeding precision/recall/F1 (executor.rs:347-375) are therefore wrong on every run with at least one phase-1 alert. The only inaccuracy in the claim's wording is the parenthetical that the persisted phase-2 alert itself has an empty provisional_ref — runtime.rs:1877 actually sets it — but that does not change the outcome, because the lookup map is built from the replayed alerts rather than the persisted rows. The path is live (collector/src/bin/replay.rs:220 also calls get_alerts), and no other code filters or repairs these counts. Severity high is appropriate: replay is the run-evaluation module and its classification metrics are systematically wrong for every run.

confirmed.title: Run summary reads the canonical verdict and start time without scoping them to the requested run
confirmed.evidence: run_summary_value receives run_id (web.rs:914) but read_final_verdict queries `SELECT final_decision,... FROM runs WHERE final_decision IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1` with neither a run_id predicate nor ORDER BY (web.rs:898-905), and started_at_ns runs `SELECT started_at_ns FROM runs ORDER BY started_at_ns DESC LIMIT 1` (web.rs:936). One database can legitimately contain several runs (main.rs:1529; web.rs:1493).
confirmed.impact: For a multi-run DB the summary combines the oldest row's canonical verdict with the newest row's start time, so a run page can display an Unsafe/Safe decision that belongs to a different run, and the two fields can describe two different runs at once. This is the value the run selector renders (frontend/components/system/run-selector.tsx:115).
confirmed.fix: Resolve the DB run id the same way serve_alerts_from_db does and add `WHERE run_id = ?1` to both queries (return a conflict when the DB is ambiguous).

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what the claim states. At /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/server/web.rs:898-901 `read_final_verdict` prepares `SELECT final_decision, final_severity, final_authority, final_alert_id FROM runs WHERE final_decision IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1` — no `run_id` predicate, no ORDER BY — while its signature at line 892 takes only `run_dir` (the requested `run_id` is available at line 914 in `run_summary_value` but is not passed in; the verdict is fetched at line 968). The start time at line 936 is `SELECT started_at_ns FROM runs ORDER BY started_at_ns DESC LIMIT 1`, again unscoped. The `runs` table is keyed by `run_id` (collector/src/responsibility/persistence/schema.rs:504-511) and the writer inserts one row per run (writer.rs:440, 506), so a DB can legitimately hold multiple rows: web.rs:1475-1500 explicitly says "a DB with several runs must never answer with another run's alerts" and handles the `ambiguous_run` CONFLICT case, and the test `get_run_alerts_filters_by_run_id_when_db_holds_several_runs` (web.rs:2755-2820) builds exactly such a DB. Other summary-adjacent endpoints correctly scope or refuse to mix (web.rs:1116, 1225-1250), which makes the omission here a real inconsistency rather than dead/legacy code. Consequently `LIMIT 1` without ORDER BY returns an arbitrary (in SQLite practice, lowest-rowid/oldest) verdict while the start time returns the newest row, so one summary payload can pair a verdict from one run with a start time from another; that payload's `final_verdict` is rendered as the run label in frontend/components/system/run-selector.tsx:115. The proposed fix (resolve the DB run id as `serve_alerts_from_db` does and add `WHERE run_id = ?1`, returning a conflict when ambiguous) is sound. Severity high is appropriate because the wrong canonical Unsafe/Safe verdict can be shown for a run.

confirmed.title: batch_interval_ms is re-armed on every record, so periodic commits never happen under load
confirmed.evidence: WriterConfig documents batch_interval_ms as "Batch commit every N milliseconds" (writer.rs:181-182), but the sleep future is created inside the loop immediately before select! (writer.rs:376-384) and is dropped whenever rx.recv() wins. It therefore fires only after batch_interval_ms of channel idleness; during traffic commits occur only at pending >= batch_size (writer.rs:556-560), on Flush, or at RunEnd. The configured default is 200 ms and main.rs uses Default (main.rs:1531).
confirmed.impact: With a steady stream slower than one record per 200 ms and fewer than 500 records per batch, the open transaction is never committed during the run: a crash (WAL recovery) discards everything since the last batch boundary, and read-only consumers (web server, replay) see no records until finalize. The documented periodic-commit latency is effectively not implemented.
confirmed.fix: Hoist a persistent deadline (tokio::time::interval, or track last_commit and recompute the remaining sleep) and reset it only after a successful commit, so the timer enforces a maximum commit age rather than an idle timeout.

verification.reason: The mechanism is exactly as cited. In writer_task the loop body creates a fresh `tokio::time::sleep(interval)` at writer.rs:381 (interval built once from batch_interval_ms at 372), then `tokio::select!` at 384 races it against `rx.recv()`; when a record arrives the unselected sleep is dropped and the next iteration starts a brand-new full-length sleep, so the timer is an idle-timeout, not a max-commit-age deadline. The only other commit triggers are `pending >= batch_size` (556-560), Flush (416-424), and the run-boundary variants (RunStart/RunEnd/RunFinalVerdict/RunRecord at ~430-520), plus the final COMMIT when the channel closes (395-399); nothing else re-arms or drives a commit, and commit_batch (1190-1212) only closes an already-open transaction. Defaults are confirmed as batch_size 500 / batch_interval_ms 200 at writer.rs:191-192, and main.rs:1530-1533 uses `..Default::default()`, with the only in-run flush at runtime.rs:2045 (end of finalize), so no periodic flush exists elsewhere. The in-code comment at 1179 ("The batch trigger is pending >= batch_size (or the interval timer)") confirms the intended semantics, and no test exercises the interval path (grep for interval/elapsed/timeout finds only 372/381). One correction to the claim's impact text: the scenario is inverted — with records arriving *slower* than one per 200 ms the sleep does fire and commit every 200 ms; the broken band is sustained traffic *faster* than 5 records/s but under 500 records per commit window, where the open transaction's age is unbounded. That is still a real defeat of the documented 200 ms periodic-commit guarantee and a live-reader/crash-exposure defect, but the loss window remains bounded by batch_size (500) records, which the batching policy already accepts, so I rate it medium rather than high.

confirmed.title: Run-scoped rows are keyed without run_id, so a reused database silently drops or steals an earlier run's rows
confirmed.evidence: process_events is UNIQUE(pid, start_time_ns) (schema.rs:163) and written with INSERT OR IGNORE (writer.rs:570), so a process observed again in a later run is never recorded for that run. agent_identities is PK agent_id (schema.rs:268) and written with INSERT OR REPLACE (writer.rs:911); subagent_boundaries is PK boundary_id (schema.rs:388) and REPLACE with the deterministic id `{parent}-{child}-{parent_start_time_ns}` (writer.rs:1021-1037). Phase-2 AgentIds are deterministically derived from ProcessIds (identity/union_find.rs:251-263), so a long-lived agent process produces the same id in the next run. Multi-run DBs are supported (main.rs:1529, web.rs:1493).
confirmed.impact: After a collector restart that appends a run to the same DB, the earlier run loses its authoritative identity and subagent-boundary rows (their run_id is moved to the new run) while the new run has no process_events for the already-running agent process. Per-run identity counts, get_authoritative_identities, and pid-to-agent joins are wrong for both runs.
confirmed.fix: Make the keys run-scoped (UNIQUE(pid, start_time_ns, run_id), PK(agent_id, run_id), PK(boundary_id, run_id)) and drop the REPLACE semantics that re-points a row owned by another run.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what the claim reports. In schema.rs the process_events table has a bare UNIQUE(pid, start_time_ns) at line 163 with run_id only a non-key column (162), agent_identities has PK agent_id at line 268 with run_id non-key (274), and subagent_boundaries has PK boundary_id at line 388 with run_id non-key (396). writer.rs confirms the conflict semantics: process_events is written INSERT OR IGNORE at line 570, agent_identities with INSERT OR REPLACE at line 911, and subagent_boundaries with INSERT OR REPLACE at line 1021 whose boundary_id is the run-independent string `{parent}-{child}-{parent_start_time_ns}` at lines 1026-1031. The deterministic IDs are real: union_find.rs:254-269 derives `agent-{sha256(pid:start_time_ns;...)}` from the sorted ProcessId set, and it is used for authoritative agents (line 603) and both sides of subagent boundaries (lines 425-426, 455-456, 512-513), so a component containing the same long-lived processes yields the same agent_id and boundary_id in a later run; runtime.rs:1650-1689 then re-persists those rows via write_blocking at finalize. The multi-run premise is also explicit, not inferred: web.rs:1491-1494 states "Reusing `-o <same log>` across restarts makes the DB accumulate runs", web.rs:1079 and 1475-1500 add multi-run resolution/`ambiguous_run` handling, main.rs:1529 builds the DB path from the reused log file, reader.rs:705 filters get_authoritative_identities by run_id, and replay/executor.rs:427 reads process_events by run_id. A REPLACE therefore deletes the prior run's agent_identities/subagent_boundaries row and reinserts it under the new run_id, and the old run's per-run reads silently return nothing; the v2 migration only made identity_process_map run-scoped (schema.rs:576-604, identity_process_beliefs), leaving agent_identities and subagent_boundaries un-scoped. One nuance that narrows but does not refute the claim: process_events are only persisted for EXEC events (runtime.rs:632-665), so an idle pre-existing process gets no process_events row in the new run regardless of the UNIQUE key; the OR IGNORE collision bites when that same ProcessId execs again after the restart (exec preserves pid and start_time_ns). The identity/boundary row theft is unambiguous, so the defect stands.

confirmed.title: Per-run provenance columns are never written: PersistRecord::RunRecord has no production producer
confirmed.evidence: RunStart inserts only (run_id, started_at_ns) (writer.rs:439-444). scenario_id, mode and collector_version are written solely by the PersistRecord::RunRecord branch (writer.rs:499-519), and no code outside persistence/writer.rs constructs PersistRecord::RunRecord (the only occurrence is the test at writer.rs:1476). The reader maps those columns (reader.rs:310-327), the frontend imports them (frontend/lib/db-import.ts:468-484) and displays them (frontend/lib/dataset-summary.ts:201).
confirmed.impact: runs.scenario_id, runs.mode and runs.collector_version are NULL in every real capture, so a database cannot establish which scenario, run mode or collector version produced its rows; the dataset-overview fields are permanently empty. The same dead branch uses INSERT OR REPLACE (writer.rs:506), so wiring it later would also reset the v3 final_* evidence columns.
confirmed.fix: Emit the run metadata from RuntimeConfig at RunStart/finalize (or UPDATE the three columns at RunEnd), and make the branch an UPDATE so it can never replace the run row and erase the verdict.

verification.reason: I re-read the snapshot and could not refute the claim. The only production RunStart producer is runtime.rs:368, which sends only run_id and timestamp_ns; the writer handles it at writer.rs:439-444 with `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO runs (run_id, started_at_ns)`, leaving scenario_id, mode and collector_version unset. Those three columns are written only by the PersistRecord::RunRecord branch at writer.rs:499-519 (SQL at 506-507). A repo-wide grep for PersistRecord/RunRecord shows the variant is constructed exactly once, at writer.rs:1476, which sits inside the `#[cfg(test)]` module starting at writer.rs:1218; there are no PersistRecord producers in collector/src/bin, tests, Python or TS. The only other SQL populating those columns is web.rs:2719, also inside the test module (`#[cfg(test)]` at web.rs:1909). The only other runs UPDATEs are ended_at_ns (writer.rs:455-458) and the final_* verdict columns (writer.rs:482-485), so nothing backfills provenance. Schema.rs:504-511 defines the three columns nullable, reader.rs:301-327 selects and maps them, and the frontend does consume them (db-import.ts:468-484, dataset-summary.ts:201), so in every real capture they are NULL. The secondary point also holds literally: if the dead branch were ever wired, its `INSERT OR REPLACE` (writer.rs:506) replaces the whole row, and since RunEnd/RunFinalVerdict write to that same row it could wipe ended_at_ns/final_* state — though that is currently unreachable, so it is a latent risk rather than an active bug. Severity: the defect is missing provenance metadata, not corruption of captured events, and it degrades dataset labeling/reproducibility rather than monitoring behavior; medium is defensible for a research dataset pipeline, so I keep it, though low would also be arguable given the branch is dead code.

confirmed.title: Persisted phase is flattened on read: timestamps become 0 and unknown values become Authoritative
confirmed.evidence: parse_phase (reader.rs:67-77) inspects only the first token of the Debug string written at writer.rs:682/734/753/848/877. It always returns Provisional{timestamp_ns:0} or Authoritative{timestamp_ns:0, overrides:None}, discarding the stored timestamp and overrides, and maps any unrecognized value to Authoritative. The frontend's own parser retains both fields (frontend/lib/db-import.ts:229-247).
confirmed.impact: Every alert/claim/edge/node served by PersistenceReader (REST /alerts, replay) reports phase timestamp 0, so consumers that order or attribute by phase time get zero (frontend/lib/types.ts:266 documents that field as the claim sort key), and a corrupt or future phase string is silently reported as the highest authority instead of an error.
confirmed.fix: Parse the full persisted representation (variant, timestamp_ns, overrides) and return a decode error, not Authoritative, for values that do not match.

verification.reason: reader.rs:67-77 does exactly what the claim says: parse_phase matches only `raw.starts_with("Provisional")` and returns `Provisional { timestamp_ns: 0 }`, otherwise unconditionally returns `Authoritative { timestamp_ns: 0, overrides: None }`, with no parsing of the stored Debug text and no error path. The writer persists the full Debug form at writer.rs:682 (evidence), 734 (graph node), 753 (graph edge), 848 (alert), 877 (claim), e.g. `format!("{:?}", alert.phase)`, and PhaseIndicator derives Debug (phase.rs:5-14), so real timestamps and any `overrides` are present in the column and then dropped on read. The lossy parser is reached at reader.rs:485 (alerts), 515 (evidence), 640 (nodes), 662 (edges), and those values are served by REST handlers at web.rs:1291 (graph) and web.rs:1514 (/alerts), so the path is live, not dead code. Two parts of the stated impact are overstated: PersistenceReader never reads `responsibility_claims` (no ResponsibilityClaim mapping anywhere in reader.rs), and the frontend claim sort key documented at types.ts:266 is derived in db-import.ts:312-350 from its own correct `parsePhaseIndicator` (db-import.ts:229-247) reading the column directly, not from the reader; also no production constructor ever builds `overrides: Some(...)` (only None), so that loss is currently inert. The unknown-value-becomes-Authoritative behavior is real and notably contradicts this file's own stated policy for corrupt columns (deser_json at reader.rs:42-53 errors rather than fabricating a value), but requires a corrupt or future phase string. Real data-fidelity/robustness bug with no demonstrated consumer reading phase timestamps through the reader today: confirm at reduced severity.

confirmed.title: v3 migration adds the canonical-verdict columns without backfilling existing runs
confirmed.evidence: migrate_to_v3 only ALTERs runs to add final_alert_id/final_decision/final_severity/final_authority/decision_provenance_json (schema.rs:697-711); it never derives a verdict from the Authoritative alert already present in the same database. read_final_verdict then returns None for such runs (web.rs:892-905) and scripts/evaluation/final_verdict_metrics.py:53-56 classifies rows without final_decision as unknown and excludes them from the denominator.
confirmed.impact: A DB migrated from v2 reports "no verdict" for every pre-v3 run even though its authoritative alert row exists, and the metric script silently drops those runs from the measured population after an upgrade.
confirmed.fix: Backfill runs.final_* in the v3 migration from the newest Authoritative alert per run, or make every consumer fall back explicitly and report how many runs used the fallback.

verification.reason: The cited migration does exactly what the claim says: schema.rs:697-711 is a loop of `ALTER TABLE runs ADD COLUMN` over the five final_* fields, with no UPDATE/backfill, and the surrounding doc comment (schema.rs:690-696) even states that the phase-2 authoritative alert already lived in `responsibility_alerts` at that time, so the data needed for a backfill exists. Nothing later fills the gap: the ladder (schema.rs:725-738) is the only migration entry point, `verify_readable_schema`/`open_responsibility_db_read_only` (schema.rs:1190-1217) accept any version <= 3 without migrating, and only the live runtime emits `PersistRecord::RunFinalVerdict` (runtime.rs:1943 -> writer.rs:463-490), so pre-v3 rows are never given a verdict. Consumer side matches the claim: web.rs:892-912 selects `WHERE final_decision IS NOT NULL` and returns None otherwise (schema.rs:504-511 confirms the base DDL has no such column, so a version-2 DB also fails the prepare and yields None), and reader.rs:287-327 only tolerates missing *columns* (injecting NULLs) rather than deriving a verdict from alerts. The one attempted fallback, fpr_runner.py:158-179, is dead code: `stats` is pre-initialized with the key `final_decision` at line 112, so the guard `if "final_decision" not in stats` at line 169 can never be true, meaning the authoritative-alert fallback never runs. final_verdict_metrics.py:53-56,65-66 then drops those rows from `decided`/`n`. The only overstatement in the claim is the word "silently": the script does emit a stderr WARNING and reports `unknown_verdict` (final_verdict_metrics.py:164-178), and a fixture with exactly this shape (authoritative alert, no final column) exists at frontend/public/data/db-sample.sqlite. Core defect and impact stand; I found no code path that backfills or falls back for migrated runs, so medium severity is appropriate.

confirmed.title: GenAI export writes a partial, world-readable file
confirmed.evidence: write_jsonl uses std::fs::File::create(path) and streams spans directly to the destination (genai.rs:124-138); there is no temp-file-plus-rename and no permission handling, so the file receives umask-derived permissions (typically 0644) and an error mid-write leaves a truncated JSONL. The capture DB deliberately chmods artifacts to 0600 for the same data class (schema.rs:1087, 1130-1145).
confirmed.impact: With --include-content the export carries alert titles, summaries and reasoning (post-redaction) in a file readable by every local user, and a failed export is indistinguishable from a complete one to any consumer of the JSONL.
confirmed.fix: Write via OpenOptions with mode(0o600) to a temp file in the destination directory and rename it into place only after a successful flush.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what the claim reports. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/export/genai.rs, write_jsonl is defined at line 124 and line 129 opens the destination with `std::fs::File::create(path)` wrapped in a BufWriter; lines 131-136 then serialize each span directly and only call `flush()` at the end. There is no OpenOptions/mode call, no temp-file-plus-rename, and no fs::set_permissions anywhere in the export module; grep over collector/src confirms the only chmod/mode(0o600) sites are elsewhere (schema.rs:1087/1130-1145, file_logger.rs:26-33, etc.), so this path is genuinely unprotected. File::create creates with 0o666 masked by the process umask, i.e. typically 0644, matching the claim. The claim's second half also holds: on any serialization or write error the `?` at lines 132-133 returns Err after earlier lines have already been committed, leaving a truncated but otherwise well-formed JSONL prefix with no sentinel, and main.rs:806 calls this directly with the user-supplied `--out` path (CLI definition at main.rs:371-381), so no caller-side atomicity or permission handling compensates. The schema.rs comparison is accurate: the capture DB explicitly restricts itself and its WAL/SHM sidecars to 0600 for the same data class (schema.rs:1082-1087 comment about umask 0644, 1130-1145 restrict_file_permissions), while the export that can carry alert title/summary/reasoning via --include-content (genai.rs:102-108) does not. I found no mitigating path: the only other write_jsonl caller is a test at genai.rs:496, tempfile is used only in tests, and the content is opt-in and redacted but the finding itself already acknowledges post-redaction. Medium severity is defensible given the opt-in requirement and redaction; I keep it.

confirmed.title: export-genai exports every run and both phases although the CLI contract is one run's alerts
confirmed.evidence: run_export_genai calls reader.get_alerts_all() (main.rs:800), while the subcommand is documented as "Export a run's responsibility alerts" (main.rs:370). get_alerts_all has no run or phase filter (reader.rs:406-416) and GenAiSpan has no run_id attribute (genai.rs:53-121).
confirmed.impact: On a database holding more than one run (possible via main.rs:1529), a single JSONL mixes provisional and authoritative alerts from different runs with no attribute identifying the run, and nothing marks which alert is the canonical verdict — the exact ambiguity schema v3 was introduced to remove.
confirmed.fix: Accept/require a run id (or resolve it like the alerts endpoint), export only that run's alerts, and add mtl.gen_ai.run.id plus the runs.final_* verdict as span attributes.

verification.reason: The claim is code-accurate on every cited point. The CLI help at collector/src/main.rs:370 literally says "Export a run's responsibility alerts as content-free GenAI spans (JSONL)", yet the ExportGenai variant (main.rs:371-380) accepts only --db/--out/--include-content — there is no run selector — and run_export_genai (main.rs:791-808) calls reader.get_alerts_all() at line 800. That reader method (collector/src/responsibility/persistence/reader.rs:406-417) issues "SELECT ... FROM responsibility_alerts ORDER BY timestamp_ns DESC" with no run_id, phase, or other WHERE clause, so one invocation returns every alert of every run. GenAiSpan (collector/src/export/genai.rs:46-55) has only scope/name/timestamp/attributes/content, and alert_span (genai.rs:53-121) inserts mtl.gen_ai.alert.id/decision/severity/authority/display_profile/confidence, primary_agent.id, agent/graph/timeline counts, and a phase string, but no run id and no runs.final_* verdict; ResponsibilityAlert itself (collector/src/responsibility/types/alert_types.rs:73-99) carries no run_id, so the information is not even available to the span builder. Multi-run accumulation in one DB is real: main.rs:1529 derives the DB path from --log-file (default "system.log", main.rs:352), runtime.rs:366 mints a fresh Uuid::new_v4() run per runtime start, and writer.rs:440 uses INSERT OR IGNORE INTO runs with no purge path (no DELETE FROM runs in persistence/), so repeated collector starts against the same log file leave several runs and both provisional/authoritative alerts (phase column, provisional_ref) in one DB. The snapshot's own GAP-REGISTER ARCH-06 records that the REST /alerts path was fixed to resolve a run id and return 409 ambiguous_run rather than mix runs via get_alerts_all, showing mixing is treated as a defect in this codebase — export-genai never received the equivalent. The only nuance, which does not refute the claim, is that main.rs:1529 is the DB-path derivation rather than the run insert, and the help text could alternatively be read as the buggy side; either way the documented one-run contract and the whole-DB implementation disagree, and the proposed fix (require/resolve a run id, filter, and add run id plus runs.final_* attributes) addresses the real gap.

confirmed.title: The writer stats/chmods both WAL sidecars once per record
confirmed.evidence: restrict_sqlite_sidecars(&db_path) (schema.rs:1160-1181, two metadata calls plus a possible set_permissions) is called at the top of the writer loop (writer.rs:376-379), and that loop iterates once per PersistRecord.
confirmed.impact: Two or more filesystem syscalls per captured event on the single writer task, for sidecars whose mode does not change, competing with the SQLite writes that task exists to perform during a high-rate capture.
confirmed.fix: Check the sidecars once per batch commit (or on a low-frequency timer) instead of once per record.

verification.reason: The code says exactly what the claim says. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/persistence/writer.rs:376 the `loop {` begins, and line 379 calls `super::schema::restrict_sqlite_sidecars(&db_path)` before the `tokio::select!` at line 384; the select receives at most one `PersistRecord` per iteration (`rec = rx.recv()`), every record arm (`Flush` at 416, `RunStart` at 429, `RunRecord` at 499, `Process` at 568, ... through `IdentityMapping` at 1043) then falls back to the top of the loop, so the call runs once per persisted record (and once more per timer tick via the `continue` at line 410). The callee /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/persistence/schema.rs:1160-1177 loops over ["-wal","-shm"], doing one `std::fs::metadata` (line 1166) per sidecar and a conditional `set_permissions` (line 1170) only when `mode() & 0o077 != 0`. So on the Linux target this is two stat syscalls per record, plus any needed chmod, executed on the single writer task that exists to perform the SQLite writes — matching the claim's evidence and impact. It is not handled or cached elsewhere: the only other call site is schema.rs:1088 (one-shot at open), and nothing in writer_task memoizes the check, so sidecars created lazily after open are the stated motivation but the per-record repetition is real. The claim is accurate; severity low is appropriate since the syscalls are cheap and the chmod rarely fires, but the redundant hot-path work is genuine.

confirmed.title: Corrupt decision_provenance_json silently reads as no provenance
confirmed.evidence: map_run_record does serde_json::from_str::<Vec<String>>(&raw).ok().unwrap_or_default() (reader.rs:323-325), whereas every other JSON column goes through deser_json/deser_required, which returns an error for corrupt data (reader.rs:31-55) as the module explicitly requires (reader.rs:48-50). The writer also silently substitutes an empty string on serialization failure (writer.rs:481).
confirmed.impact: A corrupt or future-version runs.decision_provenance_json is reported as an empty provenance list instead of an error, so get_run/list_runs present an audit trail whose reasons are silently missing.
confirmed.fix: Use deser_json(&raw, "decision_provenance") and drop the writer's unwrap_or_default so both directions fail loudly.

verification.reason: The cited code says exactly what the claim reports. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/responsibility/persistence/reader.rs, the deserialization helpers are defined at lines 31-42 (deser_required, which maps parse failures to rusqlite::Error::FromSqlConversionFailure) and 44-55 (deser_json, whose comment at lines 48-50 states "Anything else must parse: a corrupt value is an error, never an empty structure"). map_run_record at lines 310-327 nevertheless reads decision_provenance_json as an Option<String> and converts it with `serde_json::from_str::<Vec<String>>(&raw).ok()` then `.unwrap_or_default()` at lines 323-325, so both a NULL and an unparseable non-empty value collapse to an empty Vec<String>; this is the only raw `serde_json::from_str` call in the file outside the helper (grep found only line 32 and line 324). The path is live: run_record_columns includes decision_provenance_json at line 303 when v3 columns exist, and both get_run (lines 329-343) and list_runs (lines 345-356) pass rows through map_run_record, so no other layer re-validates it (repo-wide grep shows the column is only touched in reader.rs, writer.rs, schema.rs, and a test at runtime.rs:2523). The asymmetry is real and unexcused by any comment or test: reader.rs:953-983 asserts that corrupt JSON surfaces as an error for involved_agents, and reader.rs:985-1005 does the same for graph_nodes.resource_json, but no test covers provenance, and RunRecord.decision_provenance (replay_types.rs:25-26) is a plain Vec<String> with no documented "empty means unknown" contract. The writer half is also accurate: writer.rs:481 uses `serde_json::to_string(&verdict.provenance).unwrap_or_default()`, which on failure writes an empty string, whereas the surrounding writer columns (e.g. writer.rs:623, 647, 668, 819-824) substitute valid JSON literals such as "[]"/"{}" instead, and the column has no SQL default (schema.rs:703 adds it as bare TEXT), so an empty string would be read back as "no provenance". The defect is genuine, though low severity: serde_json serialization of Vec<String> is effectively infallible, and the column is only ever written by that one UPDATE, so corruption would require an external writer or a future format change; the read-side impact is limited to get_run/list_runs presenting an empty provenance list instead of an error.

confirmed.title: Health/readiness endpoints are never wired to the pipeline and can never report ready
confirmed.evidence: start_web_server_if_enabled always constructs `WebServer::with_channels(event_sender, log_file, alert_tx, None)` (main.rs:1869). `WebServer::with_health_state` and `HealthState::new` have no callers anywhere in collector/src or collector/tests, and `HealthState.ready` is initialized to false (web.rs:40-50) and never assigned. Consequently serve_ready always returns 503 (web.rs:1716-1745) and serve_health always returns `status: degraded` with "no StageMetrics producer is wired" (web.rs:1801-1813), regardless of pipeline activity.
confirmed.impact: Readiness probes never pass after startup and `/health` permanently reports Degraded, so operators/CI cannot distinguish a healthy collector from a broken one; the documented per-stage metrics can never appear. scripts/e2e/live-server-smoke.sh only checks that /health answers HTTP 200, so the dead wiring is invisible to tests.
confirmed.fix: Create one Arc<Mutex<HealthState>> in the runtime (populate stage metrics and set ready on the first processed event) and pass it through start_web_server_if_enabled; otherwise delete /health and /ready so monitoring is not deliberately misled.

verification.reason: I could not refute the claim: the wiring really is dead. `/tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/main.rs:1869` is the sole `WebServer::` construction site in the entire tree and it calls `WebServer::with_channels(event_sender, log_file, alert_tx, None)`, so `health_state` is always `None`. A repo-wide grep for `HealthState` finds only definitions/uses inside `collector/src/server/web.rs` (struct at :34, `HealthState::new` at :43-50, the `with_health_state` wrapper at :102-107) — no caller in `collector/src` or `collector/tests`; the only other construction path, `WebServer::new`, forwards `None` at web.rs:77. `HealthState.ready` is initialized `false` (web.rs:48) and is never assigned anywhere (the only `ready =`/`ready:` hits are unrelated). Consequently the routes at web.rs:287 and :293 always pass `None` into `serve_ready`/`serve_health`: `serve_ready` unconditionally returns 503 with reason "no StageMetrics producer is wired" (web.rs:1716-1745), and `serve_health` unconditionally returns `HealthStatus::Degraded` with warning "pipeline metrics unavailable: no StageMetrics producer is wired" and an empty `stages` map (web.rs:1767-1813) — served via `json_response`, which hard-codes HTTP 200 (web.rs:1855-1861), exactly as the claim's smoke-test note describes (`scripts/e2e/live-server-smoke.sh:46` only checks that `/health` answers successfully). No `StageMetrics` producer exists elsewhere either. I downgrade severity from high to medium because the collector's core pipeline is unaffected and no in-repo deployment manifest uses `/ready`, so the defect is a permanently misleading observability surface rather than a data-path or crash bug — but it is real and the dead endpoints do advertise metrics they can never deliver.

confirmed.title: Server reads a run-summary schema no producer writes (scenario_ids/state/run_status)
confirmed.evidence: run_summary_value reads summary["scenario_ids"] (web.rs:916-920), summary["status"|"run_status"|"state"] (web.rs:922-931) and summary["artifacts"][key] (web.rs:1651-1669). The benchmark producer writes the singular `scenario_id`, a boolean `success`, and `database_path`, with no state/status/artifacts key (env/src/mtagentlens_benchmark/engine/runner.py:76-90); its runs_dir is exactly the `env/runs` directory /api/runs scans (workspace.py:129, web.rs:506-511).
confirmed.impact: Every archived benchmark run is served with `scenario_ids: []` and `state`/`run_status: "unknown"`. The UI run selector falls back to a timestamp prefix instead of the scenario id (frontend/components/system/run-selector.tsx:52-54), and no run can ever be reported completed/running from its summary. artifact_availability for the DB is only correct because of the path-convention fallback, not the declared artifact.
confirmed.fix: Normalize in run_summary_value: accept `scenario_id`/`scenario_ids`, map `success` to state, and accept `database_path`/`collector_output` alongside the artifacts map; or make the producer emit the server schema.

verification.reason: The schema mismatch is exactly as claimed. In /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/server/web.rs:914-931, run_summary_value reads only summary["scenario_ids"] (915-918) and summary["status"|"run_status"|"state"] (919-928), defaulting to [] and "unknown"; web.rs:544 (/api/runs) and web.rs:885 (/api/run) both funnel through it. The benchmark producer env/src/mtagentlens_benchmark/engine/runner.py:76-90 writes run_id, scenario_id (singular), success, duration_seconds, database_path and error, merged with executor summaries that contain only agents_succeeded/agents_total/clean_profile/collector_health (executor.py:408-413, 532-538, 253-260) — no scenario_ids/state/status/artifacts. workspace.py:129 sets runs_dir = root/"runs" (i.e., env/runs), which is precisely what web.rs:505-511 scans, and runner.py is reached from cli.py:59,88, so every archived benchmark run is served with scenario_ids: [] and unknown state. web.rs:1552-1579 and 1650-1669 confirm artifact availability resolves the DB by naming convention because summary["artifacts"]["responsibility_db"] is never emitted, and frontend/components/system/run-selector.tsx:53 confirms the run_id.slice(0,12) label fallback. The only counterexample, scripts/generate-summaries.py:29-33 (which writes scenario_ids/state), is an unwired one-off that skips any directory already containing summary.json (line 14), so it never covers runner-produced runs; I found no caller for it. Severity is adjusted to medium: the mismatch is universal and contract-breaking, but the UI degrades gracefully (labels fall back, artifacts load via path conventions), no archived-run consumer depends on state except /api/runs/active, which benchmark runs never populate, and there is no crash or data loss.

confirmed.title: Summary final verdict and start time come from an arbitrary run in multi-run databases
confirmed.evidence: read_final_verdict executes `SELECT final_decision, ... FROM runs WHERE final_decision IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1` with no run filter and no ORDER BY (web.rs:892-910), and started_at_ns uses `SELECT started_at_ns FROM runs ORDER BY started_at_ns DESC LIMIT 1` (web.rs:934-945). The code itself documents that reusing `-o <log>` appends a second run to the same DB (web.rs:1079-1082), and the alerts endpoint explicitly refuses to mix runs in that case (web.rs:1479-1492).
confirmed.impact: For a DB holding several runs, GET /api/runs/{id} can report another run's final verdict and another run's start time as this run's — a wrong safety verdict attributed to a run, which is exactly what the 409 logic in /alerts exists to prevent.
confirmed.fix: Resolve the directory to the DB run UUID with the same policy used by serve_alerts_from_db and filter both queries by that run_id (409 when ambiguous).

verification.reason: The code says exactly what the claim reports. `read_final_verdict` (web.rs:892-912) opens the resolved responsibility DB and runs `SELECT final_decision, final_severity, final_authority, final_alert_id FROM runs WHERE final_decision IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1` at web.rs:900-901, taking the first row at web.rs:905 — there is no `run_id` predicate and no `ORDER BY`, so the row is whichever one SQLite scans first (in practice oldest rowid, i.e. the oldest run with a verdict). The start time at web.rs:929-942 runs `SELECT started_at_ns FROM runs ORDER BY started_at_ns DESC LIMIT 1` with no filter, so it is the newest run's start time. Both values are written unconditionally into the summary payload at web.rs:968 and 975, and `run_summary_value` is reached from `serve_run_summary_api` (web.rs:860-885), which is called by the `GET /api/runs/{id}` route at web.rs:331-332 and by the `/api/runs` index loop at web.rs:544; nothing falls back to summary.json for these two fields. Multi-run DBs are a real, documented case here: web.rs:1079-1086 notes that reusing `-o <log>` appends a second run to the same database and therefore filters `graph_snapshots` by `run_id`, while the alerts path explicitly resolves the directory to a DB run UUID and returns 409 `ambiguous_run` rather than mixing runs (web.rs:1477-1511). Verdicts are persisted per run (`UPDATE runs ... WHERE run_id = ?6`, writer.rs:482-493), so an older run's non-NULL `final_decision` remains in the table and can be the row `LIMIT 1` returns. `runs` is a plain table (schema.rs:504), not a view with a hidden filter, so there is no other place this is handled. Thus for a DB with several runs the summary endpoint can attribute another run's final safety verdict and another run's start time to the requested run — internally inconsistent and exactly the mix-up the alerts 409 guards against. The claim's "arbitrary" wording is fair (SQLite gives no order guarantee here), and the proposed fix (resolve the DB run UUID like `serve_alerts_from_db` and filter both queries, 409 on ambiguity) is the right shape.

confirmed.title: DB-backed snapshot/graph/evidence endpoints resolve the newest run instead of the requested one
confirmed.evidence: Collector run ids are UUIDs (collector/src/responsibility/runtime/runtime.rs:366) while run directories are named `<timestamp>-<hex>` (env/src/mtagentlens_benchmark/engine/runner.py:33), so the `WHERE run_id = ?` queries keyed on the directory name in serve_snapshots_from_db (web.rs:1102-1130) and serve_graph_from_db (web.rs:1215-1240) never match real rows. serve_graph_from_db then falls back to resolve_db_run_id (web.rs:1286-1291), which returns reader.list_runs().first() — the newest run per reader.rs:345-352 — and serve_evidence_from_db does the same unconditionally (web.rs:1332-1337). Only serve_alerts_from_db performs the directory→UUID mapping and 409s on ambiguity (web.rs:1479-1492).
confirmed.impact: In a DB containing more than one run, /evidence and the /graph node/edge fallback silently return the newest run's data for any requested run, while /snapshots returns an empty array. Cross-run evidence/graphs can thus be displayed under the wrong run id.
confirmed.fix: Extract the alerts run-resolution policy (one run → accept; exact UUID match → accept; otherwise 409) into a shared helper and use it in snapshots, graph and evidence.

verification.reason: I re-read every cited location and could not refute the claim. The premise holds: collector run ids are fresh UUIDs written by init_session (runtime.rs:366-370, INSERT OR IGNORE INTO runs at writer.rs:440), while benchmark run directories are named `<timestamp>-<uuid4hex12>` (runner.py:33), and the web layer passes `run_dir.file_name()` as the requested id (web.rs:1055, 1069-1172, 1186-1189). The alerts regression test at web.rs:2697-2715 encodes exactly this mismatch (dir `20260716-020833-690cf50f` vs DB run `89de8320-29b7-4297-a5c3-fb89c5f3fb5e`), so the mismatch is not hypothetical. serve_snapshots_from_db filters `WHERE run_id = ?1` with the directory name (web.rs:1083-1101) and only relaxes the filter when `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM runs` is <= 1 (web.rs:1109-1130), so a 2+ run DB yields an empty array. serve_graph_from_db likewise filters by the directory name (web.rs:1213-1234), refuses the unfiltered snapshot query when runs > 1 (web.rs:1237-1257), and then, when no snapshot matched, calls resolve_db_run_id (web.rs:1286-1291), which returns `reader.list_runs()?.first()` (web.rs:1309-1319); list_runs is `ORDER BY started_at_ns DESC` (reader.rs:344-352), i.e. the newest run, whose graph is returned by `get_graph` (web.rs:1291-1304). serve_evidence_from_db calls resolve_db_run_id unconditionally (web.rs:1332-1337) and then keys all four tables on that newest id (web.rs:1337-1352). By contrast serve_alerts_from_db builds the full id set and returns 409 `ambiguous_run` when the request matches none of >1 runs (web.rs:1479-1512), with a test proving two-run filtering and the 409 (web.rs:2749-2816 and 2750-2821). The only mitigation is that normal per-scenario collector output directories (collector_manager.py:666-669, 845) hold a single run, and docs/superpowers/HANDOFF-2026-10-19-REVISION.md records 301/301 real DBs as single-run; the multi-run DB arises when an output log is reused, a case the code itself says must "never be mixed" (web.rs:1237-1239, 1079-1082). The defect is therefore real but conditional on a multi-run database, so I would rate it medium rather than high; the proposed shared alerts-style resolution helper is the right fix.

confirmed.title: Subroute HTML is served with a one-year immutable cache
confirmed.evidence: serve_asset chooses the cache header from the request string: only paths ending in `.html` or equal to `/` get `no-cache`, everything else gets `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (web.rs:412-418). FrontendAssets::resolve_path serves `/overview` from `overview/index.html` or `overview.html` (assets.rs:74-86), so every Next.js static page except `/` is HTML delivered with an immutable one-year cache.
confirmed.impact: After an upgrade, browsers keep the old HTML routing shell for up to a year — the exact failure the adjacent comment claims this code prevents — so deleted or renamed routes keep rendering stale pages.
confirmed.fix: Decide caching from the resolved file (HTML content type or resolved filename ending in .html), not from the raw request path.

verification.reason: The claim is accurate. At collector/src/server/web.rs:414 the cache policy is chosen from the raw request path: `path.ends_with(".html") || path == "/"` yields `no-cache`, and every other path gets `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (lines 412-418). The request path reaches this function unmodified: handle_request takes `req.uri().path()` at line 255 and the catch-all `(&Method::GET, _) => serve_asset(assets, path, false)` at line 363 (HEAD at 365) forwards it verbatim; there is no redirect, rewrite, or path normalization to `.html` anywhere in the file (no 301/302/LOCATION logic exists). On the resolution side, assets.rs:74-95 builds candidates `[serve_dir/<path>, serve_dir/<path>/index.html, serve_dir/<path>.html]` whenever the path has no dot, so `/overview`, `/console`, `/traces`, `/investigations`, etc. are served from the corresponding `.html` file while the cache branch sees a path with no `.html` suffix. The app genuinely has these subroutes (frontend/app/(main)/{overview,console,traces,investigations}/page.tsx) and the UI links to them extensionless (e.g. router.push('/console') in components/live/live-status-bar.tsx:45, Link href="/overview" in components/investigation/investigation-workbench.tsx:643), so a hard load, refresh, bookmark, or fresh tab of any non-root page hits `/overview` rather than `/overview.html`. Consequently those HTML routing shells are stored for a year without revalidation, which is exactly the upgrade failure the comment at web.rs:411-413 claims to prevent; the fix should key off the resolved file (resolved filename ends in .html or the resolved MIME is text/html), not the request string. The same flaw also applies to static-export RSC payloads (e.g. `/overview.txt`), but that does not weaken the claimed HTML issue. Severity medium (not higher) is appropriate: it affects client-side cache freshness after an upgrade, not data integrity or security.

confirmed.title: /api/runs/{id}/events looks for a trace artifact the benchmark never writes
confirmed.evidence: resolve_events_artifact_path checks only summary.artifacts.trace_log and `<run>/trace.log` (web.rs:1670-1681). The benchmark starts the collector with output_dir `<run>/collector` and log_file `collector` (executor.py:102,117; collector_manager.py:634,711), producing `<run>/collector/collector` (JSONL) and `<run>/collector/collector.responsibility.db`; its summary records `collector_output`/`database_path`, not `trace_log` (executor.py:256, runner.py:84).
confirmed.impact: For every archived benchmark run, /api/runs/{id}/events returns 404 artifact_unavailable and `artifact_availability.events` is false, so the documented run-scoped event endpoint cannot serve real data; only the live route works, because it uses the configured log path directly.
confirmed.fix: Add `<run>/collector/collector` and the summary's `collector_output` to artifact resolution, keeping `<run>/trace.log` for legacy archives.

verification.reason: Confirmed, with the claim's mechanism verified end to end and one minor detail corrected. resolve_events_artifact_path (web.rs:1670-1681) tries only resolve_artifact_from_summary(run_dir, "trace_log") and then `<run>/trace.log`; resolve_artifact_from_summary (web.rs:1652-1668) requires a top-level `artifacts` object in summary.json. serve_run_events_api (web.rs:1373-1381) returns 404 `artifact_unavailable` when this returns None, and run_summary_value reports `artifact_availability.events` from the same function (web.rs:981). Benchmark runs are exactly what /api/runs indexes (`env/runs/<id>`, web.rs:503-544), and runner._save_summary (runner.py:75-88) writes summary.json with only run_id/scenario_id/success/duration_seconds/database_path/error — no `artifacts` key (and in fact no collector_output either; that field only exists in RunResult at executor.py:256), so the summary lookup always fails. executor.py:102 creates `<run>/collector`, executor.py:117 calls collector.start(collector_dir), and collector_manager.py:664-669/711 passes `-o <run>/collector/collector` (stderr goes to collector.log), so the JSONL stream lands at `<run>/collector/collector`. Real archives confirm it: /home/lzk/MtAgentLens/env/runs/20261020-220340-cfb6530f177a/collector/collector is a 930-line JSONL event stream, its summary.json has no `artifacts`, and no `<run>/trace.log` exists. Decisively, the sibling resolver resolve_responsibility_db_path (web.rs:1552-1571) explicitly handles the nested `<run>/collector/collector.responsibility.db` layout (with a dedicated test at web.rs:2380-2397), but events resolution has no analogous nested fallback — so the live route works via the configured path (web.rs:800-820) while every archived run's event endpoint 404s. Only inaccuracy: the claim says the summary records `collector_output`; it does not (runner.py only records database_path). Severity medium stands: a documented endpoint is completely non-functional for archived runs, though the data is present on disk and other endpoints (db/alerts) still work.

confirmed.title: lean=1 is ignored for the live run, returning full graph snapshots
confirmed.evidence: handle_request parses `lean=1` (web.rs:255-261) but only passes it on the archived-run branch (web.rs:335-337). The live branch calls serve_live_resource (web.rs:326-327), which hardcodes `lean = false` for alerts (web.rs:844). frontend/lib/store.ts:362 requests `/api/runs/${id}/alerts?lean=1` for the active run, so when the DB download path fails the client receives every alert including its full graph_snapshot.
confirmed.impact: The megabyte-scale payload the parameter was introduced to avoid (web.rs:255-257) is transferred for exactly the high-frequency live run and then stripped client-side (store.ts:366-367).
confirmed.fix: Thread the parsed `lean` flag through serve_live_resource into serve_alerts_from_db instead of hardcoding false.

verification.reason: The claim's mechanics hold up exactly. `handle_request` parses `lean_alerts` from the query at web.rs:258-261 (the comment at 255-257 explicitly says the parameter exists to avoid transferring megabytes of graph snapshots), but the only consumer is the archived-run branch at web.rs:336 (`serve_alerts_api(&run_dir, ..., lean_alerts)`). The live branch at web.rs:326-327 calls `serve_live_resource(run_route.resource, log_file.as_deref())` with no lean argument, and `serve_live_resource` hardcodes it at web.rs:844: `RunResource::Alerts => serve_alerts_from_db(&db_path, LIVE_RUN_ID, false).await`. `grep -n lean` finds no other occurrence between 255 and 1520, so nothing re-applies the flag later. The live run id is "live" (web.rs:770) and `live_run_summary_value` returns exactly that (web.rs:~809), so `/api/runs/active` yields a run id that routes into the live branch. The frontend call the claim cites is substantively right: store.ts:362 calls `api.getAlerts(runId)`, and api.ts:99 defines `getAlerts` as `/api/runs/${id}/alerts?lean=1` (the literal string lives in api.ts, not store.ts:362, but the request is the one described); the client then strips `graph_snapshot` at store.ts:365-367 after the full payload has crossed the wire. One correction on reachability/impact: the lean request is only reached on the fallback after `getRunDb` throws or `loadDatabaseFromBytes` reports `hasConsumableData == false` (store.ts:348-362), and live-session's resync deliberately uses `getAlertsFull` (live-session.ts:386), so this is not a high-frequency live path — it is a rarely-taken fallback. Also, `serve_alerts_from_db` (web.rs:1520-1536) does honor lean by replacing each row's `graph_snapshot` with an empty placeholder, so threading the parsed flag through `serve_live_resource` (the proposed fix) is correct and sufficient. The defect is real but its cost is bounded to a fallback path, hence the severity adjustment.

confirmed.title: SSE event ids restart per connection and Last-Event-ID is never honored
confirmed.evidence: live_event_stream creates its shared AtomicU64 inside each call (live_sse.rs:93), so every reconnect restarts ids at 1, while the module documents a global monotonic sequence usable for reconnect gap detection (live_sse.rs:23-24, 82-84). web.rs:217-231 never reads the Last-Event-ID header and subscribes a fresh broadcast receiver, so events produced while disconnected are lost without a lag frame; the frontend uses e.lastEventId as the raw-event id (live-session.ts:204) and only resyncs alerts on open (live-session.ts:227-231).
confirmed.impact: Raw-event ids collide after every reconnect (rows in live-event-tail.tsx:57-91 are keyed by id, so unrelated rows can expand together and follow-scroll can stall), replayed/queued events are silently dropped, and the advertised reconnect/resume capability does not exist.
confirmed.fix: Own the sequence counter above the connection (process-wide AtomicU64), honor Last-Event-ID with a bounded replay buffer, and emit an explicit reset or lag event when history is unavailable; also resync raw events like alerts.

verification.reason: I could not refute the claim; every element checks out in the snapshot. In `/tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/server/live_sse.rs`, `live_event_stream` constructs `Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0))` at line 93 inside the per-request function, so both branches restart at 0 and emit ids beginning at "1" (lines 97 and 110-113), directly contradicting the module's own contract at lines 23-24 ("单调递增事件 id（客户端断线重连用）") and 82-84 ("共享 `AtomicU64` ... 全局单调序列 ... 客户端断线重连可据此判断缺口"). `serve_live_events_api` (web.rs:217-231, dispatched with no request headers at web.rs:190, only Host/method checked at 155-189) never reads `Last-Event-ID` and calls `event_sender.subscribe()` / `s.subscribe()` fresh, so a broadcast receiver only observes events published after subscription — disconnected-window events disappear and no replay or resume-gap frame is possible (the only `lag` frame comes from `BroadcastStreamRecvError::Lagged`, live_sse.rs:100-102/116-118). A repo-wide grep for `last-event-id|Last-Event-ID|lastEventId` finds no backend handling. On the client, `live-session.ts:204` stores `e.lastEventId` as the row `id` (described as "后端单调 seq（重连去重用）" in live-types.ts:35-36), yet `resync()` (live-session.ts:168-178) fetches only alerts and is invoked solely from `onopen` (227-231); raw events are never resynced, and `resetRawEvents()` is called only on run switch/end (live-session.ts:145, 280), not on reconnect, while `pushRawEvents` (live-raw-events.ts:21-29) performs no id deduplication. Rows are keyed on `id` for expand state and follow-scroll (live-event-tail.tsx:57, 79, 86), so post-reconnect ids that collide with still-buffered pre-reconnect ids can toggle unrelated rows and produce a stale scroll dependency. The impact is mainly UI corruption/duplicate keys plus silent loss of events across reconnects rather than data corruption, so medium severity is appropriate and does not need adjustment.

confirmed.title: Advertised loopback MTAGENTLENS_BIND values cannot be parsed into a socket address
confirmed.evidence: main.rs:1858-1866 only warns for values other than 127.0.0.1/::1/localhost, then does `format!("{host}:{port}").parse::<SocketAddr>()`. SocketAddr::from_str performs no DNS resolution, so `localhost:7395` fails, and `::1:7395` is unbracketed and also fails; host_is_allowed (web.rs:379-395) explicitly treats `localhost` and `::1` as valid loopback binds.
confirmed.impact: `MTAGENTLENS_BIND=localhost --server` or `MTAGENTLENS_BIND=::1 --server` aborts startup with "Invalid server address" even though both values are documented/accepted as loopback-safe.
confirmed.fix: Resolve the host (ToSocketAddrs) or special-case/bracket IPv6 before parsing; reject unsupported values explicitly at argument validation time.

verification.reason: The cited code is accurate. main.rs:1858 reads MTAGENTLENS_BIND, and main.rs:1859-1862 deliberately exempts 127.0.0.1, ::1, and localhost from the non-loopback warning, marking them as intended-safe values; main.rs:1864-1866 then does `format!("{host}:{port}").parse()` and maps any error to "Invalid server address". The parse target is `std::net::SocketAddr` because `WebServer::start` takes `addr: SocketAddr` (server/web.rs:110-112), and `SocketAddr::from_str` accepts only IP-literal forms (no DNS, IPv6 bracketed), so `localhost:7395` cannot parse, and `::1:7395` is not a valid SocketAddr spelling either. The same assumption appears in server/web.rs:380-395, where `host_is_allowed` treats `localhost`/`::1` as loopback-safe binds, with tests at web.rs:1956-1957 asserting Host headers localhost:7395 and [::1]:7395 are allowed. The failure is not handled elsewhere: but this is not a false alarm; the parse error propagates through callers at main.rs:1049-1057 (and 1124-1132, 1259-1267, 1710, 1814) as RunnerError and out of main (main.rs:425), aborting startup. Only severity warrants adjustment: the failure is loud and immediate, affects a non-default env-var opt-in, and has a trivial workaround (127.0.0.1), with no security or data consequence.

confirmed.title: /api/scenarios scans only the top level and is always empty on the real tree
confirmed.evidence: serve_scenarios_index_api iterates only direct entries of `env/scenarios` and skips directories (web.rs:559-615). This repository has zero JSON files at env/scenarios top level; all scenarios are nested (e.g. env/scenarios/prompt_injection/prompt-injection.json), so the endpoint returns []. Its tests pass only because the fixture writes metadata flat (web.rs:2214-2231). No frontend, script or doc consumer of /api/scenarios exists.
confirmed.impact: The scenarios index endpoint can never return real scenarios, yet its tests give false confidence; it also adds an unauthenticated filesystem scan with no consumer.
confirmed.fix: Walk the scenario tree recursively (or read the workspace's scenario manifest), and remove the endpoint if nothing consumes it.

verification.reason: The code says exactly what is claimed. web.rs:359 routes GET /api/scenarios to serve_scenarios_index_api (web.rs:559). At 561 the directory is current_dir()/env/scenarios; 570-575 read_dir's it non-recursively; 576-579 `if !path.is_file() || ... != "json" { continue; }` skips every directory, and only then reads `id`/`description` (582-597), sorting and returning the array (599-615). The real tree is `ls -la /tmp/mtal-audit/env/scenarios`: 0 regular files and 0 JSON files at top level, only ~40 directories (benign/, prompt_injection/, privilege_escalation/, _drafts/, fixtures/, ...), while `find ... -name '*.json'` returns 528 nested files (e.g. env/scenarios/prompt_injection/prompt-injection.json), so the endpoint returns [] against the shipped tree. Elsewhere the codebase loads scenarios recursively — compare/scripts/run/pilot_observer.py:60, scripts/wire/verify_campaign.py:83-86 and compare/scripts/run/recollect_isolated.py:111 all use rglob — so the flat scan is not an alternate supported layout. The tests do pass for the wrong reason: handle_request_routes_scenarios_index_through_get_path (test call at 2233, second at 2335) relies on write_scenario_metadata/write_raw_scenario_metadata (3483-3497), which write `<id>.json` directly into `repo_root/env/scenarios` and chdir there via RepoRootGuard (3693-3707), i.e. a flat fixture that never occurs in the real tree. Finally, a repo-wide grep for "api/scenarios" matches only web.rs:359, 2233, 2335, 2354 (match_run_route negative assertion) — no frontend, script, or doc consumer exists (no "scenarios" hits in frontend/src), and no docs mention the route. Nothing refutes the claim. I reduce severity to low only because the defect is a dead endpoint returning an empty list rather than wrong data: no consumer can observe incorrect results, and the exposure is an unauthenticated read that yields nothing on the real tree; the real cost is dead code plus tests that give false assurance.

confirmed.title: /api/runs/live returns 404 for the live run whenever the responsibility DB is absent
confirmed.evidence: serve_live_resource requires live_db_path before matching the resource (web.rs:824-834), so RunResource::Summary returns 404 artifact_unavailable even though live_run_summary_value can still build a summary from the trace log (web.rs:786-822). /api/runs/active calls live_run_summary_value directly and returns a running summary in exactly that state (web.rs:302-309).
confirmed.impact: The two endpoints describing the same live run disagree: /api/runs/active reports a running run while /api/runs/live 404s (e.g. before the writer creates the DB, or if the DB is removed while the collector still writes the log).
confirmed.fix: Move the DB requirement into the Alerts/Snapshots/Graph/Evidence/Db branches and let Summary and Events work from the log alone.

verification.reason: The code says exactly what the claim reports. `serve_live_resource` (web.rs:824) obtains `db_path` via `live_db_path(log_file)` and bails with 404 `artifact_unavailable`/"responsibility_db" at web.rs:828-834 before ever matching `resource`, so `RunResource::Summary` (web.rs:836-838) and `RunResource::Events` (web.rs:845-846) can never run without the DB. `live_run_summary_value` (web.rs:788-822) returns `Some` whenever `<log>.responsibility.db` *or* the log file exists (`if db.is_none() && events.is_none() { return None }`), and `/api/runs/active` returns that value directly (web.rs:302-309), so in the log-present/DB-absent state the two endpoints genuinely disagree. I tried to refute reachability and could not: `/api/runs/live` is parsed by `match_run_route` into run_id "live" + Summary (web.rs:654-667) and dispatched to `serve_live_resource` at web.rs:326-327 with no special-case handling elsewhere; `live_events_path` is only consulted after the DB gate. The state is not merely a startup race: the `ssl`, `process`, `stdio`, and `system` commands call `start_web_server_if_enabled(..., Some(log_file), ...)` (main.rs:1049-1056, 1124-1131, 1259-1266, 1804-1811) while `PersistenceWriter::new` — which eagerly creates the DB — is only constructed in the `record`/`trace` path (main.rs:1529-1534). There, `FileLogger::new` has already created the log (file_logger.rs:76-86), so `/api/runs/active` reports a running run with `database:false` while `/api/runs/live` (and `/api/runs/live/events`) 404 forever. Documentation promises the endpoint (docs/architecture.md:297), but no frontend caller uses `/api/runs/live` summary (`getActiveRun` uses `/api/runs/active`, frontend/lib/api.ts:87), so real user impact is limited to Events plus external/scripted clients — severity low is fair.

confirmed.title: p99_latency_us is hardcoded to zero in the health schema
confirmed.evidence: StageMetricsSnapshot::from_stage_metrics sets `p99_latency_us: 0` for every stage (api_types.rs:50) while publishing it as a field of the v1.0.0 health response (api_types.rs:38). StageMetrics has no p99 input at all (collector/src/framework/analyzers/pipeline_contract.rs:606-613).
confirmed.impact: Any consumer of /health would read a measured-looking p99 of 0 µs; latency SLOs or scientific latency reporting built on it would be fabricated (currently masked only because health_state is never wired, see the health finding).
confirmed.fix: Remove p99_latency_us until a latency histogram exists, or compute it from recorded per-event latencies.

verification.reason: I re-read the cited code and could not refute the claim. /tmp/mtal-audit/collector/src/server/api_types.rs:38 declares `pub p99_latency_us: u64` as a field of StageMetricsSnapshot, which is embedded in HealthResponse.stages (api_types.rs:28) and serialized under the canonical HEALTH_SCHEMA_VERSION "v1.0.0" (api_types.rs:17, 22). StageMetricsSnapshot::from_stage_metrics at api_types.rs:44-54 sets `p99_latency_us: 0` literally on line 50 while copying every other field from StageMetrics; the source struct in collector/src/framework/analyzers/pipeline_contract.rs:606-613 has events_processed, events_emitted, errors, avg_latency_us, buffer_size, status — no p99 or latency histogram input. A repo-wide grep for p99_latency/p99_us found only these two occurrences (api_types.rs:38 and :50), so no alternate path computes or overrides the value. The only consumer is serve_health in collector/src/server/web.rs:1767-1800, which inserts `StageMetricsSnapshot::from_stage_metrics(metrics)` verbatim at web.rs:1784 into the response with no post-processing. The impact's caveat is accurate: `with_health_state` (web.rs:102) has no call sites anywhere in the snapshot, so serve_health currently runs the `None` branch (web.rs:1799-1815) with empty stages and a Degraded status, meaning the zero-p99 is latent today — but any future producer of StageMetrics immediately publishes a fabricated measured-looking p99 of 0 µs. This is a genuine hardcoded placeholder in a published schema, not a misreading; the fix (drop the field or compute from real per-event latencies) is appropriate. Severity low is right given the field is currently unreachable in production wiring, so no adjustment.

confirmed.title: EXEC events never carry command arguments: argv block is read with bpf_probe_read_user_str, which stops at the first NUL
confirmed.evidence: handle_exec copies the argv region with bpf_probe_read_user_str(&e->full_command, arg_len + 1, (void *)arg_start) (line 196). mm->arg_start..arg_end is a sequence of NUL-separated argv strings; the _str helper copies one NUL-terminated string, so only argv[0] is copied. The intended loop that replaces interior NULs with spaces (lines 202-205) is therefore dead, and it is bounded by ret-1, i.e. argv[0]'s length. process.h:76 still documents the field as 'full command line with args'. Consumers treat it as the cmdline: collector/src/responsibility/runtime/routing.rs:566-575 sets ProcessExecInfo.cmdline from it, and multi_agent_anomaly.rs:224-234 runs is_suspicious_exec on it.
confirmed.impact: Every EXEC event records only the executable name. A spawn of `bash -c "curl http://evil/x | sh"` is stored as `bash`; URLs, flags and targets (the actual intent) never reach the responsibility graph, evidence extraction or anomaly detection. Processes that differ only by arguments become indistinguishable.
confirmed.fix: Copy the clamped arg_len bytes with bpf_probe_read_user (raw copy, not the _str variant), then replace interior NULs with spaces and terminate at arg_len; add a test fixture that execs a multi-argument command and asserts the arguments survive.

verification.reason: Verified in /tmp/mtal-audit: handle_exec (process.bpf.c:150-212) reads mm->arg_start/arg_end at 186-188, clamps arg_len to MAX_COMMAND_LEN-1=255 (191-192, MAX_COMMAND_LEN defined at process.h:15), then at line 196 calls bpf_probe_read_user_str(&e->full_command, arg_len + 1, (void *)arg_start). That helper is the NUL-terminated variant: it stops at the first NUL, so for the kernel argv layout "bash\0-c\0curl ...\0" only "bash\0" is copied and ret = 5. The intended NUL-to-space loop at 202-205 is bounded by i < ret - 1 (i.e. 4 for "bash"), so it can never reach an interior NUL — the loop is dead, exactly as claimed. The fallback at 199/209 only fires on read failure or arg_len == 0, not here. No other component reconstructs the arguments: grep shows full_command is populated only at 196/199/209, process.c merely prints it verbatim (661, 682), and the only /proc/<pid>/cmdline read in the collector is in an unrelated out-of-band runner (framework/runners/outofband.rs:234). Consumers do treat it as the full cmdline: routing.rs:566-575 maps it to ProcessExecInfo.cmdline (with a comment explicitly asserting the BPF program emits it), signal_snapshot.rs:30-35 documents it as the "strongest runtime-identity signal", and multi_agent_anomaly.rs:224-234 feeds it to is_suspicious_exec (896-911), whose patterns ("curl ", "| sh", "bash -i", "python -c", "rm -rf") can never match a bare argv[0] — so that detection path is entirely dead. process.h:76 and docs (capabilities.json:80, threat-model.md:92) also promise argv, confirming intent. Claim is accurate; severity high is appropriate because the impact is loss of actual intent across responsibility graph, evidence extraction and anomaly detection.

confirmed.title: PID tracker deletion breaks the linear-probing chain, silently un-tracking live processes
confirmed.evidence: pid_tracker_remove only sets entry->is_active = false (line 106), while pid_tracker_find returns NULL at the first slot with !is_active (lines 60-62). Buckets are pid & 2047 (line 32) with linear probing. Example: insert pid 1 (slot 1) then pid 2049 (slot 2); when pid 1 exits, slot 1 is cleared and find(2049) stops at the empty slot 1, so pid 2049 is no longer found. process.c:608 calls pid_tracker_remove on every EXIT event.
confirmed.impact: should_report_file_ops and should_report_network (lines 177-193) then return false for a still-running tracked agent or child, so all of its file and network events are dropped for the rest of the capture, with no counter or warning. In a long run this progressively blinds the collector for exactly the processes it was asked to monitor.
confirmed.fix: Use backward-shift deletion (rehash the probe cluster after the removed slot) or tombstones that remain traversable by pid_tracker_find; add a regression test that inserts colliding PIDs, removes the first, and asserts the second is still found.

verification.reason: I checked bpftools/include/process_filter.h in /tmp/mtal-audit: pid_hash is `pid & 2047` (line 32), pid_tracker_find does linear probing and returns NULL on the first `!is_active` slot (lines 56-62), pid_tracker_add probes to the first empty slot (lines 84-96), and pid_tracker_remove only sets `entry->is_active = false` (lines 101-108) without backward-shift rehash or tombstones. Therefore removing a PID that sits at the head of a probe cluster makes every later entry in that cluster unreachable; e.g. insert 1 (idx 1) then 2049 (idx 2), remove 1, and find(2049) hits the now-empty idx 1 and returns NULL. The call site is real: bpftools/process/process.c:603-608 calls pid_tracker_remove on every EXIT event, and there is no re-population or rebuild afterwards (pid_tracker_init/populate_initial_pids run only once at startup, process.c:774 and 809; no other writer touches the table). The consumers at process_filter.h:176-193 gate file/network events on pid_tracker_is_tracked, and process.c:707-723 drops those events when it returns false, so a live PID whose entry becomes unreachable silently loses all subsequent file/network telemetry, and children stop being tracked too via the parent check at process_filter.h:162. This affects FILTER mode (default when -c/-p is used, and forced by collector/src/main.rs:1206-1208) and PROC mode (the binary's actual default, process.c:68, where all PIDs are inserted and collisions are common), while only FILTER_MODE_ALL is exempt (line 180-182); the existing tests (tests/test_process_filter.c:122-142, 304-330) remove only isolated PIDs and never cover removal of a colliding predecessor, so nothing refutes the defect. Severity high is appropriate: it is silent, progressive loss of exactly the telemetry the collector exists to capture.

confirmed.title: File-open rate limiter silently discards more than 30 opens/sec/pid and never accounts for them
confirmed.evidence: should_rate_limit_file increments distinct_file_count for every open and returns true once it exceeds MAX_DISTINCT_FILES_PER_SEC (30, line 27) (lines 233-239); get_file_open_count then returns 0 (lines 272-275) and handle_event breaks without emitting or recording anything. The warning flag is only consumed when the first event of a later second arrives (lines 224-231), so it is usually never emitted. The counter is applied before dedup, so even repeated opens that aggregation would handle consume the budget.
confirmed.impact: File-open evidence is hard-capped at 30 events/sec/pid; every excess open is discarded and is not included in dropped_events, so a zero dropped_events line does not mean complete capture. Agent workloads that read many files therefore produce a censored resource-access record and biased action/GT counts.
confirmed.fix: Track rate-limited drops per PID and surface them (structured event or PROCESS_RINGBUF_STATS); apply the limiter after dedup or key it on distinct paths; emit the warning on the drop itself rather than on a future event.

verification.reason: Verified in /tmp/mtal-audit/bpftools/process/process.c. MAX_DISTINCT_FILES_PER_SEC is 30 (line 27). should_rate_limit_file (lines 200-240) increments limit->distinct_file_count on every call (line 233) and returns true when the counter exceeds 30 (lines 236-238), setting should_warn_next. get_file_open_count returns 0 on that path (lines 273-275), and handle_event's FILE_OPERATION branch breaks on count == 0 without printing or incrementing anything (lines 735-739). The limiter runs at line 273, before hash dedup at line 282 and the duplicate-collapse path at lines 325-332, so repeated opens of the same path do consume the 30-event budget and the aggregation count itself is capped, biasing counts. No userspace counter exists for these drops: the only dropped accounting is the BPF-side dropped_events map incremented solely by inc_dropped() on ringbuf reserve failure (process.bpf.c lines 32-39, 113-114), printed only by print_dropped_events (lines 530-544), and nothing anywhere in the repo records rate-limited drops (grep for should_rate_limit_file/MAX_DISTINCT_FILES finds only process.c). Downstream code (compare/scripts/build/build_backend_capture_health.py lines 183-184) treats process_drop_count from PROCESS_RINGBUF_STATS as the capture-loss signal, so a zero value misrepresents completeness. The claim's one overstatement is "usually never emitted": the flag is also consumed on a later second's first open (lines 224-231) and on EXIT (lines 632-639), so a sustained high-rate workload does get a warning — though the warning is delayed, is a single boolean rather than a count, and is silently lost if the first post-second event is itself deduped and returns 0 at line 332 before the caller prints warning_msg. These nuances do not change the core defect: >30 opens/sec/pid are discarded with no event, no dropped-event accounting, and no per-drop record. Severity high is justified because the repo explicitly uses dropped_events as the honest-capture contract and this path defeats it for file-access evidence.

confirmed.title: A run with zero attached SSL probes exits 0 and looks like a successful empty capture
confirmed.evidence: attach_openssl counts attach_failures but always returns 0 (lines 408-435). The BoringSSL fallback only warns on failure (lines 700-708) and ignores the return value of attach_openssl_by_offset (line 704; that function returns -errno through __CHECK_PROGRAM). main then enters the poll loop and returns err != 0 with err == 0 (lines 724-745, 758-773). The FAIL macro was explicitly added to avoid 'clean exit with zero events' for load errors, but attach errors bypass it.
confirmed.impact: If the library is not found, the target binary is stripped and pattern detection fails, or every symbol attach fails, tls_capture keeps running with zero links and exits successfully. The collector sees a clean exit and an empty SSL stream, indistinguishable from 'the agent made no TLS calls' — a silent hole in the primary LLM-traffic evidence source.
confirmed.fix: After all attach attempts require at least one live link; if none, set err = -ENODEV and exit nonzero (or emit an explicit zero-probe control event). Propagate attach_openssl_by_offset's error instead of ignoring it.

verification.reason: The code says exactly what the claim states. In /tmp/mtal-audit/bpftools/tls_capture/tls_capture.c, attach_openssl (408-435) uses the SOFT macros, which only increment attach_failures (86-93), and then unconditionally `return 0;` at line 434; callers discard that value at lines 653 and 696. The BoringSSL fallback calls attach_openssl_by_offset at line 704 and ignores its result; although the OFFSET_CHECKED macros propagate -errno through __CHECK_PROGRAM (55-61, 107-117), that error is dropped, and the only failure path is the warn at 706-707 (verbose-only prints at 699-700). Missing libraries only warn (655, 666, 677), and the gnutls/nss attach return values are likewise discarded (664, 675). main never inspects attach_failures or any links pointer after the attach block; err remains 0 from the successful load at 634, attach calls never assign err, and the loop resets err = 0 at line 744 before `return err != 0;` at 773, so a zero-link run interrupted by SIGINT exits 0. The FAIL macro (35-40) only covers load/ringbuf/signal/poll failures (628, 636, 715, 727). Downstream does not compensate: collector/src/framework/runners/common.rs merely logs the child's termination status at debug level (~318-320) and ssl.rs never checks it; the benchmark-side canary/health gating in env/src/mtagentlens_benchmark/engine/collector_manager.py is a separate launcher check and does not change the producer's misleading exit contract. The defect is reachable (libssl absent, all symbols absent, or BoringSSL offset attach failing) and matches the stated impact.

confirmed.title: Signal-terminated processes report exit_code 0, identical to a clean exit
confirmed.evidence: handle_exit computes e->exit_code = (BPF_CORE_READ(task, exit_code) >> 8) & 0xff. The kernel stores (status << 8) for normal exits but the bare signal number (< 256) for fatal-signal exits, so the shift turns SIGKILL/OOM/segfault exits into 0. The collector persists this value via signal_graph.observe_exit (collector/src/responsibility/signals/signal_graph.rs:295-301).
confirmed.impact: Killed agents and tools are recorded as having exited successfully. Any downstream interpretation of exit status (crash detection, blame/attribution, run validity) cannot distinguish a crash or OOM kill from a normal completion.
confirmed.fix: Branch on the raw value: if exit_code > 0xff emit status = exit_code >> 8; otherwise emit the signal number in a distinct field (e.g. signal) with an explicit signaled flag. Keep a normal-exit status field for compatibility.

verification.reason: The claim survives scrutiny. /tmp/mtal-audit/bpftools/process/process.bpf.c:265 is verbatim `e->exit_code = (BPF_CORE_READ(task, exit_code) >> 8) & 0xff;`, attached to `tp/sched/sched_process_exit` (SEC at line 217; the exit payload is filled at lines 255-266). The kernel stores the raw `task_struct.exit_code` in wait-status form: normal exits are stored as `(status & 0xff) << 8` (so `>> 8 & 0xff` correctly recovers 0-255), while fatal-signal exits (`do_group_exit(signr)` from the signal path) store the bare signal number in the low 8 bits, so SIGKILL(9)/SIGSEGV(11)/OOM-kill all shift to 0 and become indistinguishable from a clean `exit(0)`. I found no compensating handling anywhere: `bpftools/process/process.h:69` declares only a single `unsigned exit_code` field (no signal/term_sig field), `process.c:623` emits it as `%u` straight into JSON, `collector/src/responsibility/runtime/routing.rs:609-613` parses it unmodified (`exit_code` → i32), and `routing.rs:193-194` passes it directly to `signal_graph.observe_exit`, which at `collector/src/responsibility/signals/signal_graph.rs:295-300` persists it into `meta.exit_code` and nothing else. It is then surfaced via `signal_snapshot.rs:27` and rendered in `routing.rs:889-894` as `code={code}` in the timeline, so a killed agent is literally reported as `code=0`.
